patterns.re: Replica \d+ panicked .* tearing down ICI communicators
patterns.summary: A worker crashed, causing the network communicators to be destroyed.
patterns.action: Look for OOM or NaN errors in the crashed replica's log.

patterns.re: Framework OOM when allocating buffer for incoming ICI message of size \d+
patterns.summary: Receiver ran out of memory before accepting the network payload.
patterns.action: Reduce activation sizes or enable memory efficient collective algorithms.

patterns.re: TMA box dimensions exceed tensor global dimensions
patterns.summary: TMA fetch box is larger than global tensor.
patterns.action: Reduce TMA block dimensions to fit tensor.

patterns.re: TMA fetch global address out of bounds
patterns.summary: TMA fetch tried to access invalid global memory.
patterns.action: Check tensor bounds and base pointers.

patterns.re: Inner dimension of TMA must be contiguous
patterns.summary: Innermost tensor dimension is not contiguous.
patterns.action: Make the innermost dimension contiguous in memory.

patterns.re: Mcast target SM exceeds cluster size
patterns.summary: Target SM for multicast is outside the cluster.
patterns.action: Constrain mcast target to current cluster size.

patterns.re: Mbarrier not initialized for mcast operation
patterns.summary: Mbarrier was used before initialization.
patterns.action: Initialize mbarrier before issuing mcast TMA.

patterns.re: cp.async.bulk source address out of bounds
patterns.summary: Bulk copy accessed out-of-bounds global memory.
patterns.action: Verify source address and bulk size.

patterns.re: Cutlass Sm90 prologue TMA load out of bounds
patterns.summary: Sm90 prologue TMA fetch is out of bounds.
patterns.action: Check prologue tile shape and tensor boundaries.

patterns.re: Cutlass TMA K dimension must be contiguous
patterns.summary: K dimension is not contiguous in Cutlass TMA.
patterns.action: Transpose or pack K dimension to be contiguous.

patterns.summary: make_tensor_ptr requested out of bounds memory.
patterns.action: Clamp tensor pointer dimensions to device limits.

patterns.re: TMA buffers exceed max shared memory per block
patterns.summary: TMA buffers exceed SMEM capacity per block.
patterns.action: Reduce block size or num_stages in Inductor.

patterns.re: Symmetric heap not aligned for TMA access
patterns.summary: Symmetric heap lacks alignment for TMA.
patterns.action: Ensure symmetric heap is 16-byte aligned.

patterns.summary: TMA operation caused context switch timeout.
patterns.action: Reduce TMA transaction size or check for deadlocks.

patterns.summary: Graphics engine exception caused by malformed TMA.
patterns.action: Validate TMA descriptor configurations.

patterns.re: Failed to allocate SHARP tree.*resource limit
patterns.summary: Switch hardware ran out of SHARP tree resources.
patterns.action: Increase SHARP quotas or reduce the number of concurrent jobs.

patterns.summary: Job attempted a reduction op not supported by SHARP ASIC.
patterns.action: Fallback to NCCL ring/tree algorithms instead of SHARP.

patterns.summary: Internal switch SHARP table corruption detected.
patterns.action: Rebuild SHARP trees via UFM or restart SM.

patterns.summary: HCA firmware hit an assertion on a SHARP Queue Pair.
patterns.action: Collect fwtrace and report to NVIDIA support.

patterns.re: NCCL WARN SHARP plugin not found
patterns.summary: The nccl-rdma-sharp-plugins library is missing.
patterns.action: Install HPC-X or nvidia-peer-memory plugins.

patterns.summary: nvidia-peermem driver missing, disabling GPUDirect SHARP.
patterns.action: Run modprobe nvidia-peermem on all hosts.

patterns.summary: NVSwitch failure trapped SHARP collective in-flight.
patterns.action: Reset the baseboard and check NVSwitch dmesg logs.

patterns.summary: A SHARP-related environment variable has invalid syntax.
patterns.action: Fix typo in NCCL_SHARP environment variables.

patterns.summary: Libfabric SHARP provider is not installed or enabled.
patterns.action: Recompile libfabric with SHARP support.

patterns.re: Non-contiguous tensor stride unsupported by SHARP
patterns.summary: Passed non-contiguous PyTorch tensor directly to SHARP.
patterns.action: Call tensor.contiguous() before distributed collective.

patterns.summary: Ranks submitted different dtypes to a SHARP collective.
patterns.action: Ensure all PyTorch ranks use identical tensor dtypes.

patterns.re: Target LID not in SHARP tree
patterns.summary: Attempted to use SHARP with an unjoined node.
patterns.action: Ensure all job ranks successfully join the SHARP group.

patterns.summary: Subnet manager accidentally reused an active SHARP Tree ID.
patterns.action: Restart UFM/OpenSM to clear ID registry.

patterns.summary: Node used wrong Partition Key for SHARP communication.
patterns.action: Fix tenant P_Key configuration in UFM/OpenSM.

patterns.summary: Linux OOM killer terminated the SHARP daemon.
patterns.action: Add swap, increase node RAM, or OOM-protect sharpd.

patterns.re: SELinux is preventing sharpd from using Unix domain socket
patterns.summary: SELinux blocked SHARP daemon IPC.
patterns.action: Set SELinux context for sharpd or disable SELinux.

patterns.summary: OS receive buffer too small for SHARP daemon.
patterns.action: Increase sysctl net.core.rmem_max to 16777216.

patterns.re: Routing loop detected in SHARP topology
patterns.summary: Miswired switches created a loop in the SHARP tree.
patterns.action: Fix physical IB cabling to match tree topology.

patterns.action: Increase net.core.rmem_max to at least 2147483647.

patterns.action: Standardize MTU across all node pools using daemonsets.

patterns.summary: DDP timeout reached during slow TCP fallback initialization.

patterns.action: Increase the router Z-loss coefficient to regularize logit magnitudes.

patterns.action: Increase aux_loss balancing weight to force even routing.

patterns.summary: Dropless MoE in MegaBlocks allocated memory for all imbalances.

patterns.summary: HuggingFace Mixtral naive MoE implementation OOMed on large context.

patterns.summary: Fairseq NLLB MoE encountered severe expert imbalance.
patterns.action: Increase balance_loss weight.

patterns.summary: Asymmetric NCCL AllToAll caused massive memory allocation on receiver.

patterns.summary: PyTorch caching allocator fragmentation during PP alternating forward/backward. (Stage/Variant 18)

patterns.summary: Interleaved 1F1B increases activation memory footprint. (Stage/Variant 58)

patterns.summary: Sequence Parallelism all-gather buffers fragmenting PP bubble. (Stage/Variant 98)

patterns.summary: Dynamic sequence lengths caused constant graph recompilations.

patterns.summary: Deadlock in ggml_cuda_op_rope during chunked prefill caused by multi-gpu tensor split stall.
patterns.action: Add explicit stream synchronization before ggml_cuda_op_rope yields to the thread pool.

patterns.re: ERROR: ggml_cuda_compute_forward.*ubatch size [0-9]+ exceeds max.*stalled at ncclAllReduce
patterns.summary: Deadlock in ggml_cuda_compute_forward during chunked prefill caused by ubatch size mismatch.
patterns.action: Add a pre-synchronization barrier before ncclAllReduce to prevent NCCL communicator deadlocks.

patterns.summary: Deadlock in ggml_cuda_op_mul_mat during chunked prefill caused by concurrent stream wait.
patterns.action: Add explicit stream synchronization before ggml_cuda_op_mul_mat yields to the thread pool.

patterns.summary: Deadlock in ggml_cuda_flash_attn_ext during chunked prefill caused by unrecorded event.
patterns.action: Add a pre-synchronization barrier before ncclAllReduce to prevent NCCL communicator deadlocks.

patterns.summary: Deadlock in llama_decode during chunked prefill caused by context shift overlap.
patterns.action: Drain the compute stream before initiating a KV cache context shift.

patterns.re: ggml_cuda_graph: dynamic shape changed during llama_kv_cache_update.*ncclAllReduce stall
patterns.summary: Deadlock in llama_kv_cache_update during chunked prefill caused by graph capture dynamic shape.
patterns.action: Add a pre-synchronization barrier before ncclAllReduce to prevent NCCL communicator deadlocks.

patterns.summary: Deadlock in ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async during chunked prefill caused by OOM stream desync.
patterns.action: Clear trailing CUDA events in the exception handler to prevent stream lockup on OOM.

patterns.re: urllib3\.exceptions\.ReadTimeoutError: HTTPSConnectionPool\(host='.*', port=443\): Read timed out\.

patterns.action: Tune urllib3 pool timeout or boto3 read_timeout.

patterns.summary: aiohttp payload error during S3 async upload.
patterns.action: Update aiohttp and check network MTU settings.

patterns.summary: Network timeout saving Lightning checkpoint via fsspec.
patterns.action: Check network connectivity and increase fsspec timeouts.

patterns.re: DeepSpeedEngine: Failed to save zero checkpoint to s3:\/\/.*
patterns.summary: DeepSpeed ZeRO checkpoint failed to upload to S3.
patterns.action: Adjust DeepSpeed checkpoint async_io timeouts.

patterns.re: google\.api_core\.exceptions\.RetryError: Deadline of .*s exceeded while calling target function
patterns.summary: GCS upload retries exhausted before completion.
patterns.action: Increase the total deadline for GCS retry policy.

patterns.summary: S3 connection timeout during multi-part upload.
patterns.action: Increase boto3 config connect_timeout setting.

patterns.re: socket\.timeout: The read operation timed out
patterns.summary: Socket timeout, possibly due to Kubernetes NAT drop.
patterns.action: Enable TCP keep-alive on the container network.

patterns.summary: GCS upload deadline exceeded.
patterns.action: Increase timeout in GCS client configuration.

patterns.summary: Lustre client evicted due to unresponsiveness to LDLM.
patterns.action: Check client health and network stability.

patterns.summary: Lustre OST lock cancellation storm detected.
patterns.action: Reduce lru_size or use O_DIRECT.

patterns.summary: WekaFS fcntl read-to-write upgrade caused deadlock.
patterns.action: Acquire write locks directly if needed.

patterns.summary: Lustre MDT setattr lock storm.
patterns.action: Avoid frequent chmod/chown on shared directories.

patterns.summary: WekaFS lease revocation timed out.
patterns.action: Force unmount unresponsive clients.

patterns.summary: HDF5 parallel I/O lock contention via MPI-IO.
patterns.action: Use collective metadata operations in HDF5.

patterns.summary: Lustre intent lookup storm detected.
patterns.action: Cache lookups or split directories.

patterns.summary: Weka DLM evicted a node due to timeout.
patterns.action: Check client network and kernel logs.

patterns.summary: Weka DLM reached its memory limit.
patterns.action: Allocate more memory to Weka backend processes.

patterns.summary: Lustre lock inversion deadlock detected.
patterns.action: Report to Lustre upstream; apply kernel patch.

patterns.summary: Worker process deadlocked or took too long. (Case 13)

patterns.summary: An NCCL correctness check returned a non-zero mismatch count. This is data corruption on the fabric, not a performance result. Every number in the same run is meaningless, and any training job that ran across this fabric may have silently corrupted gradients without raising anything.
patterns.action: Stop scheduling work on this fabric now, before tuning anything. A non-zero mismatch count is never a reason to adjust a buffer size or an algorithm. Bisect it: run the same test pairwise across node groups and compare, because an outlier pair isolates one bad node while a uniformly bad result points at a systemic fabric or switch problem. Check cable seating, port error counters and switch firmware on whatever the bisection names, then re-run the correctness check and require exactly zero before returning the nodes to the pool.
patterns.resumeFrom: not applicable, and treat checkpoints written while this fabric was in use as suspect until a correctness run passes

patterns.summary: DeepSpeed ZeRO-Offload filled the NVMe filesystem used for optimizer or parameter swap. The failed aio_write means the offload state is incomplete, even if the training process reports a later optimizer error.
patterns.action:
NOW: stop the run, inspect free bytes and inodes on the configured nvme_path, and remove only stale offload data from jobs that are no longer active.
INVESTIGATE: calculate the expected parameter and optimizer offload footprint for every local rank, then compare it with filesystem capacity and quota. Confirm ranks are not writing duplicate state into an unintended shared path.
PREVENT: reserve offload capacity per job, isolate job directories, alert before the filesystem reaches its safety margin, and clean directories through scheduler lifecycle hooks.
ESCALATE: if aio_write fails with available capacity, collect mount options, quota, kernel I/O errors, and an fio control from the same path.
patterns.resumeFrom: last complete checkpoint after the NVMe offload path is healthy

patterns.re: Node state DRAIN[^\n]{0,100}NVML health check timed out[^\n]{0,80}uncorrectable ECC
patterns.summary: Slurm drained the node because its NVML health check timed out while the GPU also reported uncorrectable ECC evidence. The timeout is a node-health failure, not a reason to return the GPU to service after a simple job retry.
patterns.action:
NOW: keep the node drained, preserve the health-check output and kernel log, and identify the GPU UUID with uncorrectable ECC activity.
INVESTIGATE: run nvidia-smi -q and DCGM diagnostics out of band. Determine whether NVML is blocked by a wedged driver, GPU reset, or a device that no longer responds.
PREVENT: time-bound health checks while retaining their output, alert on ECC growth before scheduler admission fails, and require a passing post-remediation diagnostic before RESUME.
ESCALATE: repeated uncorrectable ECC or an unresponsive GPU requires hardware service with the GPU UUID, Xid log, row-remap state, and diagnostic bundle.
patterns.resumeFrom: latest checkpoint on a healthy node

patterns.summary: A vLLM paged-attention kernel accessed an invalid GPU address. The immediate owner can be corrupted block-table metadata, an unsupported shape or dtype, or a binary compatibility defect in the selected attention backend.
patterns.action:
NOW: restart the worker to clear the invalid CUDA context and reproduce one request with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1. Preserve the first failing request shape and block-table state.
INVESTIGATE: test the same model and request with the fallback attention backend, then verify vLLM, PyTorch, CUDA, and kernel binary compatibility for the GPU architecture.
PREVENT: pin the serving stack, canary the longest supported context and concurrency, and validate block-table bounds before kernel launch.
ESCALATE: if the failure is backend-specific, collect a minimal request, model configuration, device capability, versions, and compute-sanitizer output for vLLM.
patterns.resumeFrom: request retry in a fresh worker after the attention control passes

patterns.summary: A native custom CUDA extension crashed the process during backward execution. The fault is inside the extension or its ABI boundary, not an NCCL collective simply because distributed ranks exit afterward.
patterns.action:
NOW: reproduce on one GPU with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and enable Python faulthandler so the last extension call is preserved.
INVESTIGATE: rebuild the extension against the active PyTorch and CUDA ABI, validate tensor device, dtype, contiguity, shape, and lifetime, then run compute-sanitizer on the smallest failing case.
PREVENT: pin compiler and framework versions, validate extension inputs at the boundary, and run forward plus backward sanitizer tests in release CI.
ESCALATE: preserve the native backtrace, build flags, minimal tensors, and sanitizer report for the extension owner.
patterns.resumeFrom: last checkpoint before the failed backward step

patterns.re: NCCL ring buffer allocation failed[^\n]{0,100}NCCL_BUFFSIZE[^\n]{0,120}contiguous pinned host memory
patterns.summary: NCCL could not allocate the contiguous pinned host buffer requested by NCCL_BUFFSIZE. The configured buffer and communicator count exceeded available lockable memory or the process memlock limit.
patterns.action:
NOW: restore NCCL_BUFFSIZE to its default or a measured smaller value and inspect ulimit -l plus current pinned-memory usage on every rank.
INVESTIGATE: calculate buffer demand across channels and communicators, compare it with the cgroup and memlock limits, and identify stale processes retaining registrations.
PREVENT: change NCCL_BUFFSIZE only from benchmark evidence, set and verify memlock consistently across nodes, and include communicator initialization in preflight.
ESCALATE: if the default buffer fails with adequate limits on a clean node, preserve NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, topology, limits, and registration errors for NVIDIA.
patterns.resumeFrom: job start after every rank can initialize the ring buffers

patterns.summary: PyTorch multiprocessing could not map another shared-memory region because /dev/shm is full or capped too low. This consumes shared memory, not filesystem disk and not GPU VRAM.
patterns.action:
NOW: inspect df -h /dev/shm and the container shared-memory limit, then stop stale worker processes that retain mappings.
INVESTIGATE: compare worker count, prefetch factor, batch tensor size, and sharing strategy with the configured /dev/shm capacity.
PREVENT: size /dev/shm explicitly for containerized jobs, bound worker prefetch, and monitor shared-memory usage as a separate resource.
ESCALATE: if mappings leak after workers exit, capture open shared-memory files and a minimal multiprocessing reproducer for PyTorch.
patterns.resumeFrom: job start after shared-memory capacity and worker bounds are corrected

patterns.re: could not select device driver with capabilities[^\n]{0,80}gpu[^\n]{0,100}nvidia-container-cli initialization error
patterns.summary: The container runtime could not select or initialize the NVIDIA GPU runtime. The host toolkit, runtime configuration, driver visibility, or requested GPU capability is missing before the application starts.
patterns.action:
NOW: verify nvidia-smi works on the host, then run the NVIDIA Container Toolkit sample command through the same runtime used by the workload.
INVESTIGATE: inspect Docker or containerd runtime configuration and nvidia-container-cli -k -d /dev/tty info output. Confirm the toolkit and host driver are compatible.
PREVENT: configure the runtime through nvidia-ctk, restart the runtime after changes, and gate GPU nodes on a containerized nvidia-smi check.
ESCALATE: if host access works but the toolkit sample fails, collect runtime logs, toolkit versions, driver version, and OCI hook configuration.
patterns.resumeFrom: container start after the NVIDIA runtime control succeeds

patterns.re: cuDNN version .* unsupported by this FlashAttention build

patterns.action: Update cuDNN or reinstall FlashAttention.

patterns.summary: Negative scale factor passed to attention backward.
patterns.action: Ensure scale is properly computed as a positive float.

patterns.summary: Gathering optimizer state dictionary exceeded GPU memory on rank 0.
patterns.action: Use sharded_optim_state_dict context manager to save optimizer states locally.

patterns.summary: Attempted to access un-wrapped attributes directly on the FSDP object.
patterns.action: Access original module attributes via fsdp_module._fsdp_wrapped_module.

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Expected to have finished reduction.*GemmaDecoderLayer
patterns.summary: Gradient synchronization occurred prematurely during accumulation.
patterns.action: Wrap the forward and backward passes with fsdp_module.no_sync() during accumulation steps.

patterns.re: NotImplementedError: Cannot copy out of meta tensor.*CLIPEncoderLayer
patterns.summary: FSDP failed to materialize meta-device parameters because sync_module_states=False.
patterns.action: Set sync_module_states=True when initializing FSDP with meta device parameters.

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Expected to have finished reduction.*T5Block
patterns.summary: Gradient synchronization occurred prematurely during accumulation.
patterns.action: Wrap the forward and backward passes with fsdp_module.no_sync() during accumulation steps.

patterns.summary: Type mismatch between FSDP mixed precision output and non-wrapped module expectation.
patterns.action: Cast inputs explicitly or adjust the MixedPrecision policy configuration.

patterns.summary: Gradient norm calculation yielded NaN across partitions. Occurred specifically in LayerNorm module during forward.
patterns.action: Check LayerNorm implementation and check for loss explosion or lower learning rate.

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Expected param to be synced but found partitioned
patterns.summary: Accessed a ZeRO-3 partitioned parameter before fetching. Occurred specifically in CrossAttention module during backward.
patterns.action: Check CrossAttention implementation and wrap parameter access in gatheredparameters.

patterns.summary: CPUAdam called with GPU parameters. Occurred specifically in MoE_Gate module during step.
patterns.action: Check MoE_Gate implementation and ensure offload_optimizer config is correctly applied.

patterns.re: Trying to backward through the graph a second time
patterns.summary: Computation graph retained across steps. Occurred specifically in Attention module during clip_grad_norm.
patterns.action: Check Attention implementation and ensure loss.backward() is called only once per step.

patterns.summary: Gradients lost contiguous memory layout. Occurred specifically in LayerNorm module during gather.
patterns.action: Check LayerNorm implementation and call .contiguous() on custom loss gradients.

patterns.re: AssertionError: deepspeed.zero.Init() context must be used
patterns.summary: Model initialized outside ZeRO-3 context. Occurred specifically in CrossAttention module during scatter.
patterns.action: Check CrossAttention implementation and wrap model instantiation inside zero.init().

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Checkpoint rank .*MoE_Gate.*all_gather.* missing partitioned state
patterns.summary: Restoring partitioned states on different GPU count. Occurred specifically in MoE_Gate module during all_gather.
patterns.action: Check MoE_Gate implementation and use deepspeed checkpoint conversion tool.

patterns.re: Bus error|No space left on device
patterns.summary: Distributed training frameworks like PyTorch use /dev/shm for inter-process communication (IPC). In containerized environments, the default size is too small (e.g., 64MB), causing workers to crash with a 'Bus error' when IPC memory is exhausted.
patterns.action: Increase the shared memory size by passing `--shm-size=2gb` (or higher) to Docker, or configuring an emptyDir volume with `medium: Memory` for `/dev/shm` in KubeRay.

requiredEvidence.re: Error occurs when PyTorch DDP initializes or uses shared memory for IPC
Docker or KubeRay pod lacks explicit shm-size config

patterns.summary: The decoupled checkpoint process can wait forever because its event wait has no bounded deadline or worker-health failure path.
patterns.action: Add a bounded event deadline plus child-process health checks, terminate/retry a dead writer, and verify one successful commit and one injected-writer-failure both reach terminal states.

patterns.summary: Inductor cat lowering mishandles an empty 1-D operand when normalizing an out-of-range negative dimension.
patterns.action: Normalize/validate the cat dimension before compilation or use the patched Inductor lowering; keep eager execution as containment and compare eager/compiled output for the minimized operands.
patterns.resumeFrom: the failed step after the corrected cat lowering passes eager parity

patterns.summary: Inductor TMA combo-kernel code generation emits a reference to a missing generated name.
patterns.action: Disable TMA for containment or use the patched Inductor build, then compile the minimized kernel and compare its output with eager execution before restoring TMA.
patterns.resumeFrom: job start after the generated TMA kernel passes the minimized control

patterns.re: variable modified by inplace operation|inplace operation
patterns.summary: The compiled backward path observes an unexpected in-place version change while the same graph succeeds eagerly.
patterns.action: Keep this graph eager for containment, minimize the mutation/version-counter path, and test the patched compiler build; require eager and compiled gradients to agree before re-enabling compilation.
patterns.resumeFrom: the failed step after compiled gradients match eager gradients

patterns.re: SwitchRouter: Router probabilities sum to NaN at 90
patterns.summary: FP16 overflow in router logits during softmax computation.
patterns.action: Cast router logits to FP32 before applying softmax.

patterns.summary: Capacity factor was set too strict, dropping all tokens and causing empty batch NaNs.
patterns.action: Increase expert capacity factor or implement a fallback expert for dropped tokens.

patterns.summary: Expert entropy loss logged log(0) probabilities, resulting in NaN gradients.
patterns.action: Clamp routing probabilities to [1e-6, 1.0] before computing entropy.

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Expected tensor for argument #1 'input' to have the same dtype as tensor.*gate
patterns.summary: VMoE router logits blew up due to unscaled dot-product attention in the gate.
patterns.action: Initialize gating network weights with smaller variance (e.g., 0.001).

patterns.summary: Disabled token dropping caused unbounded memory growth on popular experts.

patterns.summary: Megatron grouped GEMM allocated max buffer sizes leading to OOM.

patterns.summary: MoE memory variance caused KV cache block allocation to OOM.

patterns.summary: Tutel dynamic capacity allowed unbounded tensor growth.

patterns.summary: MegaBlocks router collapsed to single expert causing sparse OOM.
patterns.action: Increase load balancing loss.

patterns.summary: Long inference generation with MoE routed to same experts.
patterns.action: Use repetition penalty.

patterns.summary: Incorrect 2D DeviceMesh configuration caused OOM.
patterns.action: Align EP and FSDP mesh dimensions.

patterns.summary: Continuous batching expanded batch size exactly when routing was imbalanced.
patterns.action: Set a strict token-level limit in inference engine.

patterns.summary: Megatron-LM p2p_communication buffers fragmentation. (Stage/Variant 17)

patterns.summary: Interleaved 1F1B increases activation memory footprint. (Stage/Variant 37)
patterns.action: Decrease virtual pipeline parallel size. Applied at step 37.

patterns.summary: 1F1B forward pass activation fragmentation. (Stage/Variant 57)
patterns.action: Reduce microbatch size. Applied at step 57.

patterns.summary: Sequence Parallelism all-gather buffers fragmenting PP bubble. (Stage/Variant 77)
patterns.action: Reduce sequence length or increase tensor parallel size. Applied at step 77.

patterns.summary: Last PP stage OOM during pipeline flush gradient accumulation. (Stage/Variant 97)

patterns.summary: P2P receive buffer was provided as an unaligned tensor slice.

patterns.summary: FSDP flattening process generated a parameter buffer with an unaligned byte offset.
patterns.action: Ensure FSDP parameter sizes are padded to alignment boundaries.

patterns.summary: Vocabulary parallel embedding gradients were sliced at an unaligned vocabulary index.
patterns.action: Pad the vocabulary size to a multiple of the tensor parallel degree.

patterns.summary: P2P direct memory copy failed due to an unaligned destination or source pointer.
patterns.action: Ensure both source and destination buffers are allocated with cudaMalloc.

patterns.summary: NCCL P2P setup failed because the imported IPC memory handle was misaligned.
patterns.action: Ensure the memory handle exported from the peer is explicitly aligned.

patterns.summary: Asynchronous peer memcpy source pointer is unaligned.
patterns.action: Ensure the source pointer is properly aligned via cudaMalloc.

patterns.summary: Asynchronous peer memcpy destination pointer is unaligned.
patterns.action: Ensure the destination pointer is properly aligned via cudaMalloc.

patterns.summary: nv_peer_mem module rejected an unaligned virtual address mapping for GPUDirect RDMA.
patterns.action: Ensure the GPU memory pointer is aligned to a 64KB boundary for GPUDirect.

patterns.summary: GDRCopy map operation failed due to an unaligned GPU memory mapping.
patterns.action: Allocate GPU memory with cudaMalloc instead of slicing existing buffers for GDRCopy.

patterns.summary: GPUDirect Storage issued an O_DIRECT read into an unaligned GPU memory address.
patterns.action: Align the GPU memory address to the filesystem logical block size.

patterns.summary: cuFileWrite from GPUDirect Storage failed due to an unaligned GPU source buffer.
patterns.action: Allocate the source buffer via cudaMalloc instead of using a tensor view.

patterns.summary: XLA custom call to NCCL provided an unaligned device pointer.
patterns.action: Verify custom op definitions ensure tensor contiguous alignment.

patterns.summary: Megatron-LM Tensor Parallelism produced an unaligned linear layer gradient.
patterns.action: Ensure hidden sizes are divisible by the tensor parallel degree.

patterns.summary: FlashAttention output buffer in sequence parallel mode was misaligned.
patterns.action: Allocate a contiguous output buffer and copy FlashAttention results into it.

patterns.re: NodeManager failed to write object to disk.*ENOSPC.*

patterns.summary: NCCL reports that a communication ring within the TP group was broken, indicating a node crash or hardware bus error during the step.
patterns.action: Inspect the logs of all nodes to identify the specific GPU or host that crashed, and replace the failing hardware node.

patterns.summary: Failed to initialize the NCCL communicator for the TP group. Often due to mismatched rank counts or binding conflicts.
patterns.action: Verify that your MPI or PyTorch Elastic launch configuration matches the expected TP * PP * DP grid layout exactly.

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Shape mismatch during PP recv: expected.*but received.*
patterns.summary: Send/recv tensor shape mismatch between adjacent pipeline stages. Typically caused by mismatched sequence length configurations or padding.
patterns.action: Check the sequence length padding, and verify that the micro-batch size and sequence length are uniform across all stages.

patterns.re: IndexError: virtual stage index.*out of range.*interleaved pipeline.*
patterns.summary: Index out of range in interleaved pipeline schedule. Caused by invalid layer division or incorrect virtual stage mapping.
patterns.action: Adjust the layer distribution array and ensure the total layers are evenly divisible by (pipeline_model_parallel_size * virtual_pipeline_model_paralle

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Mismatched hidden state dimensions at the TP\/PP interface.*
patterns.summary: Mismatched hidden state dimensions at the TP/PP interface. Output dimension of the preceding stage does not match input of the following stage.
patterns.action: Verify model dimension arguments (--hidden-size, --num-attention-heads) are identical across all running model ranks.

patterns.re: NCCL WARN.*QP state transitions to ERR.*
patterns.summary: InfiniBand Queue Pair transitioned to error state.
patterns.action: Check dmesg for hardware faults on the NIC.

patterns.summary: NVSwitch hardware fatal error detected.
patterns.action: Run DCGM diagnostics and replace faulty baseboard.

patterns.summary: PCIe Advanced Error Reporting fatal event.
patterns.action: Update motherboard BIOS or replace riser cable.

patterns.summary: Network partition split the SP process group.
patterns.action: Fix datacenter network routing issue.

patterns.summary: GPU OOM during NCCL buffer allocation.
patterns.action: Reduce sequence length or microbatch size.

patterns.summary: Pinned memory (mlock) limit exceeded.
patterns.action: Set ulimit -l unlimited.

patterns.summary: NCCL unique ID broadcast failure during SP init.
patterns.action: Check rendezvous backend (etcd or tcp) connectivity.

patterns.summary: Duplicate rank initialization in SP group.
patterns.action: Check SLURM or TorchRun script for overlapping rank IDs.

patterns.summary: NCCL init timeout during SP bootstrap.
patterns.action: Check network connectivity to rendezvous store.

patterns.summary: The host nouveau module is loaded and blocks the GPU Operator from installing or loading the proprietary NVIDIA driver.
patterns.action: Cordon the node. Blacklist nouveau in the host boot configuration, rebuild initramfs, reboot during an approved maintenance window, then verify lsmod and the driver daemonset before uncordoning.
patterns.resumeFrom: not applicable, repair the node before rescheduling workloads

patterns.summary: DCGM observed an increase in NVLink CRC flit errors and marked the link degraded. A rising counter indicates signal or link integrity trouble, not a collective software timeout.
patterns.action:
NOW: identify the GPU and link ID, stop placing new multi-GPU work across that path, and record the counter before any reset.
INVESTIGATE: compare counters on both endpoints, inspect link state and recovery events, and run a topology-aware DCGM or NVLink bandwidth control.
PREVENT: baseline per-link counters after provisioning and alert on deltas rather than lifetime totals. Recheck after firmware, chassis, or physical service.
ESCALATE: if errors continue under a controlled link test, drain the node and provide endpoint IDs, counter deltas, firmware, and health logs to the hardware vendor.
patterns.resumeFrom: latest checkpoint on a topology that excludes the degraded link

patterns.summary: TorchDynamo captured the graph, but TorchInductor failed while lowering an operation to generated code. The useful cause is the nested LoweringException and its target operator, not the outer BackendCompilerFailed wrapper.
patterns.action:
NOW: retain the full nested exception and use the PyTorch compiler repro tooling to reduce the failing graph. Run the same function eagerly as the control.
INVESTIGATE: identify the lowering target and compare tensor shapes, strides, dtypes, and device with the operator contract. Check the active PyTorch and Triton version pairing.
PREVENT: compile representative dynamic shapes in CI, retain compiler repro artifacts, and pin the PyTorch and Triton stack used in production.
ESCALATE: if supported inputs fail on a current tested stack, submit the minified graph, nested traceback, environment report, and generated code to PyTorch.
patterns.resumeFrom: job start after the graph compiles or the region is excluded

patterns.summary: CUDA could not export an interprocess memory handle for the allocation. Device memory pressure, an ineligible allocation, or exhausted IPC and driver bookkeeping can cause this before the receiving process maps anything.
patterns.action:
NOW: stop stale producer and consumer processes, record free GPU memory, and retry the smallest supported device allocation in a fresh pair of processes.
INVESTIGATE: confirm the pointer is a CUDA device allocation eligible for legacy IPC, both processes use the same physical GPU identity, and container PID and IPC namespaces permit the exchange.
PREVENT: bound exported allocation lifetime, close imported handles deterministically, and include a two-process IPC canary in the runtime image test.
ESCALATE: if a small eligible allocation fails in clean processes, collect driver, CUDA, MIG, container, and minimal reproducer details for NVIDIA.
patterns.resumeFrom: job start after the CUDA IPC control succeeds

patterns.summary: Sentence Transformers exceeded VRAM during encoding because the token count, batch size, output handling, and other GPU residents exceeded the model memory budget. Sequence length can dominate even when the document count looks small.
patterns.action:
NOW: reduce encode batch size and cap or bucket sequence length, then repeat the same documents with no unrelated GPU process resident.
INVESTIGATE: log token lengths and peak allocated memory per batch. Find whether one outlier document or cumulative retention of output tensors drives the peak.
PREVENT: batch by token count, enforce a maximum input length, move completed embeddings to CPU promptly, and load-test the p99 document length.
ESCALATE: if memory grows across identical batches, capture a PyTorch allocation snapshot and a minimal encode loop for Sentence Transformers.
patterns.resumeFrom: the first uncommitted embedding batch after memory bounds are corrected

patterns.re: die-to-die thermal delta[^\n]{0,100}(primary die|secondary die)[^\n]{0,100}emergency throttle
patterns.summary: A Blackwell B200 module detected an unsafe temperature difference between its two dies and entered emergency throttling. The delta points to uneven cooling or contact, not ordinary workload-wide thermal saturation.
patterns.action:
NOW: drain the GPU and preserve per-die temperature, clock, power, and cooling telemetry before changing load or power state.
INVESTIGATE: compare both die sensors under idle and a controlled load, then inspect cold-plate contact, coolant flow, and module seating through the approved service path.
PREVENT: monitor per-die delta in addition to absolute temperature and qualify cooling uniformity after module or cold-plate service.
ESCALATE: a persistent delta on a correctly cooled module requires platform service with module identity, firmware, telemetry, and facility cooling data.
patterns.resumeFrom: latest checkpoint on a thermally healthy GPU

patterns.re: CUDA out of memory[^\n]{0,100}Inductor CUDA graph[^\n]{0,100}(private memory pool fragmentation|allocator)
patterns.summary: TorchInductor exhausted a private CUDA Graph memory pool even though total free memory may appear sufficient. Captured graphs retain stable addresses, so inactive blocks in the private pool cannot always satisfy a differently shaped allocation.
patterns.action:
NOW: reproduce with CUDA Graphs disabled for the compiled region. If the same batch succeeds, reduce shape variation or recapture scope instead of only lowering batch size.
INVESTIGATE: record reserved, allocated, and inactive split bytes at failure. Check whether new input shapes cause additional graph captures and private pools.
PREVENT: bucket dynamic shapes, warm the bounded shape set, and monitor reserved-to-allocated growth during a production-shaped soak.
ESCALATE: if one fixed shape fragments a fresh process, preserve the minimal compiled graph and allocator snapshot for PyTorch.
patterns.resumeFrom: job start after graph capture and shape policy are corrected

patterns.summary: A FlashInfer paged-prefill kernel accessed an invalid GPU address. Common owners are malformed page metadata, a shape or dtype unsupported by the selected kernel, or a binary built for an incompatible CUDA stack.
patterns.action:
NOW: restart the process to clear the poisoned CUDA context, then reproduce one request with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and the smallest failing page table.
INVESTIGATE: validate page indices, sequence lengths, dtype, head dimensions, and FlashInfer/PyTorch/CUDA compatibility. Run the same input with the fallback attention backend.
PREVENT: validate page metadata before launch, pin tested binary versions, and keep a small prefill kernel canary in release tests.
ESCALATE: if valid metadata fails only in FlashInfer, preserve the input shapes, device capability, versions, and compute-sanitizer result for maintainers.
patterns.resumeFrom: request retry in a fresh process after the kernel control passes

patterns.summary: AutoencoderKL ran out of VRAM while decoding tiled latent intermediates. Tiling reduces the peak for the main VAE operation, but overlap buffers, output assembly, dtype, and concurrent model residency still consume memory.
patterns.action:
NOW: decode one image at a time, keep the VAE in a reduced precision supported by the model, and remove unrelated GPU residents before retrying.
INVESTIGATE: measure allocated and reserved memory before each tile and during output assembly. Confirm the tile and overlap settings actually reduce the failing intermediate.
PREVENT: load-test the largest image dimensions, bound concurrent decodes, and select tile parameters from measured peak VRAM rather than defaults.
ESCALATE: if a minimal single-tile decode grows memory across repetitions, capture an allocation snapshot for Diffusers or PyTorch.
patterns.resumeFrom: image decode after the VAE memory budget is corrected

patterns.re: bitsandbytes[^\n]{0,80}matmul_4bit[^\n]{0,100}no kernel image is available for execution on the device
patterns.summary: The installed bitsandbytes CUDA binary does not contain a 4-bit kernel for the GPU compute capability in use. This is an architecture or binary compatibility failure, not a model-memory shortage.
patterns.action:
NOW: record the GPU compute capability, bitsandbytes version, PyTorch CUDA version, and loaded library path. Install a build that explicitly supports that architecture.
INVESTIGATE: run the bitsandbytes diagnostic and confirm the process is not loading an older libbitsandbytes CUDA library from another environment.
PREVENT: build or select wheels against every deployed GPU architecture and test matmul_4bit in the image admission suite.
ESCALATE: if the architecture is documented as supported, provide the loader output and minimal matmul to bitsandbytes maintainers.
patterns.resumeFrom: job start with a compatible bitsandbytes binary

patterns.re: PPOTrainer[^\n]{0,100}CUDA out of memory[^\n]{0,120}(reference model|policy model|value head)
patterns.summary: TRL PPO could not keep the policy, reference model, value head, activations, and optimizer state within the available VRAM. The simultaneous model residency makes this different from a single-model batch OOM.
patterns.action:
NOW: reduce per-device rollout and mini-batch sizes, then offload or shard the reference and value components before shrinking the policy context.
INVESTIGATE: measure memory after loading each model and after one rollout. Confirm duplicate reference or reward-model replicas are not placed on every actor unintentionally.
PREVENT: calculate the full actor-critic memory budget, assert placement before training, and run a one-update production-shaped memory test.
ESCALATE: if measured residency exceeds the configured placement plan, capture the TRL, Accelerate, or DeepSpeed resolved configuration and process map.
patterns.resumeFrom: last complete PPO checkpoint after the placement plan is corrected

patterns.summary: Enroot exhausted the user or filesystem quota while importing and extracting the SquashFS image. Free space elsewhere on the node does not help when the configured cache or data path has a separate quota.
patterns.action:
NOW: inspect quota and free inodes on the Enroot cache, data, and temporary paths, then remove only unreferenced cached images or select a path with sufficient quota.
INVESTIGATE: print ENROOT_CACHE_PATH, ENROOT_DATA_PATH, and ENROOT_TEMP_PATH in the Slurm job because login and compute nodes may resolve them differently.
PREVENT: size quotas for compressed image plus extracted root filesystem, clean caches by age and reference, and pre-stage common images.
ESCALATE: if usage is below quota, collect quota reports, inode counts, Enroot configuration, and the failing filesystem path for the cluster administrator.
patterns.resumeFrom: container import after quota and cache paths are corrected

patterns.re: Megatron[^\n]{0,80}Sequence Parallel requires Tensor Parallel size\s*>\s*1
patterns.summary: Sequence parallelism was enabled while tensor parallel size remained 1. Megatron partitions sequence work across the tensor-parallel group, so there is no group to partition across in this configuration.
patterns.action:
NOW: either set tensor-model-parallel-size to at least 2 or disable sequence parallelism.
INVESTIGATE: print the resolved Megatron arguments on every rank. Launcher defaults or a stale checkpoint configuration can restore sequence_parallel after a command-line change.
PREVENT: validate sequence_parallel implies tensor_model_parallel_size > 1 before process-group initialization, so the job fails before allocating model memory.
ESCALATE: if tensor parallel size is already greater than 1, verify every rank received the same resolved configuration and that the tensor-parallel group was created successfully.
patterns.resumeFrom: job start after correcting parallelism settings

patterns.re: RuntimeError: The server socket has failed to listen on any local network address.* during AllGather.*
patterns.summary: Master node could not bind to the specified MASTER_ADDR and MASTER_PORT during Forward pass.
patterns.action: Ensure MASTER_ADDR points to a valid interface on the rank 0 node. (Observed in AllGather).

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Timeout initializing process group.* during ReduceScatter.*
patterns.summary: PyTorch distributed initialization timed out during Forward pass.

patterns.re: GPU util stays at 100%, no loss is printed
patterns.summary: DDP training hangs indefinitely when some GPUs receive a batch with no ground-truth targets (e.g., denoising conditionally skipped). Those GPUs do not add certain parameters to the graph. The gradient all_reduce waits on these GPUs, causing a deadlock despite find_unused_parameters=True.
patterns.action: Modify the conditional logic to always compute and include a dummy output (e.g., 0 * param.sum()) to ensure the parameter is part of the computation graph across all GPUs.

patterns.summary: The vLLM EngineCore was SIGKILLed, this is the host/cgroup OOM killer, not a CUDA OOM. GPU memory was fine; HOST RAM was exhausted. The usual cause is CPU KV-cache swap space (--swap-space, 4 GiB per GPU by default) plus pinned weight-loading buffers exceeding the container memory limit.
patterns.action:
NOW: raise the container memory limit, or lower --swap-space (set 0 to disable CPU offload entirely) and restart.
INVESTIGATE: dmesg -T | grep -i "killed process" for the true RSS at kill time; compare against the cgroup limit (/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max). Account for --swap-space x tensor_parallel_size, it multiplies per GPU worker, which is the step most sizing calculations miss.
PREVENT: set the container memory request/limit from measured peak RSS with the swap space included; alert on container_memory_working_set_bytes crossing 85% of limit rather than waiting for the kill.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, raise the host memory limit or lower --swap-space, then restart

requiredEvidence.re: oom-?kill|Out of memory: Killed|memory cgroup|Killed process|vllm|EngineCore

patterns.re: No available memory for the cache blocks|(?:model'?s? )?max seq len \(\d+\) is larger than the maximum number of tokens that can be stored in KV cache|Cannot allocate (?:KV|kv) cache|KV cache (?:is )?(?:full|exhausted)|no free (?:blocks|KV blocks)
patterns.summary: The engine could not reserve enough GPU memory for KV-cache blocks after loading weights. This is a capacity-planning failure, not a leak: weights + activation reserve + KV blocks did not fit in gpu_memory_utilization x total VRAM. Raising gpu_memory_utilization and lowering max_model_len pull in opposite directions and only one of them is safe for you.
patterns.action:
NOW: pick ONE lever and change it decisively, lower --max-model-len to the largest context you actually serve (biggest win, no quality cost), or lower --max-num-seqs to cap concurrency. Raise --gpu-memory-utilization only to 0.92-0.95 and only if nothing else shares the GPU; higher values OOM later, during graph capture, which looks like a different bug.
INVESTIGATE: read the startup line that reports available KV cache blocks and required blocks, the ratio tells you exactly how much to cut. Confirm nothing else is resident on the device (nvidia-smi): a monitoring agent or a second replica holding 2 GiB is a common invisible cause. On hybrid Mamba/attention models, vLLM 0.8.x overestimated KV requirements by up to 7x, so check your version against the model architecture.
PREVENT: compute the KV budget before deploy, 2 x layers x kv_heads x head_dim x dtype_bytes x max_model_len x max_num_seqs, and set the flags from it. Alert on GPU KV cache usage crossing 90% sustained, which precedes preemption thrash.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, resize the KV budget and restart the engine

patterns.re: Not enough memory\.\s*Please try to increase --mem-fraction-static|--mem-fraction-static[^\n]{0,60}(?:too (?:small|large)|increase|decrease)|Prefill out of memory[^\n]{0,60}(?:lower|reduce)
patterns.summary: SGLang's static memory pool could not be allocated at the requested fraction. --mem-fraction-static is not the same knob as vLLM's gpu_memory_utilization: it sizes the KV pool AFTER weights, so the correct direction depends on whether the failure was at pool allocation (decrease) or during prefill (the pool is too small, increase, and reduce max running requests instead).
patterns.action:
NOW: read WHERE it failed. Pool allocation failed → decrease --mem-fraction-static (try 0.80). Prefill OOM with the pool already allocated → the pool is too small for the batch: keep the fraction and lower --max-running-requests or --chunked-prefill-size instead.
INVESTIGATE: the startup log prints "KV Cache is allocated. #tokens: N", that N against your max context x concurrency is the real budget check. If another process shares the GPU, the fraction is computed against TOTAL memory, not free memory, which is the most common surprise here.
PREVENT: set --mem-fraction-static explicitly rather than relying on the default; the default assumes an otherwise-empty device.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, retune --mem-fraction-static and restart the server

patterns.summary: SGLang failed while capturing CUDA graphs under --enable-torch-compile. Capture happens at startup and needs headroom on top of the static pool, so this is usually a memory failure that presents as a compiler failure, the graph capture is simply the first thing to ask for memory after the pool is taken.
patterns.action:
NOW: lower --mem-fraction-static by 0.05 to leave capture headroom, or lower --cuda-graph-max-bs so fewer graphs are captured. To ship immediately, drop --enable-torch-compile and accept the decode-throughput loss.
INVESTIGATE: the error text distinguishes the two real causes, an OOM inside capture (memory) versus a Dynamo graph break or unsupported op (compiler). Only the second is a genuine compatibility problem, and for that check the torch/sgl-kernel version pairing against the model architecture.
PREVENT: pin torch and sgl-kernel as a tested pair; treat --enable-torch-compile as a change that requires a startup soak, not a hot config flip.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, restart with reduced capture scope or compile disabled

patterns.summary: LMDeploy's TurboMind KV cache could not be allocated at the configured cache_max_entry_count. Note the semantics differ from vLLM's: cache_max_entry_count is a fraction of FREE memory after weights load, not of total, so the same numeric value behaves differently depending on what else is resident on the device.
patterns.action:
NOW: lower cache_max_entry_count (try 0.5 as a diagnostic, then tune up). Because it is a fraction of FREE memory, anything else resident on the GPU shifts the effective budget, check nvidia-smi before concluding the value is wrong.
INVESTIGATE: confirm the quantization policy matches the artifact. Serving w4a16 weights with the wrong quant_policy loads a much larger footprint and presents as a cache-allocation failure. Read the [TM] log's reported free memory at allocation time.
PREVENT: set cache_max_entry_count explicitly per deployment and re-derive it when the model, quantization, or device changes.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, lower cache_max_entry_count and restart the api_server
