patterns.re: CUDA error: Wait on uncaptured stream.*during.*AllReduce.*overlapped with GEMM.*
patterns.summary: Synchronization failure between the custom communication stream and the compute stream during overlapped TP GEMM + AllReduce execution.
patterns.action: Insert explicit torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(comm_stream) synchronization points before executing dependent compute ops.

patterns.re: Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL.*Broadcast.*TP group.*
patterns.summary: NCCL watchdog timeout in TP Broadcast operation, typically when broadcasting initial weights from Rank 0 to other TP ranks.
patterns.action: Check network connectivity and firewall rules between Rank 0 and other ranks. Ensure hostnames resolve to correct private IPs.

patterns.re: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory.*fragmentation.*AllReduce.*tensor parallel.*
patterns.summary: Severe memory fragmentation during TP AllReduce buffer allocation. Memory exists but is too fragmented to allocate contiguous NCCL buffers.
patterns.action: Set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True to prevent fragmentation, or pre-allocate NCCL buffers at startup.

patterns.summary: AWS EFA receive operation failed.
patterns.action: Check EFA security group rules and MTU.

patterns.summary: IB disabled, fallback to socket dropped due to slow speed.
patterns.action: Enable IB with NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0 or increase timeout.

patterns.summary: PCIe retransmission timeout during NCCL sync.
patterns.action: Check PCIe slot physical seating.

patterns.summary: Epoll wait timed out waiting for socket event.
patterns.action: Check if peer rank is hung in computation.

patterns.summary: NUMA node memory exhaustion during SP.
patterns.action: Adjust numactl bindings or set vm.zone_reclaim_mode.

patterns.summary: NCCL graph launch failure.
patterns.action: Disable CUDA graphs for NCCL calls.

patterns.re: Empty shard(?: encountered)?|webdataset[^\n]{0,80}tarfile\.ReadError|tarfile\.ReadError[^\n]{0,80}(?:unexpected end of data|empty file)
patterns.summary: A WebDataset shard could not be read to completion. Either the object was truncated in the store or a pipeline worker died mid-read. The dangerous case is the quiet one: with the default handler the loader can skip the shard and keep training on a smaller dataset than intended, so the loss curve looks plausible and the run is not reproducible.
patterns.action: First establish which shard, then decide whether it is corrupt or merely slow. Verify the object size and checksum in the store against the manifest. Add `handler=wds.warn_and_continue` to the decode and shardshuffle stages only after you know how many shards are affected, because that handler converts a hard failure into silent data loss. Record the surviving shard count with the run so the training set is reproducible.
patterns.resumeFrom: restart the epoch after the shard list is verified, not from mid-epoch, because the sample order changed

patterns.summary: The DCGM exporter container was killed for exceeding its memory limit. GPU telemetry stops at that moment, so dashboards go flat and alerting goes quiet while the cluster itself is still running. The usual cause is cardinality rather than a leak: a high sampling frequency multiplied by a wide field list multiplied by ephemeral pod labels.
patterns.action: Cut the cardinality before raising the limit. Reduce the collection interval to 10 seconds or slower, trim the field list in the exporter ConfigMap to the fields anything actually queries, and drop ephemeral pod names with `metric_relabel_configs` on the scrape side. Then raise the container memory limit to sit above the observed steady-state peak with headroom. A flat GPU dashboard during an incident is worse than a coarse one.
patterns.resumeFrom: not applicable, this is the monitoring plane rather than the training job

patterns.summary: Synchronized GPU phase changes created a rack-level step load that exceeded PDU transient tolerance.
patterns.action: Escalate the timestamped PDU trace to facilities. For containment, apply an approved GPU power cap or stagger rank phases, then verify the same transition stays below the measured trip threshold.
patterns.resumeFrom: the last verified checkpoint before rack power loss

patterns.summary: Xid 62 reports an internal microcontroller halt. The event alone does not establish a memory leak or permanent hardware failure; driver, firmware, and hardware causes require investigation.
patterns.action:
NOW: drain the node and reset the GPU (nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i <id>); reboot if the reset is refused.
INVESTIGATE: preserve nvidia-bug-report.sh output and dmesg. Compare the driver and firmware with the OEM-supported baseline; the Xid alone does not identify a cause.
PREVENT: pin one driver/VBIOS combination per board type; track Xid 62 per GPU serial rather than per host, so a migrating card is visible.
ESCALATE: contact NVIDIA/OEM support if the fault recurs after recovery or diagnostics fail. Replacement depends on the vendor investigation, not an invented event-count threshold.
patterns.resumeFrom: latest checkpoint on a healthy node

patterns.re: NCCL WARN[^\n]{0,120}(Network is unreachable|No route to host)|Connect to [0-9.]+<\d+> failed[^\n]{0,40}(unreachable|No route)
patterns.summary: NCCL tried to reach a peer on an interface that cannot route to it. Almost always NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME selecting the wrong NIC, a docker0/lo/management interface instead of the fabric, so ranks advertise addresses their peers cannot reach.
patterns.action:
NOW: set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME explicitly to the fabric interface on every rank, e.g. export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 (or ^docker,lo to exclude rather than include). Restart the job.
INVESTIGATE: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and read the "NET/Socket : Using [0]<iface>" line, it names the interface each rank chose. Compare against ip -br addr on two nodes and confirm they share a routable subnet. In containers, check that the pod network actually spans nodes.
PREVENT: set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME in the job template rather than relying on NCCL's auto-selection, which picks the first non-loopback interface and is not deterministic across heterogeneous nodes.
ESCALATE: interfaces correct and still unreachable → routing/firewall between nodes, not NCCL.

patterns.re: (Failed to|Couldn't|Could not|Unable to) modify QP to RTR|modify QP to RTR[^\n]{0,40}errno 110
patterns.summary: An RDMA queue pair could not transition to Ready-To-Receive, so the connection never established. On RoCE this is nearly always a GID index or MTU mismatch between the two endpoints; on InfiniBand it points at the subnet manager not having configured the path.
patterns.action:
NOW: on RoCE, confirm both endpoints use the same GID index and RoCE version, show_gids on each host, and set NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX to match. Confirm MTU agrees on both sides.
INVESTIGATE: ibstat / ibv_devinfo, the port must be ACTIVE with a valid LID (InfiniBand) or a valid GID (RoCE). On IB, check that a subnet manager is running (sminfo). Test the raw path with ib_write_bw between the two hosts before blaming the application.
PREVENT: pin NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX and the MTU in the job template; validate the fabric with perftest during node acceptance.
ESCALATE: raw ib_write_bw also fails → fabric/SM problem, escalate to the network team with the port GUIDs from both ends.

patterns.re: Only Tensors of floating point dtype can require gradients|requires? grad[^\n]{0,40}torch\.(int8|uint8|int4)
patterns.summary: A LoRA adapter was attached to a quantized (int8/int4) base layer and the training path tried to make the quantized weight itself require gradients. Only the floating-point adapter weights are trainable; the quantized base must stay frozen.
patterns.action:
NOW: call prepare_model_for_kbit_training(model) after loading the quantized base and BEFORE get_peft_model(). It freezes the quantized weights and casts the layers that must stay in float.
INVESTIGATE: print the trainable set, [n for n,p in model.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]. Only lora_A/lora_B (and optionally norms and the head) should appear. Any base weight in that list is the bug.
PREVENT: keep the order load base → prepare_model_for_kbit_training → get_peft_model. Reversing the last two is the single most common cause.
ESCALATE: if a custom module sets requires_grad_(True) broadly, scope it to the adapter parameters instead.

patterns.re: Failed to initialize NVML[^\n]{0,60}(Libloading|cannot be found|could not load)|libnvidia-ml\.so[^\n]{0,40}(cannot be found|not found)
patterns.summary: The NVIDIA device plugin could not load libnvidia-ml.so, so it never registered nvidia.com/gpu with the kubelet. Every GPU pod on the node stays Pending with "Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" while the node itself looks healthy.
patterns.action:
NOW: check the plugin pod logs (kubectl logs -n gpu-operator -l app=nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset) and confirm the node advertises the resource: kubectl describe node <node> | grep nvidia.com/gpu.
INVESTIGATE: the library lives on the host and is mounted into the plugin container. A failure here means the driver is not installed on the host, the driver daemonset has not finished, or the volume mount / LD_LIBRARY_PATH does not reach it. Check driver readiness first, the plugin legitimately fails until the driver is up.
PREVENT: order the plugin behind the driver (the GPU Operator does this; a hand-rolled daemonset often does not). Add a node-level readiness gate so the scheduler does not consider the node before the resource is advertised.
ESCALATE: driver healthy and library present but the plugin still cannot load it → version skew between the driver and the plugin image.
patterns.resumeFrom: pod scheduling, once the resource is advertised

patterns.re: trtllm-build[^\n]{0,90}(Out of memory|OOM)|Out of memory during weight-only[^\n]{0,40}quantization
patterns.summary: The TensorRT-LLM engine build ran out of HOST memory, not GPU memory. Quantization holds full-precision weights in RAM while it converts them, so a 70B model can need well over 100 GB of system memory to build even though the resulting engine is small.
patterns.action:
NOW: build on a machine with more RAM, or add swap. Check the actual ceiling with free -g while the build runs, the failure is host-side.
INVESTIGATE: the peak is roughly the full-precision checkpoint size plus the quantized copy. Confirm you are not building inside a container with a memory limit lower than the host's (docker run -m / Kubernetes limits), that is the most common cause of an OOM on a machine that appears to have plenty.
PREVENT: build engines on a dedicated high-RAM builder rather than on the serving node, and cache the artifact. Serving nodes are sized for VRAM, not RAM.
ESCALATE: use a converted checkpoint format that streams weights (safetensors with lazy load) instead of materialising the whole model.
patterns.resumeFrom: engine build restart on a larger host

patterns.re: XlaRuntimeError[^\n]{0,60}RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED|RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED:[^\n]{0,60}Out of memory while trying to allocate
patterns.summary: XLA could not allocate device memory. JAX preallocates ~75% of VRAM at first use by default, so an OOM here often reflects the preallocation policy or memory fragmentation across recompilations rather than a genuinely oversized model.
patterns.action:
NOW: try XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=false, or set XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION to a value that leaves room for other processes. If another process shares the GPU, preallocation is almost certainly the cause.
INVESTIGATE: the message states the exact byte count requested, compare it against free VRAM. Check for repeated recompilation (jax.log_compiles(True)): each distinct input shape produces a new executable, and shape churn fragments the arena.
PREVENT: pad inputs to fixed bucket shapes so XLA compiles a bounded set of executables. Use donate_argnums to let XLA reuse input buffers for outputs.
ESCALATE: genuinely too large → shard with jax.sharding across devices, or enable gradient checkpointing (jax.checkpoint).

patterns.summary: The kubelet evicted the pod for exceeding its ephemeral-storage limit. On training pods this is almost always checkpoint or dataset cache written to the container filesystem instead of to a mounted volume.
patterns.action:
NOW: identify what is filling the writable layer, commonly HuggingFace cache (~/.cache/huggingface), checkpoint output, or logs. Mount a volume for each and point the corresponding env var at it (HF_HOME, output_dir).
INVESTIGATE: kubectl describe pod shows the limit and observed usage. Note that emptyDir also counts toward ephemeral-storage unless it is memory-backed or a real PVC.
PREVENT: give training pods a PVC for checkpoints and caches, and set ephemeral-storage requests/limits deliberately rather than inheriting a namespace default sized for stateless services.
ESCALATE: if checkpoints must be local for speed, use a hostPath or local NVMe PV and upload asynchronously.
patterns.resumeFrom: latest checkpoint on the mounted volume

patterns.summary: The GPU Operator driver daemonset could not build the NVIDIA kernel module for the running kernel. Until it succeeds the node has no driver, so every GPU pod stays Pending while the node otherwise looks healthy.
patterns.action:
NOW: read the driver container logs (kubectl logs -n gpu-operator -l app=nvidia-driver-daemonset). The build error names the missing piece, usually kernel headers or a compiler version mismatch.
INVESTIGATE: the driver container must match the HOST kernel. A node that auto-upgraded its kernel without a matching driver image is the usual cause. Confirm: uname -r on the node vs the kernel the driver image targets. Precompiled driver images only cover specific kernel versions.
PREVENT: pin node kernel versions, or use the precompiled driver image matched to your node OS image and upgrade both together. Disable unattended kernel upgrades on GPU nodes.
ESCALATE: gcc version mismatch specifically → the driver must be built with the same compiler the kernel was; use the operator's matching driver toolkit image rather than the generic one.
patterns.resumeFrom: pod scheduling, once the driver is loaded

patterns.summary: Priority Flow Control pause frames saturated a link. PFC exists to make RoCE lossless, but a congested or misconfigured fabric can propagate pause backward through switches, a "congestion tree" that stalls traffic far from the original hotspot.
patterns.action:
NOW: identify the congestion point rather than the reporting node. The host logging the storm is usually a victim; the source is wherever the pause originated.
INVESTIGATE: check PFC counters on the switch ports along the path (pause frames sent vs received). A port sending far more pauses than it receives is near the source. Confirm PFC is enabled consistently on the same priority across every host and switch, a single mismatched hop creates exactly this.
PREVENT: deploy ECN/DCQCN alongside PFC so congestion is signalled end-to-end and rate-limited at the sender, rather than relying on pause frames alone. Alert on PFC pause duration.
ESCALATE: fabric-wide storms → network team; this is a switch configuration problem, not a host one.

patterns.re: OMP: Error #15|libomp\.so[^\n]{0,70}libgomp\.so already initialized|found libgomp\.so already initialized
patterns.summary: Two OpenMP runtimes were loaded into one process (Intel/LLVM libomp alongside GNU libgomp). Behaviour is undefined, in practice thread pools collide, causing deadlocks, oversubscription, or crashes in multi-threaded inference.
patterns.action:
NOW: find which libraries pull in each runtime, ldd on the offending .so files, or set LD_DEBUG=libs to trace load order. MKL/Intel builds pull libomp; many PyPI wheels built with GCC pull libgomp.
INVESTIGATE: the common pairing is a conda numpy/MKL alongside a pip-installed torch or a compiled extension. Standardise on one channel for everything that links OpenMP.
PREVENT: install the whole numeric stack from one source (all conda, or all pip with consistent wheels). KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE silences the message but leaves the undefined behaviour in place, do not use it as a fix.
ESCALATE: if both runtimes are unavoidable, pin OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 to remove the thread-pool collision at the cost of intra-op parallelism.
patterns.resumeFrom: process restart with a consistent runtime

patterns.summary: FSDP ran out of memory gathering a layer's full weights for the forward pass. Sharding reduces STEADY-STATE memory, but each layer is briefly unsharded to compute, so the peak is set by the largest single layer, not by the sharded average.
patterns.action:
NOW: reduce the unshard peak rather than the model size. Enable CPU offload for parameters, or wrap at a finer granularity so fewer parameters are gathered at once.
INVESTIGATE: the message names the layer. Look at its parameter count, a single fat embedding or MLP projection is usually the whole peak. torch.cuda.memory_summary() right before the failure shows how much headroom was actually left.
PREVENT: set an explicit auto_wrap_policy (transformer_auto_wrap_policy on the block class) instead of wrapping the whole model as one unit, an unwrapped model gathers everything simultaneously and defeats sharding at exactly this moment.
ESCALATE: still short at the finest useful wrap granularity → activation checkpointing, or move to a larger-memory GPU; the layer genuinely does not fit.

patterns.re: graph replay[^\n]{0,60}invalidated memory|CUDA graph replay detected invalidated
patterns.summary: A CUDA graph was replayed after the memory it captured was freed or reallocated. Graphs record raw device pointers, so any tensor whose storage moved between capture and replay leaves the graph reading memory that is no longer its own.
patterns.action:
NOW: make the input and output buffers STATIC. Allocate them once, copy new data into them in place (static_input.copy_(new_data)), and replay, never rebind the graph to freshly allocated tensors.
INVESTIGATE: anything that reallocates between capture and replay breaks this, a changing batch shape, torch.empty inside the step, or an allocator flush (torch.cuda.empty_cache()). Confirm shapes are identical every iteration.
PREVENT: use torch.cuda.graphs.make_graphed_callables or the CUDAGraph pool APIs, which own the static buffers for you. Do not call empty_cache() while graphs are live.
ESCALATE: genuinely dynamic shapes cannot be graphed, bucket them into a small set of fixed shapes and capture one graph per bucket.

patterns.re: NVDEC[^\n]{0,80}(decode sessions|stream allocation failed)|concurrent video decode sessions[^\n]{0,20}exceeded
patterns.summary: The GPU's hardware video decoder ran out of concurrent sessions. NVDEC session count is a fixed hardware/driver limit, and consumer boards are capped far below data-center parts regardless of available memory.
patterns.action:
NOW: cap concurrent decoders in the dataloader to below the board's limit, or reuse a decoder pool instead of creating one per worker.
INVESTIGATE: count how many decode contexts are actually open, it is usually num_workers × videos-in-flight, which multiplies faster than people expect. GeForce boards are limited well below A100/L40S class.
PREVENT: pool decoders and hand them out, rather than allocating per sample. For large-scale pipelines, pre-decode to frames offline and read those; hardware decode is rarely the throughput bottleneck once workers are tuned.
ESCALATE: sessions are a hardware ceiling, if the pipeline genuinely needs more, fall back to CPU decode for the overflow or move to a data-center GPU.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint action; reduce decoder concurrency and restart

patterns.re: TarError[^\n]{0,80}Unexpected end of archive|Unexpected end of archive while reading shard
patterns.summary: A WebDataset tar shard ended mid-record. The shard is truncated, either the upload was incomplete, or an HTTP stream was cut and the reader treated the partial body as the whole file.
patterns.action:
NOW: identify the shard from the message and verify it independently: tar -tf <shard> (local) or compare Content-Length against the bytes actually received (HTTP).
INVESTIGATE: over HTTP this is usually a connection reset being read as EOF rather than a genuinely corrupt object. Retry the same shard, if it reads cleanly, the object is fine and the transport is at fault.
PREVENT: store and check a size or checksum per shard, and configure the reader to retry on short reads rather than treating them as end-of-data. Silent truncation means the run trains on a subset without ever reporting it.
ESCALATE: the object really is truncated in storage → re-upload that shard; a partial shard skews the epoch and is worth fixing rather than skipping.
patterns.resumeFrom: latest checkpoint; re-shard or re-upload before resuming

patterns.re: nvidia-gridd|Failed to acquire license from DLS
patterns.summary: The vGPU guest could not reach its Delegated License Service. NVIDIA vGPU throttles clocks severely when unlicensed, so the symptom users report is "the GPU got slow", not "a license expired".
patterns.action:
NOW: check the licensing service in the guest, nvidia-smi -q | grep -A3 "vGPU Software Licensed Product", and systemctl status nvidia-gridd.
INVESTIGATE: confirm the guest can reach the DLS host and port (7070 by default), this breaks after network policy changes far more often than after license changes. Check the client configuration token has not expired.
PREVENT: monitor license lease state in the guest and alert on expiry, not on the resulting slowdown. Performance degradation is a terrible first signal for a licensing problem and sends people debugging the workload.
ESCALATE: DLS reachable and lease still refused → license server capacity or an expired entitlement; check the served/available counts on the DLS instance.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint action; clocks restore when licensed

patterns.summary: A Habana collective timed out waiting for a peer. Like every collective timeout this names the ranks that WERE waiting, not the one that failed to arrive, the OAM module in the message is the reporter, not necessarily the fault.
patterns.action:
NOW: find the module that did not participate rather than debugging the one that reported. Check hl-smi across all nodes for a device in a bad state.
INVESTIGATE: verify the scale-out network between nodes (Gaudi uses RoCE over its own ports) and that every rank sees the same world size. hl-smi -Q shows link status per port; a single down port removes a path and stalls the collective.
PREVENT: run a hccl_demo all-reduce preflight before large jobs, and monitor per-port link state. Gaudi's fabric is integrated, so a port fault presents as a hang rather than an error.
ESCALATE: all modules healthy and links up → raise with Habana support including the HCL log and the world-size configuration; do not treat it as an application bug.

patterns.action:
NOW: make the mapping unique, every rank in the communicator must own exactly one device. The usual cause is the launcher, not the code: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` pinned to a single index while more than one task per node was requested means every local rank sees that one device as index 0. Either widen CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to one index per local rank, or drop it and let each rank select its own device with `torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)` before `init_process_group`.
INVESTIGATE: print `local_rank`, `torch.cuda.current_device()` and the PCI busId from every rank at startup. Two ranks reporting the same busId is the defect, and it is visible before NCCL ever runs. In containers, also confirm the runtime is not mounting the same /dev/nvidia* device into several ranks.
PREVENT: assert the mapping is unique at startup, gather the busId from every rank and fail fast if the set is smaller than the world size. That turns a confusing NCCL abort into a one-line configuration error.

patterns.action: Decrease num_workers in DataLoader or increase OS locked memory limits.

patterns.summary: System RAM exhausted during ZeRO CPU offloading.
patterns.action: Enable NVMe offload or increase system RAM.

patterns.re: Failed to allocate communication buffer in DeepSpeed
patterns.summary: DeepSpeed could not allocate contiguous memory for all-reduce buffers.
patterns.action: Reduce reduce_bucket_size in DeepSpeed ZeRO config.

patterns.summary: Failed to allocate bf16 tensor during mixed precision training.

patterns.re: Failed to allocate fp32 master weights for DeepSpeed
patterns.summary: OOM creating FP32 master weights for mixed precision.

patterns.summary: Host memory exhausted during ZeRO-3 parameter CPU offloading.

patterns.re: DeepSpeed NVMe offload failed to allocate
patterns.summary: NVMe offload failed due to disk space or mapping error.

patterns.action: Reduce max_tokens or batch size for inference.

patterns.summary: DeepSpeed could not allocate contiguous memory for comm buffers.
patterns.action: Reduce reduce_bucket_size in DeepSpeed ZeRO config.

patterns.summary: Host memory exhausted during FSDP parameter CPU offloading.
patterns.action: Increase system RAM or swap space.

patterns.summary: OOM allocating mixed precision buffers in FSDP.
patterns.action: Check MixedPrecision configuration to ensure bf16 is used for parameters and buffers.

patterns.summary: OOM while instantiating FSDP model from meta device.
patterns.action: Ensure parameters are materialized iteratively.

patterns.summary: OOM in FSDP side stream used for unsharding parameters.
patterns.action: Limit prefetching or use single-stream FSDP execution.

patterns.summary: find_unused_parameters overhead caused OOM.
patterns.action: Set find_unused_parameters=False if not needed.

patterns.summary: Torch RPC framework exhausted memory receiving tensors.
patterns.action: Limit concurrent RPC calls.

patterns.summary: OOM while Accelerate moves model shards to devices.
patterns.action: Adjust max_memory map in dispatch_model.

patterns.summary: HuggingFace Datasets map function exhausted CPU RAM.
patterns.action: Reduce num_proc or use batched=True.

patterns.summary: vLLM tensor parallel NCCL communication failed due to memory.
patterns.action: Ensure enough unreserved GPU memory for NCCL buffers.

patterns.re: CUDA out of memory during vLLM memory profiling
patterns.summary: vLLM profiling step OOMed while determining max KV cache blocks.
patterns.action: Reduce max_num_seqs or enable enforce_eager.

patterns.re: NCCL WARN Bootstrap connection.*timeout|Hang during NCCL connection establishment
patterns.summary: In multi-rail configurations on AWS instances with multiple EFA devices, NCCL connection establishment can hang indefinitely during bootstrap if the number of rails isn't correctly detected or utilized by the aws-ofi-nccl plugin.
patterns.action: Explicitly set the environment variable OFI_NCCL_FORCE_NUM_RAILS=<num_interfaces> (e.g., 4 for p4d, 8 or 32 depending on setup) to enforce correct utilization of all EFA interfaces and resolve the deadlock.

requiredEvidence.re: Multi-node distributed training setup with multiple EFA interfaces per node (e.g., p4d or p5 instances)
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO shows process stuck during bootstrap\/connection establishment

patterns.summary: Using generic HPC-X MPI distributions with the EFA provider can lead to device-not-found errors or silent communication hangs. Generic MPI distributions lack the specific integrations, patches, and configurations present in the Amazon-provided OpenMPI.
patterns.action: Switch to the Amazon-provided OpenMPI included with the AWS EFA installer, which is explicitly tested and patched for full compatibility with EFA and libfabric.

requiredEvidence.re: Application is a multi-node MPI workload running on EFA-enabled instances
Generic HPC-X MPI is being used instead of the Amazon-provided OpenMPI

patterns.summary: Training or fine-tuning large OPT models in BF16 diverges because the layer normalization epsilon (e.g., 1e-8) is vastly smaller than BF16's minimum representable precision. The epsilon underflows to 0, leading to division by zero if the variance is also small.
patterns.action: Change the LayerNorm epsilon value in the model configuration to a larger value (e.g., 1e-3 or 1e-2) that is safely representable in BF16, or keep LayerNorm computations strictly in FP32.
patterns.resumeFrom: restart fine-tuning from pretrained weights with updated config

patterns.summary: Memory corruption or out-of-bounds memory access during CUDA graph replay, frequently caused by stale pointers or improper KV cache padding in generated kernels.
patterns.action: Set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to identify the offending kernel, fix stale pointers, or disable graph replay to verify kernel correctness.

patterns.summary: In large multi-slice deployments, kuberay-tpu-webhook truncates long service names, resulting in malformed TPU_WORKER_HOSTNAMES environment variables and causing distributed training initialization to hang.
patterns.action: Upgrade kuberay-tpu-webhook to the latest version which fixes service name truncation, or use shorter release/cluster names to avoid hitting the 63-character limit.

patterns.re: received NVLink inband message arrived on an NVLink .* which is not part of any active partition
patterns.summary: A synchronization or configuration mismatch between the NVIDIA driver and the NVSwitch fabric routing table causes packets to arrive on unpartitioned NVLinks. This often occurs during multi-node scaling with dynamic topology changes or physical link instability.
patterns.action: Check for Fabric Manager link failures and adjust ACCESS_LINK_FAILURE_MODE in nv-fabricmanager configuration if links are physically flapping. Otherwise, restart Fabric Manager to clear and rebuild partition tables.

requiredEvidence.re: syslog showing NVLink inband message routing error
multiple GPU nodes communicating over NVSwitch

patterns.re: Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL\(OpType=BROADCAST, Timeout\(ms\)=\d+\) ran for \d+ milliseconds
patterns.summary: NCCL watchdog times out during multi-GPU evaluation due to an unrecoverable Peer-to-Peer (P2P) communication failure between specific GPUs.
patterns.action: Set the environment variable NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 to disable P2P communication, falling back to shared memory and PCIe.

patterns.re: Worker \(pid:\d+\) was sent SIGKILL!\[CRITICAL\] WORKER TIMEOUT
patterns.summary: Deploying a HuggingFace Transformers pipeline using Gunicorn with the '--preload' flag causes worker timeouts. The model and tokenizer are loaded in the master process and then forked to workers. The Rust threads for the FastTokenizer do not survive the fork, deadlocking incoming inference requests.
patterns.action: Disable '--preload' in Gunicorn so each worker initializes its own tokenizer, or set TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false to disable the multi-threaded fast tokenizer.

patterns.summary: InfiniBand Subnet Manager experienced continuous flapping and failed to stabilize the fabric due to a cloned OS image introducing duplicate Node GUIDs. This caused continuous Set(PortInfo) MAD packet drops and effectively split the subnet.
patterns.action: Identify and re-generate unique Node GUIDs on the cloned hosts, then restart the Subnet Manager service.

requiredEvidence.re: UFM events showing Subnet Manager mastership flapping
Multiple nodes with identical Node GUIDs

patterns.summary: When using communication libraries like mpi4jax with JAX on TPUs, the XLA compiler may optimize away CustomCall operations that do not have explicit data dependencies, causing mismatched send/receive calls across ranks.
patterns.action: Ensure all custom communication callbacks are flagged with has_side_effect=True or enforce explicit token-based control dependencies.

patterns.summary: DeepSpeed ZeRO-2/3 with CPU offload shifts optimizer states and gradients to CPU RAM. In distributed Kubernetes setups, if the Pod's memory limits are not provisioned to handle the full model state and optimizer states multiplied by the number of offloaded ranks, the pod gets OOMKilled.
patterns.action: Increase pod CPU memory limits. Alternatively, tune DeepSpeed cpu_offload params (e.g., enabling NVMe offloading) or reduce batch size.

requiredEvidence.re: OOMKilled exactly during step() or backward pass

patterns.summary: Ray relies on shared memory for its plasma object store. In Kubernetes, if the pod limit is lower than the physical node memory but Ray sizes itself based on node memory, or if the object store overflows the container's /dev/shm limit, the cgroup OOM killer terminates the pod.
patterns.action: Explicitly set --object-store-memory and --memory limits when starting Ray nodes, ensuring their sum fits comfortably within the pod's limits.memory.
patterns.resumeFrom: restart ray cluster and resume tuning from checkpoint

patterns.re: Failed to attach to shared memory segment
patterns.summary: On systems with multiple NUMA nodes, NCCL cuMem host allocations fail on some nodes, causing fallback to /dev/shm. Processes fail to communicate because they are attached to different memory mechanisms.
patterns.action: Set environment variable 'NCCL_CUMEM_HOST_ENABLE=0' to force consistent /dev/shm allocation across nodes.

patterns.re: nvidia-container-cli: container error: cgroup mount point not found
patterns.summary: In Kubernetes environments where the container runtime uses the systemd cgroup driver, it creates complex nested cgroup paths (e.g., `kubepods-...`). Older versions of `nvidia-container-cli` fail to parse these hierarchies, unable to locate the correct mount point.
patterns.action: Upgrade to NVIDIA Container Toolkit >= 1.8.0 which improves systemd path parsing, switch to CDI (Container Device Interface), or revert the container runtime to use the `cgroupfs` driver.

requiredEvidence.re: systemd cgroup driver used in kubernetes

patterns.summary: The background pin_memory thread deadlocks while waiting for a queue condition if worker processes crash silently or there are OS-level threading conflicts during epoch shutdown.
patterns.action: Set pin_memory=False to bypass the background pinning thread, or ensure drop_last=True.
patterns.resumeFrom: Restart training script from latest checkpoint

patterns.re: ActorDiedError: The actor died unexpectedly before finishing this task.*SIGSEGV
patterns.summary: Ray Train worker processes crash unexpectedly with a segmentation fault when PyTorch DataLoaders are configured with multi-processing (num_workers > 0). The forks made by the dataloader conflict with Ray's internal threading or CUDA context management.
patterns.action: Set `num_workers=0` in the PyTorch DataLoader configuration, or switch to using `ray.data` for distributed data ingestion.

patterns.re: DataLoader worker \(pid \d+\) is killed by signal|GPU utilization drops to 0%
patterns.summary: Slurm restricts the CPU affinity of the main PyTorch process to a specific set of cores. PyTorch DataLoader workers inherit this exact CPU affinity mask. Due to how Slurm enforces binding, all child dataloader workers may end up fighting for a single logical core or a restricted core set, causing severe data-loading bottlenecks and GPU starvation.
patterns.action: Ensure `--cpus-per-task` matches `num_workers + 1` in Slurm. Use PyTorch's `worker_init_fn` or `os.sched_setaffinity` in the dataset to explicitly distribute worker processes across the allocated CPU cores, overcoming the inherited single-core lock.

requiredEvidence.re: Slurm `--cpus-per-task` is set, restricting the CPU set

patterns.re: Invalid shape and type mismatch in elementwise addition
patterns.summary: During trtllm-build, the network graph encounters an elementwise addition node where one input is BFloat16 (from model weights) and the other is Float (from a plugin or unsynced constant), causing an immediate build failure.
patterns.action: Verify convert_checkpoint.py casted all necessary biases or residual constants to BFloat16, and explicitly configure plugins (e.g. --gemm_plugin bfloat16) to match the model weights.
patterns.resumeFrom: Rerun convert_checkpoint.py with consistent precision flags.

patterns.summary: JIT compiling persistent kernels with num_stages > 1 can lead to segmentation faults due to incorrect shared memory allocation or invalid tile size configurations during pipeline generation.
patterns.action: Reduce num_stages=1 in the @triton.jit configuration to disable pipelining, or properly align tile sizes to shared memory banks.
patterns.resumeFrom: Restart script with modified kernel configuration

patterns.re: The V1 engine consistently fails to initialize.*ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks
patterns.summary: The vLLM V1 Engine over-estimates KV cache block allocation on GPUs with smaller memory (e.g., 12GB), leading to initialization crashes even when the V0 engine worked perfectly.
patterns.action: Set environment variable `VLLM_USE_V1=0` to fallback to the stable V0 engine, or significantly lower `--gpu-memory-utilization`.

patterns.summary: Pipeline parallelism fails because a stage input does not produce gradients w.r.t. the next stage. PP computes and returns a gradient for every input tensor of a stage over dist.isend, which carries tensors and cannot carry None, so an input that legitimately has no gradient has nothing to send. The same model runs under FSDP or without parallelism because neither requires a per-input gradient to cross a stage boundary, that contrast is the diagnostic, not a sign the model is wrong.
patterns.action:
1. Identify which stage input has no gradient path. At the stage boundary, check each input after backward:
   for n, t in stage_inputs.items(): print(n, t.requires_grad, t.grad_fn is not None)
2. If the tensor is only being FORWARDED and is not meant to be differentiated (routing indices, masks, position ids, MoE assignments), detach it at the boundary so PP does not expect a gradient for it:
   x = x.detach()
3. If it should be differentiated, make sure the path is real, a branch taken only conditionally will produce no gradient on the steps it is not taken, which is the same failure appearing intermittently.
4. As a bounded workaround, pass a zeros_like gradient for that input so the P2P send has a tensor to carry, and confirm the parameter updates are unchanged against an FSDP control run before trusting it.
5. This is an upstream limitation rather than a misconfiguration: record the PyTorch version, and check the release notes or bisect across versions before assuming a code change on your side is required.

patterns.re: setting `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1` result in an OOM error
patterns.summary: Using pipeline parallelism (`--pipeline-parallel-size > 1`) allocates KV cache blocks unevenly across GPUs. This causes memory fragmentation or OOM on specific pipeline stages, unlike tensor parallelism which partitions evenly.
patterns.action: Switch to `--tensor-parallel-size` if running on the same node, or tune `--gpu-memory-utilization` downwards to leave more headroom for intermediate activations.

patterns.summary: PCIe switch buffer overrun during massive MoE AllToAll phases caused micro-latency spikes breaking NCCL.
patterns.action: Lower `NCCL_BUFFSIZE` to prevent overwhelming the PCIe switch buffers during burst communication phases.

patterns.summary: Micro-voltage drop (PSU/VRM) caused instant hardware slowdown and corrupted multiple ASIC domains.
patterns.action: Check nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE for HW Slowdown. This is a severe electrical fault. RMA the PSU or GPU immediately. Firmware updates will not fix this.

patterns.summary: GPU Hardware Fault (REBOOT Tier) - Xid 79/151/168 detected. The GPU has fallen off the bus or requires a full node reboot to recover.
patterns.action: Drain the affected node. Reboot the host system completely to re-initialize the PCIe bus and GPU state.

negativeEvidence.re: replay(?:ing|ed)? archived|archived dmesg|postmortem|historical log|end of archive

patterns.summary: NVSwitch hardware error (SXid), a system-wide NVSwitch fault affecting all connected GPUs.
patterns.action: `dmesg -T | grep SXid` and `journalctl -u nvidia-fabricmanager -n 100`. Restart Fabric Manager: `systemctl restart nvidia-fabricmanager`. If persistent, schedule RMA for the NVSwitch board.

patterns.summary: GPU dropped off the PCIe bus during DMA (Xid 64), bus mastering died mid-transfer.
patterns.action: Node reboot is required to recover the PCIe bus state. If recurrent, reseat the GPU or RMA the baseboard.

patterns.summary: NVLink uncorrectable error (Xid 74), data integrity fault on the NVLink fabric.
patterns.action: Target the GPU logging the Xid 74 for diagnostics. If paired with an SXid, the NVSwitch is the root cause. Otherwise, check for NVLink lane degradation.

patterns.summary: RmInitAdapter Failure - The NVIDIA driver failed to initialize the GPU adapter.
patterns.action: This often indicates the GPU has fallen off the bus or is physically damaged. Reboot the node. If it persists, RMA the GPU.

patterns.re: (?:sm clock|graphics clock).*throttled|downclocking to \d+\.?\d* GHz|clock frequency dropped
patterns.summary: SM Clock Throttling Detected - Hardware is downclocking, causing performance asymmetry (micro-straggler).
patterns.action: Check GPU temperatures and power delivery. Downclocking is typically a self-preservation mechanism for thermal limits or power cap enforcement.

patterns.summary: Severe Iteration Straggler - A specific step took >10,000ms, indicating a gray failure or node degradation.
patterns.action: Correlate with thermal throttling or ECC correctable errors on this specific node. If this rank consistently spikes, drain the node to prevent collective drag.

patterns.summary: InfiniBand NIC Hardware Error - mlx5/IB core fatal error detected on the host.
patterns.action: Check `ibstatus` or `ibv_devinfo`. If the port is DOWN or reports a hardware fault, a node reboot is required. Reset the NIC via PCI if reboot fails.

patterns.summary: InfiniBand Retry Exceeded - Receiver Not Ready (RNR) NAKs indicate the receiving node is overwhelmed or hung.
patterns.action: This is often a symptom of the remote node hanging (e.g., CPU OOM or Kernel Deadlock). Denpex will isolate the hung node.

patterns.summary:
NCCL could not open a connection to one specific rank during bootstrap. This is reachability, not a GPU fault.

The NCCL proxy thread sets up the transport between pairs of ranks before any collective runs.
"Proxy Call to rank N failed (Connect)" means that handshake never completed with that one rank.
The surrounding "ncclInternalError: Internal check failed" is NCCL's catch-all wrapper and says
nothing on its own, which is why the rank number and the "(Connect)" qualifier are the whole
signal here.

Because this happens at INIT, the job usually dies before a single step, and the GPUs are
typically healthy. Chasing Xid errors or updating drivers is the wrong direction.

What this does not establish. It does not say WHY that rank is unreachable. The three usual
causes are a blocked port range, the wrong network interface being selected, and the peer process
having already exited. Step 2 separates them, and they need different fixes.
patterns.action:
Find out why that specific rank is unreachable, before changing anything else.

1. Confirm the peer is actually alive. A rank that crashed during its own init looks identical
   from here. Check that rank's own log first, and its exit code if it is gone. If it died, it is
   the real incident and this is the symptom.

2. If the peer is alive, test reachability from the failing host to it:
     ping -c3 <peer-host>
     nc -vz <peer-host> <port>          # NCCL uses ephemeral ports, not just MASTER_PORT
   A ping that works with a refused port is a firewall or security-group rule.

3. Open the port range NCCL actually needs. It negotiates ephemeral ports by default; either
   allow the ephemeral range between the nodes, or pin it:
     export NCCL_PORT_RANGE=<low>-<high>     # then allow exactly that range

4. Make sure every rank chooses the SAME interface. On multi-homed hosts NCCL can pick a
   management NIC on one node and the fabric on another, and they cannot reach each other:
     export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=<the fabric interface, e.g. ib0 or eth1>
   Verify with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO that every rank logs the same interface.

5. Re-run and confirm the job reaches its first collective. Verify:
     NCCL_DEBUG=INFO <launch> 2>&1 | grep -i "Connected all rings"
   That line is the proof the transport came up for every pair, not just for most of them.
patterns.resumeFrom: job restart once the peer is reachable

patterns.summary: NFS Storage Disconnect - The NFS mount dropped or the file handle was invalidated.
patterns.action: Remount the NFS volume on the affected node. If the NFS server is saturated, consider staging data locally.

patterns.summary: D-State Task Hang - A process is stuck in uninterruptible sleep (D-state), waiting on hardware or network I/O.
patterns.action: Usually caused by a dead storage mount (NFS/GPFS) or a failing PCIe bus. The node must be rebooted, as D-state tasks cannot be killed (`kill -9` will fail).

patterns.summary: GSP RPC Timeout - The GPU System Processor (GSP) firmware stopped responding to the driver.
patterns.action: Reboot the node. If the issue persists, disable GSP-RM via module parameter: `options nvidia NVreg_EnableGpuFirmware=0`.

patterns.summary: Hardware Slowdown (Thermal) - GPU is derating clock speeds specifically due to thermal limits.
patterns.action: Investigate rack cooling and node fan RPMs. If using liquid cooling, check the coolant loop for leaks or blockages. Thermal throttling causes significant global stragglers.

patterns.summary: Hardware Slowdown (Power) - GPU is derating clock speeds specifically due to power delivery issues or enforced power caps.
patterns.action: Verify power limits (`nvidia-smi -pl`). Check PSU health. Power capping creates unpredictable performance asymmetry across the cluster.

patterns.re: (?:Torchrun elastic agent fails to discover all peers|SLURM_PROCID does not match the expected LOCAL_RANK|Connection refused during Torch distributed rendezvous)
patterns.summary: Torchrun and SLURM Job Step Incompatibility
patterns.action: Avoid torchrun when using srun; initialize process groups directly using SLURM environment variables, or run a single torchrun command per node.

patterns.re: (?:NCCL timeout during gather_state_dict|timeout waiting for rank 0 to broadcast|stuck in torch.save)
patterns.summary: Checkpoint Save/Restore Gathering Timeout
patterns.action: Use distributed checkpointing (e.g., FSDP native sharded state_dict or DistCP) instead of gathering the full model to rank 0.

patterns.re: (?:nvlddmkm stopped responding and has successfully recovered|TDR detected|Display driver nvlddmkm stopped responding)
patterns.summary: nvlddmkm TDR (Timeout Detection and Recovery)
patterns.action: Increase TdrDelay in the registry, or resolve thermal throttling. Lower GPU memory clocks or power limits to improve stability.

patterns.re: PytorchStreamReader failed reading zip archive|failed finding central directory|unsupported pickle protocol|invalid load key|ValueError: unsupported pickle protocol
patterns.summary:
The checkpoint is fine. The process reading it is older than the process that wrote it.

"failed finding central directory" reads like corruption and almost never is when the log also
records a version difference between writer and reader. PyTorch writes checkpoints as a zip
container, and the container format has changed across releases: a file written with a newer
torch (and, with pickle protocol 5, a newer Python) is not always readable by an older one. The
bytes are intact, the reader just cannot parse the header.

This is why falling back to an earlier checkpoint does not help. Every checkpoint in the run was
written by the same container, so they all fail the same way, and walking backwards through them
costs hours and finds nothing.

What this does not establish. It does not say which of Python or torch is the binding constraint.
Step 1 below answers that in a few seconds, and it is worth running before changing anything,
because upgrading the wrong one leaves you exactly where you started.
patterns.action:
Confirm the archive is intact, then read it with a matching environment.

1. Prove it is not corruption, so you stop treating it as corruption:
     unzip -t /path/to/model.pt        # a clean archive reports "No errors detected"
     md5sum /path/to/model.pt          # compare against the copy on the writing node
   If both pass, the file is byte-for-byte correct and the reader is the problem.

2. Read the versions that matter, on BOTH sides:
     python -c "import sys, torch; print(sys.version, torch.__version__)"
   Pickle protocol 5 needs Python 3.8 or newer. The newer zip container needs a torch recent
   enough to know it, and that is usually the binding constraint rather than Python.

3. Load with the writer's environment. The container image that produced the checkpoint is the
   fastest correct answer, and it needs no conversion.

4. If you must read it from the older environment, convert it once from the newer one:
     # in the WRITER environment
     import torch
     sd = torch.load("model.pt", map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
     torch.save(sd, "model_legacy.pt", _use_new_zipfile_serialization=False, pickle_protocol=4)
   Protocol 4 and the legacy container are readable by considerably older stacks.

5. To stop it recurring, pin the training and inference images to the same torch version, or
   record the writer torch/Python version in the checkpoint directory and fail fast at load time
   when they disagree, rather than surfacing it as a zip error.
patterns.resumeFrom: the same checkpoint, loaded with the torch version that wrote it

patterns.summary: SGLang's DetokenizerManager process is gone or its IPC channel is broken. Generation continues on the GPU but no text reaches clients, requests hang or return empty. The GPU stays busy, so every utilisation-based health signal reports the server as healthy.
patterns.action:
NOW: restart the server; a detached detokenizer cannot be reattached. Drain first, in-flight requests will never complete.
INVESTIGATE: look for an OOM kill of the detokenizer child (dmesg -T | grep -i "killed process", it holds the full tokenizer, which is not free for large vocabularies) and for ZMQ socket errors in its own stderr. Confirm the tokenizer files are still readable if they live on a network mount that may have gone stale (stat the tokenizer.json path from inside the container).
PREVENT: make the readiness probe request a real completion and assert non-empty TEXT, a probe that only checks the process or /health cannot see this failure at all.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, restart the server; in-flight requests are unrecoverable

patterns.summary: trtllm-serve could not load the engine directory. Almost always a shape problem in the artifact: the engine directory must contain one rankN.engine per tensor-parallel rank plus config.json, and a partially-synced or wrong-TP artifact fails here rather than at build.
patterns.action:
NOW: list the engine directory and confirm rank0.engine … rank{TP-1}.engine all exist with non-zero size, alongside config.json. A missing or truncated rank file is the usual cause after an interrupted object-store sync.
INVESTIGATE: compare the file count against the TP size in config.json. If they disagree, the artifact was built for a different TP and cannot be served at this one. Verify checksums rather than sizes, a truncated engine sometimes loads and then fails mid-request.
PREVENT: publish engine directories as a single atomic, checksummed artifact; validate rank-file count and digest at startup before binding the serving port.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, repair or re-sync the engine artifact, then restart

patterns.summary: LMDeploy's --tp does not divide the model cleanly, or does not match the TP the weights were converted for. TurboMind bakes the shard layout into the converted weights, so serving TP must equal conversion TP, a mismatch is a hard load failure, not a repartition.
patterns.action:
NOW: set --tp to the value the weights were converted with, or re-convert for the TP you intend to serve. Also confirm num_key_value_heads is divisible by tp, a GQA model with 8 KV heads cannot run tp=16.
INVESTIGATE: read the TP recorded in the converted model's config and compare against the launch flag. Under a scheduler, this produces a crash loop that looks like a resource problem.
PREVENT: record conversion TP in the artifact name or metadata and assert it against the launch flag in the entrypoint.
patterns.resumeFrom: re-convert for the intended TP, or relaunch with the matching --tp

patterns.summary: The NIXL agent handshake between disaggregated workers failed, so no KV transfer can occur. Handshake carries memory-registration metadata, which means this fails at startup or at first transfer, before any request succeeds, and the workers otherwise look healthy.
patterns.action:
NOW: verify both workers can reach each other on the NIXL side channel (the metadata port, not just the HTTP port) and that the RDMA device is visible in both containers (ibv_devinfo). A missing /dev/infiniband bind mount is the most common cause.
INVESTIGATE: confirm both sides run the same NIXL version and the same backend (UCX vs GPUDirect). Registration also needs sufficient locked memory, check ulimit -l inside the container, which defaults far too low in many images.
PREVENT: add a startup handshake self-test so a misconfigured pair fails loudly at deploy instead of on first traffic; template the RDMA device mount and memlock limit rather than setting them per deployment.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, fix RDMA device access / NIXL config, then restart both workers

patterns.summary: Time-to-first-token has crossed into seconds because requests are queueing, not because prefill got slower. TTFT = queue wait + prefill; once the queue is non-trivial the queue term dominates completely, so every optimisation aimed at prefill will produce no measurable improvement.
patterns.action:
NOW: shed load (429 at the gateway) and scale out. Client-side retries against a saturated queue multiply arrival rate and are the fastest way to make this worse.
INVESTIGATE: split TTFT into its two terms before changing anything. Queue depth near zero with high TTFT = genuinely slow prefill (look at --enable-chunked-prefill, prefix-cache hit rate, long inputs). Queue depth high = capacity, and no prefill tuning will help. Check whether KV-cache utilisation is also pinned, which caps admission independently of compute.
PREVENT: alert on queue depth (leading) rather than TTFT (lagging); set an explicit admission bound so overload degrades as fast rejections instead of unbounded latency.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, shed load and scale out; the engine is healthy

requiredEvidence.re: ttft|time to first token|Waiting:|Pending:|#queue-req|GPU KV cache usage

negativeEvidence.re: no free blocks|No available memory for the cache blocks|Cannot allocate (?:KV|kv) cache|KV cache (?:is )?(?:full|exhausted)

patterns.summary: A prefix-cache block hash collision or mismatch was detected. Prefix caching keys reusable KV blocks by content hash, so a collision serves one request's KV state to another: output is fluent and wrong, and it is a CROSS-REQUEST correctness fault, which in a multi-tenant deployment means one tenant's context can influence another's output.
patterns.action:
NOW: disable prefix caching (--no-enable-prefix-caching) until the version is confirmed clean. Treat this as a correctness and isolation incident, not a performance one, fluent wrong output does not show up in any error metric.
INVESTIGATE: check your engine version against known prefix-caching correctness fixes; several have shipped. Determine whether affected requests crossed tenant boundaries, which decides whether this is a customer-notification event.
PREVENT: pin engine versions with a correctness smoke test that asserts identical output for identical input with caching on and off; keep tenants on separate replicas where cross-contamination is unacceptable.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, disable prefix caching and restart; audit affected responses

patterns.summary: TGI's launcher is restarting a model shard in a loop. The router keeps accepting requests while shards flap, so clients see intermittent failures rather than a clean outage, and the launcher's own log shows only the restart, never the cause. Note this is TGI's model sharding, not FSDP's.
patterns.action:
NOW: read the SHARD's stderr, not the launcher's. The launcher reports that a shard died; the shard reports why. Restart the whole container once you have that.
INVESTIGATE: the usual causes are a CUDA OOM inside the shard (lower --max-batch-prefill-tokens), a shard OOM-killed by the host, or an unsupported dtype/quantization for the device. Confirm --num-shard matches the visible GPUs.
PREVENT: capture per-shard logs separately; set the readiness probe on a real generation so a flapping shard fails readiness instead of serving intermittent errors.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, fix the shard-level cause and restart the container

negativeEvidence.re: GPU is lost|GPU has been reset

patterns.summary: ncclUnhandledCudaError, a CUDA call inside NCCL failed. This is almost always a DOWNSTREAM symptom: the CUDA context was already broken (prior Xid, OOM, illegal access) when NCCL touched it.
patterns.action:
NOW: read the log BEFORE this line, the primary fault (Xid/ECC/OOM/assert) precedes it.
INVESTIGATE: dmesg -T | grep -iE "xid|nvrm"; nvidia-smi -q -d ECC; if nothing, run with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to surface the original kernel error.
PREVENT: enable TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING (default in recent torch) so the true error propagates.
ESCALATE: only after the underlying CUDA fault is identified, do not debug NCCL itself for this enum.

patterns.re: ValueError: Target modules? .* not found in the base model|Please check the target modules and try again|peft.*target_modules.*(invalid|not found)
patterns.summary: PEFT/LoRA target_modules mismatch, the configured module names (e.g. q_proj) do not exist in this architecture (different naming: query_key_value, Wqkv, c_attn…).
patterns.action:
NOW: print([n for n,_ in model.named_modules()][:80]) and pick the real attention/MLP projection names.
INVESTIGATE: model family changed? (llama→gpt-neox style names differ); PEFT version's TRANSFORMERS_MODELS_TO_LORA_TARGET_MODULES_MAPPING may already know it: target_modules="all-linear" as a quick fix.
PREVENT: per-architecture adapter configs in your training lib.

patterns.re: Out of memory: Killed process \d+ \((python|torchrun|pt_main_thread)|oom_kill_process.*python|Memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process
patterns.summary: HOST (CPU RAM / cgroup) OOM kill of a training process, the kernel or cgroup killed python. This is NOT GPU memory: dataloader caches, tokenized datasets in RAM, or rank-0 auxiliary services are the usual growth source.
patterns.action:
NOW: identify which pid/rank died (exitcode -9 / signal 9) and its cgroup limit vs peak RSS (memory.peak).
INVESTIGATE: per-worker RSS over time (smem/pidstat); pin_memory + huge prefetch factors; rank0-only services (TB/eval/upload).
PREVENT: cap dataset cache; raise pod limits or move aux services to sidecars; alert at 90% cgroup usage.
ESCALATE: n/a.

patterns.re: Unexpected bus error encountered in worker|Bus error \(core dumped\)|insufficient shared memory
patterns.summary: Shared-memory (/dev/shm) exhaustion killed a DataLoader worker with SIGBUS, classic container default --shm-size=64m.
patterns.action:
NOW: df -h /dev/shm inside the container; relaunch with --shm-size=16g (docker) / emptyDir medium=Memory (k8s).
INVESTIGATE: worker count × batch bytes vs shm size.
PREVENT: set shm explicitly in every training pod template.

negativeEvidence.re: Out of memory: Killed process|oom_kill|Memory cgroup out of memory

patterns.re: Failed to bind NVLink SHARP \(NVLS\) Multicast memory|NVSwitch multicast resources\/slot ids are used|transport\/nvls\.cc[^\n]{0,40}Cuda failure 1 'invalid argument'
patterns.summary: NVLink SHARP (NVLS) multicast setup failed (slot exhaustion or invalid argument).
patterns.action: Disable NVLS with NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0; on NCCL 2.29.x downgrade to 2.28.x. Check Fabric Manager multicast slot usage.

patterns.summary: GPU MMU page fault (Xid 31), often an NVLS/Fabric Manager cascade.
patterns.action: Stop nvidia-fabricmanager, run nvidia-smi --gpu-reset, then restart fabricmanager; reboot if it persists. Never restart Fabric Manager under load.

patterns.summary: NCCL could not read the RoCE GID (zero-GID / macvlan layout).
patterns.action: Set NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX to a valid RoCE v2 entry (show_gids); upgrade to NCCL 2.26.2+ which skips zero-GID entries.

patterns.re: NET\/OFI Unable to register memory.*RC: ?12|Unable to register memory.*RC: ?12
patterns.summary: Insufficient memlock limit for RDMA memory registration. OFI transport cannot pin GPU memory.
patterns.action: Set memlock to unlimited in /etc/security/limits.conf (* soft/hard memlock unlimited); for Docker pass --ulimit memlock=-1:-1; for K8s add IPC_LOCK capability.

patterns.summary: bf16 gradient norm underflow, norms can round to zero in bf16 precision (7 mantissa bits).
patterns.action: Upgrade DeepSpeed to >=0.13.5 which computes norms in fp32; or use fp16; or increase learning rate.

patterns.summary: NaN from gradient buffer reuse race when both overlap_comm and contiguous_gradients are True in DeepSpeed ZeRO-3.
patterns.action: Disable one: set overlap_comm: false or contiguous_gradients: false in DeepSpeed config.

patterns.re: client socket has timed out after \d+s while trying to connect
patterns.summary: NCCL cross-node TCP connection timed out, two nodes cannot establish a bootstrap connection.
patterns.action: Set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME to the correct fabric interface (eth0, ib0); ensure no firewall between nodes on the MASTER_PORT range; verify hostname resolution resolves to routable IPs across all nodes.

patterns.summary: Checkpoint state_dict keys mismatch, model architecture changed between save and load (added/removed layers), preventing direct state_dict load.
patterns.action: Inspect mismatched keys: `ckpt = torch.load("checkpoint.pt"); model_sd = model.state_dict(); print([k for k in ckpt.keys() - model_sd.keys()])`. Use `strict=False` in load_state_dict: `model.load_state_dict(ckpt, strict=False)`. Remove unexpected keys from checkpoint: `for k in list(ckpt.keys()): if k not in model_sd: del ckpt[k]`. Initialize new layers with `model.load_state_dict(ckpt, strict=False)` then fine-tune.

patterns.summary: GPU context lost (Xid 13 / CUDA error 35), driver killed the CUDA context, usually TDR or engine reset.
patterns.action: Check dmesg for preceding Xid events. Reset the GPU: `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i <index>`. Verify no other workload is interfering (watchdog TDR). Reboot if recurrent.

patterns.summary: GPU page retirement limit exceeded, hardware has exhausted remap spare pages; GPU is at EOL.
patterns.action: `nvidia-smi -q -d PAGE_RETIREMENT`. If pending/retired pages > 0 AND `uncorrectable` is > `max_retired_pages_limit`: schedule RMA. The GPU will continue to fail.

patterns.re: context is destroyed|CUDA error 25|cudaErrorContextIsDestroyed|context has been destroyed|error 25[^\n]*context
patterns.summary: CUDA context destroyed (error 25), the CUDA driver primary context was lost mid-operation, usually from a concurrent GPU reset or TDR event.
patterns.action: Check dmesg for Xid events preceding this error. Do NOT reset GPUs during active training. Set `CUDA_VISIBLE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID` for stable context addressing. Reboot the node if recurrent. Disable GSP firmware: `modprobe nvidia NVreg_EnableGpuFirmware=0`.

patterns.summary: PyTorch DDP: NCCL collective found mismatched tensor shapes across ranks. Usually from non-deterministic forward pass or input size variation.
patterns.action: python -c "import torch; torch.distributed.barrier()" 2>&1. Fix: set torch.distributed.nn._DDP_comm_hooks to a correct hook; verify dataloader returns same batch sizes across ranks; pad/collate_fn to uniform shapes.

patterns.re: RuntimeError.*Trying to backward through the graph a second time|double backward.*retain_graph|autograd.*engine.*bad function call
patterns.summary: PyTorch: backward called twice without retain_graph=True. Common in GANs, contrastive learning, or multi-loss scenarios.
patterns.action: Add retain_graph=True to first backward(), or call .detach() to isolate subgraphs; reconstruct loss graph for each backward pass.

patterns.summary: DeepSpeed ZeRO-3: parameter partition size mismatch across ranks. Usually when world_size differs between training and resume.
patterns.action: python -c "import deepspeed; print(deepspeed.__version__)" 2>&1. Fix: ensure --nproc_per_node is consistent across runs; delete zero_to_fp32.json and optimizer state before resume.

patterns.re: from_pretrained.*shape.*mismatch|Some weights of.*were not initialized|size mismatch for.*layer.*weight.*copying
patterns.summary: HF Transformers: model configuration shape does not match pretrained weights. Common with custom vocab_size or num_labels.
patterns.action: python -c "from transformers import AutoConfig; c=AutoConfig.from_pretrained("model_name"); print(c)" 2>&1. Fix: set config.vocab_size = tokenizer.vocab_size in from_pretrained(..., ignore_mismatched_sizes=True).

patterns.summary: JAX: XLA device assignment OOM during compilation. Pre-compilation memory budget exhausted.
patterns.action: XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_memory_limit_mb=40960" python train.py 2>&1. Fix: set XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=.80; increase XLA GPU memory limit.

patterns.summary: Gloo bind failed, port in use, IPv4/IPv6 conflict, or network interface not available.
patterns.action: Set MASTER_PORT to an unused port (check: ss -tlnp). Disable IPv6: export GLOO_IFACE=eth0 or set GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME. Kill leftover processes: fuser -k $MASTER_PORT/tcp.

patterns.summary: NCCL socket bind failed, ports in use, address conflict, or ephemeral port exhaustion.
patterns.action: Kill stale processes: fuser -k 29500-29550/tcp. Set NCCL_SOCKET_NTHREADS=2 to use fewer sockets. Increase ephemeral port range: sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 65535".

patterns.re: (?:block manager|BlockTable|PhysicalTokenBlock).*(?:unable|failed|alloc|error)|Unable to allocate physical block|block manager.*no free blocks|self\.allocator.*no block|ran out of physical blocks
patterns.summary: vLLM block manager exhausted, no free physical blocks for new tokens.
patterns.action: Increase `gpu_memory_utilization`. Reduce `max_num_seqs` or `max_model_len`. Consider `--num-gpu-blocks-override` to increase block count.

patterns.summary: vLLM tokenizer files missing, cannot load tokenizer from HuggingFace Hub or local path.
patterns.action: Verify `--tokenizer` path exists. Run `huggingface-cli login` and `huggingface-cli download <model> --local-dir ./model`. Set `--trust-remote-code` if needed.

patterns.summary: TGI router timed out, max_concurrent_requests exceeded or queue full.
patterns.action: Increase `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` or `MAX_BATCH_PREFILL_TOKENS`. Add more TGI shards. Set `--max-best-of 1` to reduce overhead.

patterns.summary: TensorRT-LLM plugin version mismatch. GPT attention plugin incompatible with runtime.
patterns.action: Rebuild engine with same TensorRT-LLM version as runtime. `pip install tensorrt_llm==<version> --force-reinstall`. Clean build directory: `rm -rf ./engine/*`.

patterns.summary: Triton custom backend crash, backend implementation missing or runtime error.
patterns.action: Verify backend .so exists in `$TRITON_BACKENDS_DIR`. Rebuild backend with matching Triton SDK version. Check `--backend-config`. Inspect Triton logs for dlopen errors.

patterns.summary: Lustre OST target is unavailable or client has been evicted.
patterns.action: lctl ping <ost_name>; lctl dl; lctl recover; check lnet status; dmesg | grep -i "evicted"; restart lnet if needed: lctl network up.

patterns.summary: Lustre connection to OST timed out; reconnect limit reached.
patterns.action: lctl ping <ost_uuid>; lctl dl; lctl recover; check network: lctl list_nids; lctl network up; if LNet is down: modprobe lnet; lctl network configure.

patterns.summary: Lustre MDS (Metadata Server) is unresponsive or in recovery.
patterns.action: lctl ping <mds_uuid>; lfs check servers; lctl dl | grep MDS; on MDS: lctl recover; if stuck: mount -o abort_recovery <mdt_device> <mnt>.

patterns.summary: NFS stale file handle (ESTALE), file was deleted or server replaced.
patterns.action: ls -la <parent_dir>; stat <file>; if server changed: remount: umount -f <mount>; mount -t nfs <server>:<export> <mount>.

patterns.summary: NFS server not responding or NFS timeout (soft mount).
patterns.action: ping -c 5 <server_ip>; nfsstat -s; rpcinfo -p <server>; increase timeo: mount -o remount,timeo=600,retrans=5 <mount>.

patterns.summary: S3 AccessDenied (403) or NoSuchKey (404) on object request.
patterns.action: aws s3 ls s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/ --no-sign-request; aws s3api head-object --bucket <bucket> --key <key>; check IAM policy.

patterns.summary: GPUDirect Storage (GDS) cuFile initialization failure (nvidia-fs).
patterns.action: lsmod | grep nvidia_fs; modprobe nvidia_fs; dmesg | grep -i "nvidia.fs"; check nvidia-fs version: cat /proc/driver/nvidia-fs/version.

patterns.summary: GDS: nvidia-peermem driver not loaded (peer memory access).
patterns.action: lsmod | grep nvidia_peermem; modprobe nvidia_peermem; dmesg | grep -i "peermem"; check kernel module parameters: modinfo nvidia_peermem.

patterns.summary: posix_fallocate/ftruncate failed, disk completely full.
patterns.action: df -h <filesystem>; du -sh <checkpoint_dir>; lsof +L1 (reclaim space held by deleted-but-open files first). Free scratch/logs/core-dumps before touching checkpoints. If checkpoints must move, MOVE the oldest to secondary storage (rsync then verify), deleting every >1G file in a checkpoint dir destroys all recovery points.

patterns.summary: EIO on read/write, failing disk with bad sectors.
patterns.action: smartctl -a /dev/<device> | grep -E "(Reallocated_Sector|Pending_Sector|Uncorrectable)"; badblocks -sv /dev/<device>; dmesg | grep -i "ata.*error"; if >0 reallocated: replace disk.

patterns.summary: Node failed during job execution, hardware or network issue.
patterns.action: Run scontrol show node <nodename>; check slurmd logs; drain node with scontrol update nodename=<n> state=drain.

patterns.summary: Job held, admin hold or unsatisfied dependency.
patterns.action: scontrol release <jobid>; check dependency chain with scontrol show job <jobid> --details.

patterns.summary: Init container config error, env var from Secret or ConfigMap not found.
patterns.action: kubectl describe pod <pod>; verify Secret/ConfigMap exists: kubectl get secret <name>; check namespace.

patterns.summary: Image pull failure, missing image, bad tag, or registry auth error.
patterns.action: kubectl describe pod <pod> to see exact error; fix image tag; create imagePullSecret: kubectl create secret docker-registry.

patterns.summary: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu resources, scheduler cannot fit pod on any node.
patterns.action: kubectl describe pod <pod>; check allocatable GPUs per node; request fewer GPUs or add GPU nodes.

patterns.summary: NVIDIA device plugin down or not ready. GPU resources unavailable.
patterns.action: kubectl logs -n gpu-operator -l app=nvidia-device-plugin; restart daemonset with kubectl rollout restart.

patterns.summary: PVC not found or pending, storage class missing or quota exceeded.
patterns.action: kubectl get pvc <name>; kubectl describe pvc <name>; check StorageClass exists; verify CSI driver.

patterns.re: NET\/IB : Got completion with error 12, opcode 1
patterns.summary: RoCE IB hardware signaled a memory management error.
patterns.action: Check RDMA memory region registration limits.

patterns.re: RCCL WARN xGMI unhandled system error
patterns.summary: Generic system error occurred over XGMI transport.
patterns.action: Enable RCCL_DEBUG=INFO for more granular stack traces.

patterns.summary: Ray placement group failed to acquire resources in time.
patterns.action: Check cluster scaling and resource requests.

patterns.summary: ROCm SMI systemd service failed to start.
patterns.action: Check system logs for driver initialization issues.

patterns.re: RCCL INFO: Fallback to PCIE for node routing
patterns.summary: RCCL routed over PCIe instead of Infinity Fabric.
patterns.action: Check XGMI links to ensure they are active.

patterns.re: Excessive CRC errors on ICI RX .* dropping packets
patterns.summary: Corrupted packets detected at the receiver.
patterns.action: Check physical link integrity and optical alignment.

patterns.re: Failed to read EEPROM on ICI transceiver via I2C
patterns.summary: Management interface to the transceiver failed.
patterns.action: Reseat module or replace if I2C bus is permanently wedged.

patterns.re: Heavy fabric congestion .* backpressure applied to source
patterns.summary: Core switch fabric is overloaded.
patterns.action: Optimize model parallelism to reduce network communication.

patterns.summary: Switch failed to supply data fast enough to the transmitter.
patterns.action: Investigate internal switch fabric congestion.

patterns.re: Host link state \(UP\) mismatches firmware state \(DOWN\)
patterns.summary: Driver software state is out of sync with hardware reality.
patterns.action: Force link state refresh via API.

patterns.re: Timeout broadcasting compilation cache over ICI
patterns.summary: Nodes failed to share compiled executables over the network.
patterns.action: Distribute executables via host filesystem instead of ICI.

patterns.re: Multicast mask contains only self SM
patterns.summary: Multicast mask targets only the calling SM.
patterns.action: Use regular TMA load instead of mcast.

patterns.summary: mbarrier try_wait exceeded timeout.
patterns.action: Ensure all transactions complete in time.

patterns.re: TMA descriptor corrupted during MPI exchange
patterns.summary: TMA descriptor corrupted during MPI exchange.
patterns.action: Use safe byte arrays for descriptor exchange.

patterns.summary: NCCL timed out waiting for SHARP tree initialization.
patterns.action: Check UFM for tree allocation delays and restart job.

patterns.summary: Failed to initialize SHARP communication group.
patterns.action: Verify SHARP daemon connectivity and UFM licenses.

patterns.summary: UFM cannot monitor more SHARP trees due to telemetry limits.
patterns.action: Reduce SHARP telemetry frequency or increase pool size.

patterns.re: MAD drops detected on SHARP QP
patterns.summary: Subnet Manager management packets dropped, affecting SHARP.
patterns.action: Increase SM priority or check for fabric congestion.

patterns.summary: Completion Queue leak in the SHARP user daemon.
patterns.action: Restart sharpd and update SHARP software stack.

patterns.summary: PCIe doorbell drops caused SHARP stalls.
patterns.action: Adjust PCIe relaxed ordering or Max Payload Size.

patterns.summary: PCIe Post Package Repair triggered on HCA memory.
patterns.action: Replace the faulty ConnectX-7 network adapter.

patterns.summary: NCCL timeout out communicating with SHARP daemon.
patterns.action: Check CPU load and sharpd responsiveness on host.

patterns.re: NVLink deadlock detected during SHARP offload
patterns.summary: Deadlock between intra-node NVLink and inter-node SHARP.
patterns.action: Update NVSwitch firmware and use NCCL 2.18+.

patterns.summary: NVSHMEM could not allocate workspace for SHARP.
patterns.action: Increase NVSHMEM heap size via environment variable.

patterns.re: power cap limit reached.*SHARP latency spike
patterns.summary: Power capping induced extreme latency, breaking SHARP timeout.
patterns.action: Ensure stable power delivery or relax NCCL timeouts.

patterns.re: SHARP topology constraints violated by pod placement
patterns.summary: Kubernetes scheduled pods on mismatched IB rails for SHARP.
patterns.action: Ensure proper NUMA and IB rail affinity in pod specs.

patterns.re: Multus IB MAC collision.*SHARP auth fail
patterns.summary: Duplicate IB MACs in K8s Multus broke SHARP routing.
patterns.action: Fix Multus IPAM or MacVLAN configuration.

patterns.summary: DeepSpeed gradients overflowed SHARP FP16 accumulator.
patterns.action: Disable SHARP for FP16 reductions or use FP32.

patterns.summary: Mixture of Experts AllToAll overloaded SHARP routing.
patterns.action: Fallback to standard NCCL for AllToAll operations.

patterns.re: Pipeline parallel deadlock waiting on SHARP
patterns.summary: DeepSpeed pipeline scheduling deadlocked with SHARP tree.
patterns.action: Ensure forward/backward pass symmetry across ranks.

patterns.re: Accelerate hook failed during SHARP sync
patterns.summary: HuggingFace Accelerate gradient hook stalled on SHARP.
patterns.action: Disable find_unused_parameters or check model graph.

patterns.summary: Out of order IB packets broke SHARP state machine.
patterns.action: Disable adaptive routing for SHARP traffic classes.

patterns.re: VL arbitration stall on SHARP queue
patterns.summary: Switch arbitration engine stuck delaying SHARP packets.
patterns.action: Reboot the spine switch experiencing the stall.

patterns.summary: IB SerDes lane margining failed, destabilizing link.
patterns.action: Update switch firmware to improve SerDes tuning.

patterns.summary: Subnet manager sweep paused hardware SHARP processing.
patterns.action: Minimize dynamic node joins/leaves to reduce sweeps.

patterns.summary: High CPU load starved the SHARP daemon of cycles.
patterns.action: Pin sharpd to an isolated CPU core.

patterns.summary: Netfilter conntrack dropped SHARP daemon TCP packets.
patterns.action: Bypass iptables/conntrack for IB IPoIB traffic.

patterns.re: IRQ affinity missing for SHARP completion queue
patterns.summary: IB interrupts not spread across cores, causing SHARP bottleneck.
patterns.action: Run mlnx_tune or set_irq_affinity.

patterns.re: page cache eviction stalled SHARP pinned memory
patterns.summary: Severe memory pressure stalled GPUDirect SHARP mappings.
patterns.action: Clear page cache or reduce host memory usage.

patterns.re: SHARP telemetry buffer overflow on switch
patterns.summary: Switch dropped SHARP performance telemetry data.
patterns.action: Disable unnecessary SHARP telemetry features.

patterns.re: neuronx-cc killed by signal 9.*cache miss count 100.*OOM
patterns.summary: Host OOM during neuronx-cc compilation due to excessive dynamic shape graph tracking.
patterns.action: Reduce dynamic shape variations or increase host RAM and NEURON_CC_FLAGS cache size.

patterns.re: neuronx-cc killed by signal 9.*cache miss count 200.*OOM
patterns.summary: Host OOM during neuronx-cc compilation due to excessive dynamic shape graph tracking.
patterns.action: Reduce dynamic shape variations or increase host RAM and NEURON_CC_FLAGS cache size.

patterns.re: neuronx-cc killed by signal 9.*cache miss count 300.*OOM
