patterns.summary: NCCL watchdog timeout triggered because one node is running slower than others, causing asynchronous execution to drift.
patterns.action: Profile nodes for stragglers. Set TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 (NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING is the deprecated pre-2.2 name).

patterns.summary: FSDP parameter mismatch due to different mixed precision settings across ranks.
patterns.action: Ensure MixedPrecision configuration is identical across all FSDP instances.

patterns.summary: FSDP checkpoint saving hang/crash because one rank ran out of disk space on a shared filesystem.
patterns.action: Clear disk space on shared filesystem or use sharded state dicts to multiple disks.

patterns.summary: Slurm job killed by node health checker (NHC) because GPU power consumption spiked over allowed limit.
patterns.action: Lower power limit via nvidia-smi or adjust batch size to stabilize power draw.

patterns.summary: FSDP mixed precision mismatch during gradient reduction, shapes or types don't align.
patterns.action: Verify forward pass output shapes and activation checkpointing consistency.

patterns.summary: Slurm requeue fails because old NCCL SHM files were not cleaned up from previous crash.
patterns.action: Add an epilogue script to rm /dev/shm/nccl* before job start.

patterns.summary: NCCL deadlock caused by unequal tensor sizes in all_gather during FSDP sharded state dict consolidation.
patterns.action: Ensure all ranks have identical model architectures before saving FULL_STATE_DICT.

patterns.summary: Slurm SRUN environment variable SLURM_STEP_NODELIST parsed incorrectly by PyTorch distributed init.
patterns.action: Manually extract and set MASTER_ADDR from scontrol show hostnames.

patterns.re: NCCL WARN Call to ibv_poll_cq failed with error 12
patterns.summary: InfiniBand RDMA write failure (CQE error) causing NCCL ring break.
patterns.action: Check IB fabric health, possibly isolating faulty switch or HCA.

patterns.summary: FSDP OOM during optim.step() because of AdamW state materialization overlapping with NCCL buffers.
patterns.action: Reduce batch size, use AnyPrecision AdamW, or enable CPU offload for optimizer states.

patterns.summary: NCCL unhandled cuda error because of uncorrectable ECC error on a single GPU.
patterns.action: Drain the node in Slurm and RMA the affected GPU.

patterns.summary: PyTorch FSDP auto-wrap policy mismatch across ranks resulting in uneven parameter partitioning.
patterns.action: Ensure auto_wrap_policy deterministic behavior across ranks.

patterns.summary: NCCL P2P disabled silently because of ACS (Access Control Services) enabled in BIOS.
patterns.action: Disable ACS in the BIOS for the PCIe root ports connected to the GPUs.

patterns.summary: FSDP memory spike during checkpointing because state_dict_type=FULL_STATE_DICT is used on all ranks instead of just rank 0.
patterns.action: Use FULL_STATE_DICT only on rank 0, or switch to SHARDED_STATE_DICT.

patterns.summary: Slurm network fabric plugin (PMIx) version mismatch between controller and compute nodes breaking rank discovery.
patterns.action: Update PMIx uniformly across the Slurm cluster.

patterns.summary: PyTorch FSDP deadlock in forward due to variable sequence lengths leading to unequal number of collectives.
patterns.action: Pad all sequences to the same length or use Join context manager.

patterns.summary: Slurm batch script limits open files (ulimit -n), causing NCCL sockets to fail to open on scale-up.
patterns.action: Add 'ulimit -n 65536' to the Slurm job script.

patterns.summary: NCCL internal error caused by PCIe bus error (AER) during peer-to-peer transfer.
patterns.action: Inspect dmesg for AER logs and reseat/replace the offending GPU.

patterns.summary: PyTorch FSDP sharding_strategy=SHARD_GRAD_OP crashing when a parameter receives no gradient.
patterns.action: Set find_unused_parameters=True or ensure all params participate in the loss.

patterns.summary: NCCL topology XML override file contains invalid node paths, causing fallback to socket and subsequent timeout.
patterns.action: Validate the XML syntax and PCIe addresses in the topology file.

patterns.summary: PyTorch FSDP state dict load failure because of mismatch in process_group sizes after resuming on different Slurm node count.
patterns.action: Reshard the checkpoint offline for the new world size before loading.

patterns.summary: Slurm Epilog script from previous job didn't clean up /dev/shm, causing PyTorch FSDP memory mapping to fail.
patterns.action: Clean up /dev/shm in Slurm prologue/epilogue scripts.

patterns.summary: Slurm PMI2 failing to broadcast MASTER_ADDR properly, causing connection refused in PyTorch init_process_group.
patterns.action: Switch to PMIx or manually populate MASTER_ADDR using hostname of rank 0.

patterns.summary: PFC pause frame storm causing network-wide head-of-line blocking for RoCEv2 traffic.
patterns.action: Identify the misbehaving node generating pause frames. Validate DCQCN/PFC switch configurations to isolate the stormy port.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL WARN Call to .* failed with error .*Timeout

patterns.re: NCCL INFO NET\/IB : GPU Direct RDMA Disabled for HCA
patterns.summary: PCIe Access Control Services (ACS) is enabled, blocking peer-to-peer DMA between GPU and NIC.
patterns.action: Disable PCIe ACS in the BIOS or append pcie_acs_override=downstream to kernel boot parameters.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL WARN.*cannot bind memory for GPU Direct RDMA

patterns.re: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Correctable, type=Physical Layer
patterns.summary: Massive influx of PCIe correctable errors overwhelming the AER handler, often leading to link degradation.
patterns.action: Update motherboard BIOS/BMC firmware. If persistent, replace the riser cable or motherboard.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL INFO.*PCIe bandwidth dropped from Gen4x16 to Gen4x8

patterns.re: ibv_modify_qp.*failed to modify QP to RTR
patterns.summary: InfiniBand port is stuck in INIT state and cannot transition to ARMED/ACTIVE, failing Queue Pair transitions.
patterns.action: Check Subnet Manager connectivity and ensure the node is authorized in the SM partitions.

patterns.summary: System exhausted the maximum number of pinned memory pages allowed for RDMA Memory Registration.
patterns.action: Increase memlock limits in limits.conf and adjust mlx5_core module params if needed.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL WARN NET\/IB : failed to register MR

patterns.summary: System BIOS failed to allocate sufficient PCIe Base Address Register (BAR) space for all GPUs and NICs.
patterns.action: Enable 'Above 4G Decoding' and 'Resizable BAR' in the system BIOS/UEFI.

requiredEvidence.re: dmesg.*not enough MMIO resources for SR-IOV

patterns.re: NCCL WARN .* packet loss detected on RoCE interface
patterns.summary: Switch buffers are overflowing because ECN/PFC is misconfigured or disabled, turning the lossless RoCE fabric into a lossy network.
patterns.action: Configure Priority Flow Control (PFC) properly on the switch and host NICs for the designated QoS traffic class.

patterns.summary: A firmware bug in the NIC is causing the transmit queues to stall silently during heavy NCCL all-reduce operations.
patterns.action: Upgrade or downgrade the NIC firmware using mstflint or OEM tools.

requiredEvidence.re: dmesg.*NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth.*transmit queue .* timed out
NCCL WARN .* Call to .* failed with error .* system error

patterns.summary: IOMMU is actively blocking the peer-to-peer DMA mappings required for GPUDirect RDMA.
patterns.action: Add iommu=pt or intel_iommu=on iommu=pt to the kernel boot command line to allow passthrough.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL WARN.*NET\/IB : GPU Direct RDMA Disabled

patterns.summary: Duplicate MAC addresses exist on the RoCEv2 L2 network, causing ARP flapping and blackholed RDMA traffic.
patterns.action: Identify the cloned VM/container or misconfigured NIC causing the MAC collision and assign a unique MAC.

patterns.summary: DSCP tags set by NCCL are not being correctly mapped to the lossless Traffic Class (TC) by the host NIC or switch.
patterns.action: Configure the tc_to_priority mapping using mlnx_qos to ensure the correct DSCP maps to the lossless priority queue.

patterns.summary: InfiniBand HCA is thermal throttling and dropping the link to prevent hardware damage.
patterns.action: Check server fan speeds, airflow baffles, and ensure the QSFP optics are rated for the temperature range.

patterns.summary: A fatal PCIe Advanced Error Reporting (AER) event occurred, causing the OS to drop the GPU completely off the bus.
patterns.action: Requires a hard reboot. Investigate physical PCIe seating, riser integrity, or faulty GPU.

patterns.re: NCCL WARN.*NET\/IB : Got completion with error 12
patterns.summary: High Forward Error Correction (FEC) uncorrectable errors due to dirty optics or failing fiber cables, causing severe packet loss.
patterns.action: Clean the fiber optic connectors or replace the faulty optical cable/transceiver.

patterns.summary: NCCL net-plugin is linked against a different version of MLNX_OFED than what is running in the kernel, causing dynamic linking errors or kernel panics.
patterns.action: Ensure the user-space libibverbs and kernel OFED drivers are exactly aligned in version.

patterns.re: NCCL INFO .* RoCE .* Retransmission rate .* spike
patterns.summary: Congestion Notification Packets (CNPs) are being blocked by a switch ACL because they lack proper QoS tagging.
patterns.action: Update switch ACLs to explicitly permit CNP frames (UDP port 4791) and ensure they are assigned to the highest priority queue.

patterns.summary: The PCIe link is stuck in a retraining loop due to electrical instability, effectively disabling the GPU or NIC.
patterns.action: Force PCIe Gen3 in BIOS to stabilize the link temporarily; replace hardware for a permanent fix.

patterns.re: NCCL WARN .* Timeout .* waiting for data
patterns.summary: InfiniBand fabric has entered a credit loop deadlock due to incorrect routing tables (e.g., Up/Down routing violated).
patterns.action: Reconfigure OpenSM routing algorithm from min-hop to fat-tree or up-dn to prevent routing loops.

patterns.re: NCCL WARN NET\/IB : remote address changed
patterns.summary: Subnet Manager reallocated LIDs dynamically while NCCL was running, instantly breaking all established Queue Pairs.
patterns.action: Configure OpenSM to use persistent LIDs (lmc_persistent_guid or similar) to prevent LID changes across sweeps.

patterns.summary: An intermediate switch is stripping or flattening VLAN 802.1p priority tags, breaking RoCEv2 QoS mapping.
patterns.action: Configure the switch ports to trunk mode or trust L2/L3 QoS to preserve VLAN PCP tags.

patterns.summary: The HCA does not possess the correct Partition Key (PKey) required to communicate with the target node in the IB fabric.
patterns.action: Add the node's GUID to the correct partition in the Subnet Manager configuration (partitions.conf).

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL WARN.*NET\/IB : Failed to modify QP to RTR

patterns.summary: The QSFP/OSFP transceiver exceeded safe temperatures, causing the NIC firmware to aggressively throttle or shut down the port.
patterns.action: Increase fan curve in BMC, replace the failing optic, or ensure proper datacenter cooling.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL WARN.*NET\/IB : Got completion with error

patterns.summary: IOMMU is enabled in strict mode (no passthrough), which prevents the proprietary nv_peer_mem kernel module from pinning PCI memory.
patterns.action: Set iommu=pt in grub configuration and update-grub.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL WARN.*NET\/IB : GPU Direct RDMA Disabled

patterns.summary: Two physical HCAs or Virtual Functions share the exact same GUID, causing the Subnet Manager to continuously flap or ban the nodes.
patterns.action: Reflash the HCA firmware to regenerate a unique MAC/GUID, or fix the SR-IOV VF configuration script.

patterns.summary: Host is sending RoCEv2 frames at 4096 MTU, but a transit switch is configured for standard 1500 MTU, dropping all payload frames.
patterns.action: Enable Jumbo frames (MTU 9216 or 4096) on all switch ports in the RoCEv2 data path.

patterns.summary: Host exhausted hardware resources (MSI-X vectors or memory) while attempting to instantiate too many SR-IOV Virtual Functions for ConnectX.
patterns.action: Reduce the number of requested VFs (sriov_numvfs) or enable system support for more MSI-X vectors.

patterns.summary: System BMC or PCIe switch firmware initiated an unprompted PCI bus reset while NCCL was actively transferring data.
patterns.action: Update BMC/BIOS firmware or disable aggressive automatic fault-recovery resets in the BIOS.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL WARN.*Call to .* failed with error .* unhandled system error

patterns.summary: Misconfigured BGP/OSPF routes in the spine-leaf fabric created a routing loop for RoCEv2 traffic, causing packets to drop due to TTL expiration.
patterns.action: Audit the routing tables on the switches and fix the routing loop.

patterns.summary: The HCA hardware encountered a Local Catastrophic Error, stalling all RDMA queues permanently until reset.
patterns.action: Reload the mlx5_core driver (modprobe -r mlx5_core && modprobe mlx5_core) or reboot the host.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL WARN.*NET\/IB : Got completion with error

patterns.re: NCCL INFO .* PCI bus .* bandwidth .* extremely low
patterns.summary: Poor signal integrity on the PCIe riser caused the link to auto-negotiate down from x16 width to x4 or x1, crippling GPU/NIC bandwidth.
patterns.action: Reseat the GPU/NIC and the PCIe riser. Replace the riser cable if the issue persists.

patterns.summary: The HCA hardware exhausted its internal Memory Translation Table (MTT) space, preventing any new RDMA memory regions from being registered.
patterns.action: Increase the log_mtts_per_seg or log_num_mtt module parameters for mlx5_core, or use larger page sizes (HugePages) to reduce MTT usage.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL WARN.*NET\/IB : failed to register MR

patterns.re: Unable to attach or mount volumes: unmounted volumes
patterns.summary: CSI driver timeout during volume attachment, stalling pod creation.
patterns.action: Check storage backend load and CSI controller logs; restart CSI controller if deadlocked.

requiredEvidence.re: timeout expired waiting for volumes to attach or mount for pod
rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded

patterns.summary: Container ran out of shared memory (/dev/shm) during multiprocessing dataloading.
patterns.action: Increase container /dev/shm size using emptyDir volume with medium: Memory or --shm-size.

requiredEvidence.re: DataLoader worker \(pid \d+\) is killed by signal: Bus error

patterns.summary: CNI IPAM exhausted pod IPs in the subnet, preventing new pods from starting.
patterns.action: Expand the pod subnet CIDR or clean up stale pods leaking IPs.

requiredEvidence.re: network: failed to allocate for range: no IP addresses available

patterns.summary: Container reached the maximum allowed process IDs limit (pids.max), stalling multiprocessing.
patterns.action: Increase pod PID limits in Kubelet config or optimize multiprocessing pools.

requiredEvidence.re: cgroup: fork rejected by pids controller

patterns.re: Pod ephemeral local storage usage exceeds the total limit
patterns.summary: Pod evicted for exceeding ephemeral local storage limit due to large logs or temp files.
patterns.action: Increase ephemeral-storage requests/limits or write temp data to CSI volumes.

requiredEvidence.re: Evicted.*usage exceeds the total limit of containers ephemeral-storage

patterns.re: 0\/.* nodes are available: .* node\(s\) had volume node affinity conflict
patterns.summary: CSI volume provisioned in a different zone/topology than available GPU nodes.
patterns.action: Enable WaitForFirstConsumer volume binding mode in StorageClass.

patterns.summary: CSI sidecar containers killed by OOM during high volume churn.
patterns.action: Increase memory limits for CSI attacher and provisioner sidecar deployments.

patterns.summary: Process killed by cgroup OOM killer despite host having free memory.
patterns.action: Increase container memory limits or optimize data pipeline memory footprint.

requiredEvidence.re: Memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process

patterns.summary: Container JSON log file filling up node disk due to lack of log rotation.
patterns.action: Configure containerd log-opts max-size and max-file for automatic log rotation.

patterns.re: CUDA out of memory|Out of memory
patterns.summary: Large files written to /tmp tmpfs mount consumed all container RAM, causing OOM.
patterns.action: Remove tmpfs mount for /tmp or restrict its size; use emptyDir disk instead.

patterns.summary: Kubernetes NetworkPolicy blocking ephemeral ports required for MPI/NCCL communication.
patterns.action: Update NetworkPolicy to allow ingress/egress on required ephemeral port ranges.

patterns.summary: Underlying EXT4 filesystem remounted read-only due to IO errors on local CSI volume.
patterns.action: Run fsck on the underlying block device or replace the faulty disk.

patterns.summary: Container hit open files limit (ulimit -n) during massive dataset processing.
patterns.action: Increase soft/hard NOFILE limits in Pod securityContext or Docker daemon.

patterns.re: Volume is already exclusively attached to one node
patterns.summary: Volume failed to detach from previous node due to node crash, blocking re-attach.
patterns.action: Force detach the volume via cloud provider console or wait for node fencing.

patterns.summary: Job attempted to write to a volume mounted as ReadOnlyMany.

patterns.summary: GPU clocks throttled by software due to high HBM or GPU temperatures.
patterns.action: Check node cooling fans, ambient air temperature, and chassis airflow. Clean heat sinks.

patterns.summary: Hardware-enforced thermal slowdown: the GPU crossed its slowdown temperature and cut its own clocks to protect itself. The die is undamaged and the protection is working as designed, which means the fault is real and sits in the cooling path or power delivery, not in the silicon.
patterns.action:
Quantify the throttle before touching anything, the numbers tell you how much throughput is being lost:
  nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE,TEMPERATURE,POWER   # throttle reasons, current vs slowdown temp
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.sm,clocks.max.sm,temperature.gpu,power.draw,power.limit --format=csv
Compare the SM clock against its maximum and the current temperature against the slowdown threshold: a card held above its slowdown temp runs at a fraction of its rated clock, and "SW Power Cap: Active" at the enforced power limit means it is also being held back by the power budget.
Then fix the environment on the affected node: inlet/ambient temperature, blocked or reversed airflow, dust in the heatsink, failed or de-rated fans, hot-aisle placement, and seating of the cooling solution. Re-measure the clock after each change.
Do not replace a GPU that reports zero ECC errors and no Xid, thermal slowdown is the card protecting itself, and the replacement will throttle identically in the same slot.

patterns.summary: PCIe Advanced Error Reporting detected correctable errors (e.g., bad TLP). The hardware recovered each one, so the decisive question is not whether they occurred but whether the link stayed at full width and speed.
patterns.action:
Check the negotiated link first, that is what separates a real fault from background counts:
  nvidia-smi -q | grep -A3 "GPU Link Info"     # Current vs Max
  lspci -vv -s <bdf> | grep -E "LnkCap|LnkSta"  # negotiated width/speed
A link trained BELOW its maximum (for example Gen1 x4 / 2.5GT/s where Gen5 x16 is expected) turns a corrected-error storm into real lost bandwidth, and it explains a host-to-device copy rate far below peer nodes. That is a physical-layer fault: drain the node, reseat the card and its riser/cable, then re-check that the link retrains to full width and speed.
A high correction RATE (thousands per minute) with a full-width link still points at the same physical remedy. Corrected counts alone, at a low rate and full width, are not grounds for replacing hardware, check ECC and temperatures before suspecting the die.

patterns.summary: Structured-output (guided decoding) grammar compilation failed for a request. The request 500s but the engine survives, so this shows up as a partial outage affecting only schema-constrained callers, easy to misread as a client bug.
patterns.action:
NOW: identify the offending schema from the request log; unsupported constructs are usually recursive $ref, unbounded patternProperties, or a regex with lookaround. Simplify or pin the caller to a supported subset.
INVESTIGATE: which backend is active (--guided-decoding-backend); xgrammar and outlines have materially different JSON Schema coverage, so switching backends is a legitimate fix. Grammar compilation is cached per-schema, a single bad schema arriving at high rate also costs latency for everyone.
PREVENT: validate schemas at the gateway against the chosen backend's supported subset; alert on guided-decoding error rate separately from overall 5xx.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, the engine is healthy; fix or reject the offending schema

patterns.re: #queue-req:\s*(?:[5-9]\d{2,}|\d{4,})|The server is not accepting new requests|Scheduler[^\n]{0,50}(?:queue (?:full|overflow)|backpressure)|too many (?:pending|queued) requests
patterns.summary: SGLang's scheduler queue is saturated, hundreds of requests waiting behind the running batch. Every queued request accumulates its full wait in client-visible TTFT, so this is an availability incident presenting as latency. Adding retries at the client makes it strictly worse.
patterns.action:
NOW: shed load at the gateway (reject with 429 rather than queueing) and scale replicas out. Do NOT raise --max-running-requests to absorb it: that trades queueing delay for per-token slowdown across every in-flight request, and usually raises p99 further.
INVESTIGATE: separate arrival-rate growth from service-time growth. Rising #queue-req with stable gen throughput = you are under-provisioned. Rising #queue-req with FALLING gen throughput = something upstream (cache thrash, eager fallback, a straggler GPU) cut capacity, and scaling out will mask a fixable regression.
PREVENT: enforce admission control with an explicit queue bound and a 429 rather than unbounded queueing; alert on #queue-req, which leads TTFT by minutes.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, shed load and scale out; the engine is healthy

patterns.summary: LMDeploy's weight conversion to the TurboMind format failed. This runs before any server exists, and the usual cause is an architecture TurboMind does not implement, its supported set is materially narrower than transformers'. An unsupported architecture is a hard stop, not a tuning problem.
patterns.action:
NOW: check the model architecture against LMDeploy's supported list for your version. If TurboMind does not support it, switch the backend to PyTorch (lmdeploy serve api_server --backend pytorch), which supports a wider set at lower throughput.
INVESTIGATE: the [TM][ERROR] line names the specific weight or layer that could not be mapped, that identifies whether this is a whole-architecture gap or a single unexpected tensor (a merged LoRA, a custom head). Confirm tp matches the head count as well.
PREVENT: validate architecture support in CI before promoting a model; pin the LMDeploy version, since supported architectures change between releases.
patterns.resumeFrom: re-run the conversion after correcting the backend or architecture; source weights are unchanged

patterns.summary: The disaggregated workers disagree about their roles, two producers, two consumers, or mismatched rank counts in kv_transfer_config. Nothing crashes: requests either hang or never route, which reads as a load-balancer problem rather than a config error.
patterns.action:
NOW: print kv_transfer_config from every worker and confirm exactly one kv_producer (prefill) and one kv_consumer (decode) per pair, with kv_rank values that agree with kv_parallel_size.
INVESTIGATE: a templated deployment that renders the same role to every replica is the usual cause. Verify the rendered config in the running container rather than in the chart. Then confirm the router knows which pool is which, correct worker roles with a router pointing at the wrong pool fails identically.
PREVENT: derive roles from the StatefulSet ordinal rather than a shared template value, and assert role uniqueness at startup.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, correct kv_transfer_config roles and restart the affected workers

patterns.summary: The scheduler is preempting and re-running sequences. Every preemption discards computed KV state and re-prefills that sequence later, so the GPU stays fully busy producing tokens it has already produced, utilisation looks perfect while goodput falls. This is the most misleading failure mode in serving.
patterns.action:
NOW: reduce --max-num-seqs so the admitted working set fits in KV cache. Counter-intuitively, admitting FEWER requests raises completed-tokens-per-second here, because the wasted re-prefill work disappears.
INVESTIGATE: correlate preemption count against KV-cache utilisation, preemption starts when utilisation saturates. With swapping enabled (--swap-space > 0) preempted state moves to host RAM instead of being discarded, trading PCIe bandwidth for recompute; measure which is cheaper for your sequence lengths rather than assuming.
PREVENT: monitor GOODPUT (completed tokens/s) alongside raw throughput; alert on preemption rate, which is a direct measure of wasted work and has no other explanation.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, lower admitted concurrency; the engine is healthy

patterns.summary: Chunked prefill is misconfigured, usually max_num_batched_tokens set below max_model_len with chunking disabled, or a chunk size conflicting with another flag. The flags are interdependent and mostly unvalidated, so the failure surfaces either at startup or on the first long request.
patterns.action:
NOW: with chunked prefill ENABLED, max_num_batched_tokens is a per-step budget and may be well below max_model_len (512-2048 is typical). With it DISABLED, max_num_batched_tokens must be at least max_model_len or long requests cannot be served at all. Set them as a consistent pair.
INVESTIGATE: confirm which mode is active from the startup banner rather than from your intended config, defaults have changed across versions and an inherited config may not mean what it did. If long requests specifically fail, this is the disabled-mode case.
PREVENT: set both flags explicitly rather than relying on defaults, and assert the invariant in the launch wrapper; load-test with your longest real request, not an average one.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, set a consistent prefill flag pair and restart

patterns.summary: JAX `host_callback` (or `io_callback`) caused a deadlock between the accelerator and the host CPU. Usually caused by the host callback thread blocking indefinitely or missing synchronization.
patterns.action: Verify the Python function passed to `host_callback` completes in bounded time and does not contain blocking I/O calls that wait on accelerator state. Consider migrating to `jax.experimental.io_callback` if using older APIs.

negativeEvidence.re: GPU is lost|GPU has been reset

patterns.re: peer access (is )?not supported between these two devices|cudaErrorPeerAccessUnsupported
patterns.summary: CUDA P2P/IPC rejected between devices - on multi-node fleets this is almost always a mixed-driver placement (half-upgraded pool), not NVLink hardware.
patterns.action:
NOW: rerun constrained to one driver pool (scheduler label).
INVESTIGATE: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version across the placement; confirm links healthy (nvidia-smi nvlink -s).
PREVENT: gang-schedule on driver-version label; finish rollouts before large jobs.

patterns.re: Remounting filesystem read-only|EXT4-fs error[^\n]{0,80}journal|Aborting journal on device|journal commit I\/O error
patterns.summary: Filesystem forced read-only after a journal abort (underlying block-device error). Writes (checkpoints/logs) fail with EROFS; existing data is intact but the device needs attention.
patterns.action:
NOW: redirect checkpoint output to a healthy volume; do NOT delete anything on the RO mount.
INVESTIGATE: dmesg for the block error beneath the journal abort; NVMe: nvme smart-log (media errors, wear); fsck after drain.
PREVENT: SMART/media-error alerting; RAID or checkpoint replication for critical paths.
ESCALATE: recurring journal aborts on one device -> replace it.

patterns.summary: JAX: pmap/pjit axis size mismatch. Sharded axis size doesn't match device count or mesh specification.
patterns.action: Verify pmap axis_size equals jax.local_device_count(); in pjit ensure mesh axes product equals device count.

patterns.summary: vLLM multimodal processor failed, image/video input could not be parsed or embedded.
patterns.action: Verify input resolution is within model limits. Reduce image size or use `--limit-mm-per-prompt <N>` to cap multimodal tokens.

patterns.summary: Triton CUDA memory pool exhausted, no free GPU memory for request inference.
patterns.action: Reduce `--cuda-memory-pool-bytes`. Set `--cuda-memory-pool-scavenge`. Increase `--model-instances` limits. Consider reducing `max_batch_size` in model config.

patterns.summary: NIC receive ring buffer overflowed dropping packets.
patterns.action: Increase ethtool rx-usecs and ring size parameters.

patterns.re: RCCL WARN: invalid usage of RCCL_IB_DISABLE
patterns.summary: User incorrectly configured RCCL_IB_DISABLE flag.
patterns.action: Set RCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 properly if avoiding RoCE.

patterns.re: OCS dynamic reconfiguration exceeded .* ms timeout
patterns.summary: Dynamic topology adjustment took too long, interrupting traffic.
patterns.action: Disable dynamic OCS or increase timeout thresholds.

patterns.re: Received unexpected packet type \w+ in state \w+
patterns.summary: Protocol violation detected by the network hardware.
patterns.action: Update LibTPU and driver to ensure protocol compatibility.

patterns.re: libtpu: Requested QoS traffic class \d+ rejected by switch
patterns.summary: Network switches do not support the requested priority class.
patterns.action: Update switch firmware or adjust libtpu QoS settings.

patterns.re: Cannot send unaligned tensor over ICI without bounce buffer
patterns.summary: Performance warning/error for misaligned memory.
patterns.action: Ensure tensors are properly padded to match hardware alignment requirements.

patterns.re: mbarrier shared memory layout is deprecated
patterns.summary: Deprecated SMEM layout used for mbarrier.
patterns.action: Update to modern mbarrier SMEM layouts.

patterns.re: Neuron runtime.*mmap failed.*KMD version mismatch.*error code 6
patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to KMD version mismatch.
patterns.action: Check system logs for KMD version mismatch and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.action: Check system logs for cache coherence issue and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to device busy.
patterns.action: Check system logs for device busy and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to page fault in device module.
patterns.action: Check system logs for page fault in device module and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.re: Neuron runtime.*mmap failed.*KMD version mismatch.*error code 56
patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to KMD version mismatch.
patterns.action: Check system logs for KMD version mismatch and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to device busy.
patterns.action: Check system logs for device busy and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to mailbox timeout.
patterns.action: Check system logs for mailbox timeout and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to device busy.
patterns.action: Check system logs for device busy and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.summary: High TCP FIN timeout causing port exhaustion between runs.
patterns.action: Reduce sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout to 15.

patterns.summary: Calico Felix conntrack dropping fast TCP ACKs.
patterns.action: Tune nf_conntrack_tcp_loose sysctl in Calico nodes.

patterns.re: Intel QPI\/UPI interconnect saturated by TCP fallback
patterns.summary: Cross-socket TCP memory copies saturated motherboard interconnects.
patterns.action: Pin processes strictly to local NUMA domains.

patterns.summary: InfiniBand HDR port mlx5_2 rejected packets due to Azure P_Key partition enforcement.
patterns.action: Check Azure metadata service for valid IB P_Key and ensure NCCL_IB_PKEY is correctly exported.

patterns.summary: UFM or Azure Subnet Manager failed to update routes for HDR port mlx5_3.
patterns.action: Contact Azure support to verify UFM routing tables or restart the IB interface.

patterns.summary: InfiniBand HDR link mlx5_4 flapping or transitioned to PORT_DOWN state.
patterns.action: Perform VM redeploy or node replacement via Azure portal to fix faulty optical transceiver.

patterns.summary: InfiniBand HDR link mlx5_7 flapping or transitioned to DOWN state.
patterns.action: Perform VM redeploy or node replacement via Azure portal to fix faulty optical transceiver.

patterns.summary: Service Level misconfigured on mlx5_6 causing congestion control drops.
patterns.action: Export NCCL_IB_SL=1 to match Azure NDv4 QoS traffic class requirements.

patterns.summary: In-network compute (SHARP) failed to allocate resources on partition for mlx5_0.
patterns.action: Disable SHARP via NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0 or check UFM quota.

patterns.summary: Gradient clipping across imbalanced experts caused memory spike.
patterns.action: Use local gradient clipping instead of global.

patterns.summary: Node affinity grouping packed too many heavy experts on one node.
patterns.action: Randomize expert placement.

patterns.summary: Extreme request lengths routed to same expert caused local OOM.
patterns.action: Enable request length balancing.

patterns.summary: Auto-encoder router consumed too much memory in Tutel.
patterns.action: Use standard Top-K router.

patterns.summary: Topology-aware routing grouped too many tokens on one GPU.
patterns.action: Disable topology-aware routing.

patterns.summary: Data parallel MoE replicated experts incorrectly.
patterns.action: Use proper expert parallelism setup.

patterns.summary: Zero-bubble pipeline scheduling accumulated MoE forward activations.
patterns.action: Use 1F1B schedule instead.

patterns.summary: Interleaved 1F1B increases activation memory footprint. (Stage/Variant 9)
patterns.action: Decrease virtual pipeline parallel size. Applied at step 9.

patterns.summary: 1F1B forward pass activation fragmentation. (Stage/Variant 29)
patterns.action: Reduce microbatch size. Applied at step 29.

patterns.summary: Sequence Parallelism all-gather buffers fragmenting PP bubble. (Stage/Variant 49)
patterns.action: Reduce sequence length or increase tensor parallel size. Applied at step 49.

patterns.summary: Last PP stage OOM during pipeline flush gradient accumulation. (Stage/Variant 69)
patterns.action: Use fp8/bf16 optimizer or reduce gradient accumulation steps. Applied at step 69.

patterns.summary: Transformer layer activation recomputation vs PP bubble size mismatch. (Stage/Variant 89)
patterns.action: Use selective activation recomputation. Applied at step 89.

patterns.summary: Thread locks during aggressive cancellation.
patterns.action: Batch cancellation requests asynchronously.

patterns.summary: Constant swapping of KV pages causing stalls.
patterns.action: Increase KV cache size or decrease batch size.

patterns.summary: Custom sorting kernel deadlocked.
patterns.action: Revert to default sorting kernel.

patterns.re: Race condition in spec KV update
patterns.summary: Draft and target updating KV cache concurrently.
patterns.action: Enforce strict synchronization.

patterns.summary: LayerNorm reduction hung across thread blocks.
patterns.action: Verify GPU health.

patterns.summary: INT4/INT8 weight unpacking hung.
patterns.action: Check for invalid quantization parameters.

patterns.summary: Deadlock in ggml_cuda_op_rope during chunked prefill caused by multi-gpu tensor split stall.
patterns.action: Add a pre-synchronization barrier before ncclAllReduce to prevent NCCL communicator deadlocks.

patterns.summary: WekaFS flock interrupted by system call.
patterns.action: Implement retry logic for EINTR.

patterns.summary: WekaFS fcntl wait could not be interrupted.
patterns.action: Use non-blocking fcntl calls (F_SETLK instead of F_SETLKW).

patterns.summary: OpenCV threading deadlocks with multiprocessing forks. (Case 9)
patterns.action: Set cv2.setNumThreads(0) in worker_init_fn.

patterns.summary: HDF5 objects cannot be pickled across workers. (Case 10)
patterns.action: Instantiate HDF5 handles in worker_init_fn.

patterns.summary: OpenCV threading deadlocks with multiprocessing forks. (Case 16)
patterns.action: Set cv2.setNumThreads(0) in worker_init_fn.

patterns.re: DataLoader worker \(pid \d+\) is killed by signal: Killed.*var22
patterns.summary: OS OOM killer terminated worker due to RAM usage. (Case 22)
patterns.action: Reduce num_workers or batch_size.

patterns.re: Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess.*var95
patterns.summary: CUDA context initialized before workers forked. (Case 95)
patterns.action: Set multiprocessing start method to spawn.

patterns.re: DataLoader worker \(pid \d+\) is killed by signal: Bus error.*var98
patterns.summary: Exhausted /dev/shm shared memory limit. (Case 98)
patterns.action: Increase Docker --shm-size.

patterns.summary: Worker process deadlocked or took too long. (Case 104)
patterns.action: Increase DataLoader timeout.

patterns.summary: NCCL IB plugin detected an unaligned Q_Key access during transport initialization.
patterns.action: Ensure uniform NCCL network configurations across all participating nodes.

patterns.summary: Adam denominator became zero because epsilon underflowed in embedding_layer on A10G_24GB (BF16).
patterns.action: Increase Adam epsilon to at least 1e-5 or 1e-4.

patterns.summary: Adam denominator became zero because epsilon underflowed in attention_qkv on A10G_24GB (BF16).
patterns.action: Increase Adam epsilon to at least 1e-5 or 1e-4.

patterns.summary: Adam denominator became zero because epsilon underflowed in attention_proj on A10G_24GB (BF16).
patterns.action: Increase Adam epsilon to at least 1e-5 or 1e-4.

patterns.summary: Adam denominator became zero because epsilon underflowed in mlp_dense_1 on A10G_24GB (BF16).
patterns.action: Increase Adam epsilon to at least 1e-5 or 1e-4.

patterns.summary: Adam denominator became zero because epsilon underflowed in mlp_dense_2 on A10G_24GB (BF16).
patterns.action: Increase Adam epsilon to at least 1e-5 or 1e-4.

patterns.summary: Adam denominator became zero because epsilon underflowed in layer_norm_1 on A10G_24GB (BF16).
patterns.action: Increase Adam epsilon to at least 1e-5 or 1e-4.

patterns.summary: Adam denominator became zero because epsilon underflowed in layer_norm_2 on A10G_24GB (BF16).
patterns.action: Increase Adam epsilon to at least 1e-5 or 1e-4.

patterns.summary: Mellanox command interface timed out.
patterns.action: Reboot node and check NIC firmware version.

patterns.summary: GPU thermal throttled, causing SP ring to lag and timeout.
patterns.action: Improve datacenter cooling or reduce power limit.

patterns.summary: MTU mismatch dropping large NCCL TCP packets.
patterns.action: Ensure MTU is consistent (e.g., 9000) across all nodes.

patterns.summary: AWS EC2 instance network bandwidth limit exceeded.
patterns.action: Upgrade to an instance type with higher network bandwidth.

patterns.summary: GPU memory leak across SP microbatches OOMs NCCL.
patterns.action: Fix backward pass reference cycles in PyTorch.

patterns.summary: NCCL internal integer overflow on large SP group.
patterns.action: Update NCCL to latest version or reduce tensor size.

patterns.summary: The dynamic FP16 loss scaler is halving repeatedly and skipping optimizer steps. Each skipped step is a step of compute that produced no weight update, so the run is burning GPU hours at full cost and making no progress. A few of these at the start of training is normal calibration; a sustained sequence is not.
patterns.action: Count the skipped steps before changing anything, because the answer differs by rate. Occasional overflow early in training is the scaler calibrating and needs nothing. A sustained sequence means FP16 has run out of dynamic range for these gradients: switch mixed precision to BF16, which has the exponent range of FP32 and needs no loss scaling at all. If the hardware cannot do BF16, lower the initial scale and raise the scale window so the scaler stops overshooting, and check for an unclipped gradient explosion upstream.
patterns.resumeFrom: the last checkpoint before the overflow sequence began, since the skipped steps changed no weights

negativeEvidence.re: Current loss scale already at minimum

patterns.summary: The GPU negotiated a PCIe link narrower or slower than the slot supports. Nothing crashes, throughput silently drops, host-to-device copies stall, and the job looks mysteriously slow. A x16 Gen5 link running at x1 Gen1 delivers roughly 1/64th of expected bandwidth.
patterns.action:
NOW: confirm it is not an idle-state reading. PCIe link state downshifts when the GPU is idle. Re-read under load: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=pcie.link.width.current,pcie.link.gen.current --format=csv -l 2 while a transfer runs.
INVESTIGATE: if it stays degraded under load, lspci -vvv -s <bdf> | grep -E "LnkCap|LnkSta" to see negotiated vs capable; check for AER corrected errors (dmesg | grep -i aer), a reseated card, a riser or cable, and BIOS bifurcation settings for the slot.
PREVENT: record link width and gen under load in node acceptance testing, and alert on any GPU whose negotiated width drops below its capability.
ESCALATE: degradation that follows the card into a known-good slot → RMA the card. Degradation that stays with the slot → riser, cable, or mainboard.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint action required; this is a throughput fault, not a crash

patterns.summary: Triton's dynamic batcher held requests longer than max_queue_delay_microseconds and dropped them. The server is saturated: arrival rate exceeds what the model instances can clear, so the queue never drains within the delay budget.
patterns.action:
NOW: decide whether to shed or to scale. Raising max_queue_delay_microseconds only trades drops for latency, it does not add capacity.
INVESTIGATE: check nv_inference_queue_duration_us against nv_inference_compute_infer_duration_us in the metrics endpoint. Queue >> compute means you are instance-starved, not model-slow. Confirm GPU utilisation: if it is below ~80%, add model instances (instance_group count); if it is pinned at 100%, add GPUs or a faster engine.
PREVENT: set max_batch_size and instance_group from a measured load test rather than defaults, and alert on queue duration rather than on drops, drops are the last symptom, not the first.
ESCALATE: sustained saturation at full GPU utilisation → capacity problem; quantize the model or scale horizontally.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint action; this is a serving capacity fault

patterns.re: packet reordering detected|Packets arrived out of sequence
patterns.summary: Traffic spread across multiple NICs arrived out of order. RoCE is highly sensitive to reordering, go-back-N retransmission means a reordered flow collapses throughput rather than degrading gracefully, and can stall the pipeline entirely.
patterns.action:
NOW: disable multi-NIC striping for a single flow, export NCCL_CROSS_NIC=0, and re-measure. If throughput recovers, reordering was the cause.
INVESTIGATE: reordering across NICs usually means ECMP hashing is spreading one QP's packets over multiple paths. Confirm the fabric hashes on the full 5-tuple and that both NICs are in the same layer-2 domain with matching MTU. Check port counters for out-of-sequence on the receiving HCA.
PREVENT: keep a given queue pair pinned to one NIC and one path; use NCCL_IB_HCA to bind ranks to the NIC on their own NUMA node.
ESCALATE: fabric-side ECMP misconfiguration → network team, with the out-of-sequence counters as evidence.

patterns.re: float division by zero[^\n]{0,70}GradScaler|GradScaler\.step\(\)[^\n]{0,70}(unscaled to zero|division by zero)
patterns.summary: The AMP gradient scaler reached a state where every gradient was zero or non-finite, so the scale update divided by zero. The scaler is reporting a numerical collapse upstream, not causing one.
patterns.action:
NOW: do not patch the scaler. Find the step where gradients first became non-finite, log torch.isfinite on the gradient norm each step and locate the first failure.
INVESTIGATE: all-zero gradients usually mean the loss detached from the graph (an in-place op, a .detach(), or a branch that returns a constant). All-Inf usually means an exploding forward pass. Check which by inspecting a single gradient tensor at the failing step.
PREVENT: prefer BF16, which needs no loss scaling at all on Ampere and later. If FP16 is required, add gradient clipping and verify the loss is finite before backward().
ESCALATE: gradients finite but the scaler still collapses → the scaler's growth interval is fighting a genuinely marginal model; switch precision rather than tuning the scaler.

patterns.summary: ZeRO-2 batches gradients into a fixed communication bucket before reduce-scatter. A gradient tensor larger than the bucket, or too many arriving at once, exhausts it and the reduction cannot proceed.
patterns.action:
NOW: raise allreduce_bucket_size (and reduce_bucket_size) in the DeepSpeed config. 2e8 is a common working value; the default is often too small for large embeddings.
INVESTIGATE: find the largest single gradient, max(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()). If one tensor exceeds the bucket, no amount of tuning batch count helps; the bucket must exceed the largest tensor.
PREVENT: size the bucket from the model rather than copying a config from a smaller run. Larger buckets cost memory but reduce the number of collectives, so this is usually a throughput win too.
ESCALATE: bucket large enough and still failing → host memory pressure on the pinned communication buffers; check ulimit -l and available RAM.

patterns.re: Shared memory ring buffer overwrite|RCLError[^\n]{0,90}(ring buffer|Shared memory)
patterns.summary: A ROS 2 publisher overwrote shared-memory ring buffer entries a subscriber had not yet consumed. The consumer is slower than the producer, so frames are being lost, and with zero-copy transport the subscriber can read a partially overwritten message rather than simply missing one.
patterns.action:
NOW: increase the QoS depth (history/depth) on the topic, or slow the publisher. If the consumer is a GPU inference node, the fix is usually on the consumer side.
INVESTIGATE: measure the actual consumer latency per message against the publish period. A GPU node that occasionally exceeds the period only overflows intermittently, which is why this looks random. Check for a synchronous CUDA call in the callback.
PREVENT: use a RELIABLE QoS with adequate depth for data that must not be lost, or BEST_EFFORT with a small depth when dropping is acceptable, the failure mode here is a topic configured for neither.
ESCALATE: consumer genuinely cannot keep up → decouple with a queue and drop deliberately at a known point, rather than letting the transport corrupt frames.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint action; this is a live pipeline fault

patterns.summary: The actor blocked waiting for a ZeRO-3 parameter gather owned by the critic. Two ZeRO-3 models in one process share a parameter coordinator; if their forward passes interleave, each can wait on a collective the other has not entered.
patterns.action:
NOW: serialise the two models' forward passes, never run actor and critic concurrently in the same process under ZeRO-3.
INVESTIGATE: py-spy dump on the hung rank shows which gather each model is inside. If both are in a parameter gather, this is the deadlock; if only one is, the other rank has already died and this is collateral.
PREVENT: put actor and critic in separate DeepSpeed engines with separate process groups, or drop the critic to ZeRO-2 (it is far smaller than the actor, so the memory saving from ZeRO-3 on it is minimal and not worth this class of bug).
ESCALATE: keep ZeRO-3 on both only with an explicit ordering barrier between their forward passes, and verify with a short run before committing a long one.

patterns.summary: The AWQ GEMM kernel was launched with a grid or block configuration the device rejects. AWQ kernels assume shapes divisible by their tile size; an unusual hidden dimension or a batch of 1 can produce a degenerate launch.
patterns.action:
NOW: check the shapes in the message against the kernel's tile constraints. AWQ typically requires the K and N dimensions to be multiples of the group size (commonly 128).
INVESTIGATE: M=1 (single-token decode) hits a different kernel path than batched prefill and is where this usually appears. Confirm whether it reproduces only at batch size 1.
PREVENT: quantize with a group_size that divides the model's hidden dimensions, and validate one forward pass at both M=1 and M>1 before deploying.
ESCALATE: shapes are valid and it still fails → an autoawq build compiled for a different architecture; reinstall matched to the GPU and CUDA version.

patterns.summary: Milvus could not load a vector index segment into GPU memory. Segments are loaded whole, so a single oversized segment fails even when total free VRAM across the collection looks sufficient.
patterns.action:
NOW: check the segment size against free VRAM on the query node. The limit is per-segment, not aggregate.
INVESTIGATE: segment size is governed by the collection's segment.maxSize; a collection built with large segments cannot be loaded on a smaller GPU. Confirm how many segments the query node is holding, they accumulate as collections are loaded.
PREVENT: tune segment.maxSize to the query node's VRAM at collection creation, and release collections that are not being queried rather than leaving everything resident.
ESCALATE: add query nodes so segments distribute, or move the index type to one with a smaller GPU footprint.

patterns.summary: The Neuron runtime's DMA ring buffer filled, transfers were queued faster than the device drained them. The accelerator is keeping up with compute but not with the data being pushed at it.
patterns.action:
NOW: reduce in-flight transfers, lower the dataloader prefetch depth and the number of concurrent inference requests per NeuronCore.
INVESTIGATE: neuron-monitor shows DMA queue depth and utilisation. A saturated DMA channel with low NeuronCore utilisation means the bottleneck is transfer, not compute, batching larger and less often is the fix, not smaller and more often.
PREVENT: size prefetch to the measured device drain rate rather than to host memory availability, and keep tensors in the device-preferred layout so the runtime is not doing implicit conversions on the DMA path.
ESCALATE: saturated at minimal concurrency → the model's activation traffic exceeds the interconnect; reshard so fewer tensors cross the device boundary.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint action; reduce concurrency and retry

patterns.summary: Xid 45 records driver cleanup after a CUDA context was terminated. It is usually evidence of an earlier application exit, GPU reset, or administrator action, not the initiating hardware fault.
patterns.action:
NOW: inspect the driver and process logs immediately before Xid 45. The cause is the event that forced cleanup, not the cleanup record itself.
INVESTIGATE: correlate the timestamp with OOM kills, SIGKILL, GPU reset commands, container termination, and earlier Xid codes. An earlier non-cleanup Xid takes precedence.
PREVENT: preserve at least several minutes of kernel and scheduler logs around every Xid so cleanup records retain their causal context.
ESCALATE: if Xid 45 repeats without a visible process exit or reset, collect nvidia-bug-report.sh output before reboot and open a driver support case.
patterns.resumeFrom: latest checkpoint after the initiating event is identified

patterns.summary: InfiniBand initialization failed for NCCL during Initialization.
patterns.action: Check IB setup, or fallback to sockets using NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1. (Observed in Barrier).

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Expected to mark a variable ready only once.* during Gather.*
patterns.summary: Multiple forward passes or in-place modifications broke the DDP graph during Forward pass.
patterns.action: Avoid multiple forward passes on the same DDP instance without backward, or avoid in-place ops on parameters. (Observed in Gather).

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Expected to have finished reduction in the prior iteration before starting a new one.* during Broadcast.*
patterns.summary: A parameter was not used in the forward pass, breaking DDP reduction during Backward pass.
patterns.action: Set find_unused_parameters=True or ensure all parameters are used in forward. (Observed in Broadcast).

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Module topology mismatch across ranks.* during Barrier.*
patterns.summary: Different ranks have instantiated models with different architectures during Checkpoint save.
patterns.action: Ensure random seeds and conditional model initializations are deterministic across ranks. (Observed in Barrier).

patterns.re: AssertionError: ZeRO stage .* during Gather.* requires .* during Gather.*
patterns.summary: Invalid DeepSpeed ZeRO configuration during Initialization.
patterns.action: Correct the DeepSpeed configuration file for the selected ZeRO stage. (Observed in Gather).

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Engine build failed: Exceeded maximum allowed plugins in graph
patterns.summary: Too many custom plugins caused the TensorRT graph compilation to fail.
patterns.action: Disable unnecessary plugins like fused_mlp if not strictly required.

patterns.action: Scale cluster.

patterns.re: NaNs detected in packed QKV backward pass
patterns.summary: Packed QKV tensor layout caused gradient accumulation issues.
patterns.action: Check tensor strides and contiguous memory layout.

patterns.summary: NVLink topology prevented opening a P2P connection.
patterns.action: Check nvidia-smi topo -m for NVLink status.

patterns.re: Deadlock between TP communication and PP communication
patterns.summary: Circular dependency between Tensor and Pipeline parallelism comms.
patterns.action: Check schedule overlap and stream assignments.

patterns.summary: OOM while accumulating gradients before stepping.
patterns.action: Check for memory leaks in the training loop before loss.backward().

patterns.re: NaN when training t5-large with bf16
patterns.summary: Training T5-large with BF16 on multiple GPUs leads to NaN loss. Despite BF16's large dynamic range, the low precision (7 mantissa bits) causes severe rounding errors and underflow-like vanishing updates during gradient synchronization across multiple devices.
patterns.action: Ensure gradient clipping is enabled (e.g., max_grad_norm=1.0) and disable loss scaling if enabled. If NaNs persist, selectively upcast the cross-attention layer or RMSNorm to FP32.

patterns.summary: Hangs or crashes due to incompatible NCCL operations or process group modifications occurring while a CUDA stream is in capture mode.
patterns.action: Ensure distributed communication operations are fully synchronized before graph capture begins and avoid eager-mode NCCL calls during capture.

patterns.re: High I\/O wait during optimizer step with ZeRO-Infinity
patterns.summary: When using ZeRO-Infinity to offload to NVMe, standard file I/O over PCIe bottlenecks on drive write speeds and PCIe Gen3 limits, rather than utilizing the full bandwidth of the PCIe bus, resulting in massive performance drops during optimizer updates.
patterns.action: Upgrade to high-bandwidth PCIe Gen4/Gen5 NVMe drives configured in RAID 0. Enable GPUDirect Storage (GDS) if available, and ensure `nvme_path` points to the striped NVMe array to parallelize I/O across multiple PCIe lanes.

requiredEvidence.re: iostat showing 100% utilization on NVMe drives
DeepSpeed config using ZeRO-Infinity with offload_optimizer to nvme

patterns.re: NCCL WARN Fallback to socket transport
patterns.summary: Improper GPU index remapping (often via container orchestration or distributed frameworks like Ray using CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES) causes NCCL to misidentify the hardware topology on H100 NVSwitch systems, preventing NVLink establishment and falling back to slow socket transport.
patterns.action: Remove restrictive CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES remapping. Rely on cgroups for GPU isolation if possible, and verify correct topology discovery and NVLink utilization using NCCL_DEBUG=INFO.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO logs showing unexpected socket fallback instead of NVLink
Heavy remapping or masking via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES

patterns.summary: Setting the JAX compilation cache directory to a GCS bucket with incorrect permissions or high latency causes the compiler to hang indefinitely while attempting to read/write cache entries during JIT compilation.
patterns.action: Point the compilation cache to a fast local NVMe drive or ensure correct IAM permissions for the GCS bucket.

patterns.re: NCCL WARN Call to munmap failed
patterns.summary: Systemd automatically cleans up IPC shared memory segments associated with a user when they log out, ripping the memory out from under a running background NCCL process and causing an error.
patterns.action: Set 'RemoveIPC=no' in '/etc/systemd/logind.conf' and restart systemd-logind.

patterns.re: ncclUnhandledCudaError: Call to CUDA function failed|Socket Timeout
patterns.summary: When using Slurm with PMIx to launch distributed PyTorch jobs, strict process binding managed by the PMIx layer can restrict NCCL's background helper threads (used for network communication). This starvation prevents NCCL from completing collective operations within the default timeout window.
patterns.action: Disable strict MPI binding by passing `--bind-to none` to `srun` or setting `export OMPI_MCA_hwloc_base_binding_policy=none`. Additionally, ensure `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` is used to verify thread placement.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL backend is used for distributed training

patterns.re: ValueError: You are trying to save a non contiguous tensor
patterns.summary: During the precision conversion and saving of the model weights prior to engine building, slicing or reshaping specific layers results in non-contiguous memory allocations in PyTorch. Safetensors throws a ValueError when attempting to serialize.
patterns.action: Inject .contiguous() calls to the tensor operations in the conversion script before they are saved to the checkpoint dictionary.

patterns.re: KV cache ~7x memory overestimation for hybrid Mamba\/attention models
patterns.summary: In vLLM 0.8.x, the KV cache profiler treats hybrid models (like Qwen3.5) with O(1) Mamba layers as if all layers require O(n) KV blocks. This inflates reported capacity and overallocates memory, leading to OOM.
patterns.action: Downgrade vLLM to <0.8.0 or artificially lower `--max-model-len` until the KV cache allocation logic is patched to account for non-attention layers.

patterns.summary: MIG SM context switch failed to clear registers.
patterns.action: Isolate node, block tenant, capture nvidia-bug-report, review dmesg and audit logs.

patterns.action: Isolate node, block tenant, capture nvidia-bug-report, review dmesg and audit logs.

patterns.action: Isolate node, block tenant, capture nvidia-bug-report, review dmesg and audit logs.

patterns.action: Isolate node, block tenant, capture nvidia-bug-report, review dmesg and audit logs.

patterns.action: Isolate node, block tenant, capture nvidia-bug-report, review dmesg and audit logs.

patterns.summary: WekaFS experiencing high UDP packet drops due to network congestion, severely degrading read performance.
patterns.action: Tune network QoS, enable PFC/ECN on switches if using RoCEv2, and verify network topology oversubscription.

patterns.summary: BeeGFS client session ticket expired during a very long training epoch without I/O on a specific file handle.
patterns.action: Increase the BeeGFS session ticket timeout or ensure periodic touch/stat operations on open files.

patterns.re: WekaIO.*unaligned read fallback to buffered I\/O
patterns.summary: DataLoader requested O_DIRECT reads with unaligned buffer offsets, forcing WekaFS to fallback to slow buffered I/O.
patterns.action: Ensure DataLoader read buffers are aligned to 4KB/logical block size boundaries when using O_DIRECT.

patterns.summary: XLA SPMD partitioner OOMs during ZeRO-3 parameter sharding due to redundant rematerialization.
patterns.action: Adjust sharding annotations or disable redundant rematerialization in XLA SPMD.

patterns.summary: XLA compiler out-of-memory when aggressively fusing element-wise operations with broadcasted tensors.
patterns.action: Disable aggressive fusion or reduce the size of the broadcasted tensors.

patterns.summary: TorchDynamo unsupported Python feature yield causing silent fallback to eager mode and degrading performance.
patterns.action: Remove the yield statement and refactor the code to avoid generators in compiled regions.

patterns.summary: Triton failing to allocate shared memory when num_stages exceeds hardware limits, silently falling back to num_stages=2.
patterns.action: Reduce num_stages or optimize shared memory usage in the kernel.

patterns.summary: torch.compile failing to capture mutations on custom nn.Module attributes.
patterns.action: Avoid mutating custom attributes or use PyTorch's native state management.

patterns.summary: XLA compiler failing to optimize scatter-gather patterns, falling back to slow scalar loops.
patterns.action: Rewrite scatter-gather patterns using standard tensor operations or optimize them manually.

patterns.summary: Hardware offloading (SHARP) disabled due to NVSwitch parity mismatch.
patterns.action: Disable SHARP for job, restart from checkpoint.

patterns.summary: Infinity Fabric CRC error storm saturating PCIe AER logs.
patterns.action: Monitor CRC rates, replace cables if persistent.

patterns.summary: ROCm firmware crash due to unhandled IF telemetry spike.
patterns.action: Update ROCm SMI tooling and driver.

patterns.re: DRF weight calculation error: NaN or Infinity
patterns.summary: Dominant Resource Fairness (DRF) plugin encounters floating-point precision loss on heterogenous GPU nodes, halting the allocation cycle.
patterns.action: Update Volcano to a version patching the DRF math overflow or switch to proportion plugin.

requiredEvidence.re: panic: floating point exception in dominant resource fairness

patterns.re: Eviction storm detected in overcommitted queue .*
patterns.summary: The overcommit plugin triggers cascading evictions across nodes when ephemeral storage spikes during distributed checkpoints.
patterns.action: Disable overcommit for ephemeral storage or increase node disk sizes.

patterns.type: PMI2 Job Step ID KVS Overwrite
patterns.summary: Concurrent srun executions within the same batch allocation collide on PMI2 step IDs, causing KVS keys to overwrite each other.
patterns.action: Ensure sequential srun execution or use distinct MPI namespaces.

patterns.summary: FSDP mixed precision mismatch where parameters were cast but buffers were not.
patterns.action: Ensure buffer_dtype is explicitly set to match param_dtype in MixedPrecision policy.

patterns.re: RuntimeError: gradient computation.*modified by an inplace operation
patterns.summary: Inplace modification during FSDP activation checkpoint recomputation.
patterns.action: Replace inplace operations (e.g., ReLU(inplace=True)) with out-of-place equivalents in checkpointed layers.

patterns.summary: Gradient accumulation steps dynamically changed, causing ZeRO-3 reduction sync mismatch.
patterns.action: Keep gradient_accumulation_steps constant or manually trigger gradient reductions.

patterns.re: RuntimeError: amax history is stale or uninitialized
patterns.summary: FP8 amax history buffer was not updated, leading to division by zero scaling.
patterns.action: Ensure the forward pass context properly invokes the amax update callback.

patterns.summary: WekaFS RDMA Memory Region exhaustion during heavy collective checkpointing across GPUs.
patterns.action: Increase MLNX_OFED memory registration limits (log_num_mtt) or switch to NVMe-oF.

patterns.re: Lustre.*MDS in recovery|waiting for MDS recovery
patterns.summary: Lustre MDS entered recovery mode, causing all checkpointing operations to hang.
patterns.action: Wait for MDS recovery to complete or check MDS hardware health.

patterns.summary: TPU GRPC connection timed out, likely due to preemption or network isolation on GCP.

patterns.action: Install rdma-core or libibverbs-dev package on the affected node. Check LD_LIBRARY_PATH if it's installed in a non-standard prefix.

patterns.action: Isolate node and check IB fabric counters for symbol errors.

patterns.re: NVLink error .* bridge failure .* link 4 .* CRC
patterns.summary: Obscure NVSwitch bridging failure causing intermittent packet loss on inter-GPU transfers (Case 28).
patterns.action: Check topology XML for suboptimal NIC-to-GPU affinity.

patterns.re: NCCL WARN NVSwitch bridging timeout .* rank \d+
patterns.summary: Advanced NCCL topology timeout in multi-rail environment (Case 48). Suspected IB interface instability or CPU bottleneck during Ring/Tree synchronization.
patterns.action: Drain node, reset GPUs via nvidia-smi, and test IB bandwidth.

patterns.summary: Slurm step memory cgroup limit hit during NCCL all-gather in FSDP due to memory spike.
patterns.action: Enable FSDP CPU offload or limit the sharding strategy memory overhead.

patterns.summary: FSDP use_orig_params=True crashing during gradient clipping due to uninitialized grads on one rank.
patterns.action: Check if a specific parameter didn't receive gradients. Set model.zero_grad(set_to_none=False).

patterns.summary: NCCL hangs during broadcast because the root rank crashed silently with a segfault.
patterns.action: Debug root rank for out-of-bounds memory access. Add fault tolerance to restart.

patterns.summary: NCCL Tree topology generation failed, falling back to Ring and causing extreme slowdown leading to watchdog timeout.
patterns.action: Check NCCL topology XML, update NCCL version, or explicitly set NCCL_ALGO=Tree.

patterns.summary: Slurm cgroup v2 memory max constraint killing rank 0 during PyTorch dataset preprocessing because rank 0 does all the work.
patterns.action: Distribute data preprocessing across all ranks or do it offline.

patterns.summary: NCCL hang due to mismatched NCCL versions between PyTorch wheel and system module loaded by Slurm.
patterns.action: Unset LD_LIBRARY_PATH for NCCL or build PyTorch from source against the system NCCL.

patterns.summary: Slurm killing job due to time limit (TimeLimit), but PyTorch hangs during cleanup because of pending NCCL ops.
patterns.action: Trap SIGTERM in Python, abort pending NCCL communicators gracefully, and save checkpoint.

patterns.re: NCCL INFO NET\/RoCE .* Retransmission rate > .* threshold
patterns.summary: DCQCN is not generating Congestion Notification Packets (CNPs) despite ECN marks, leading to severe packet drops and retransmissions.
patterns.action: Verify Mellanox OFED RoCE QoS configurations (mlnx_qos) and ensure Trust State is set to DSCP.

patterns.summary: The local HCA MTU is smaller than the fabric/SM MTU, causing queue pair creation failures or IP fragmentation.
patterns.action: Align the HCA port MTU and the OpenSM partition MTU configurations.

patterns.re: NCCL INFO .* Inter-node bandwidth .* 1\/N of expected
patterns.summary: Hash polarization in the spine-leaf fabric is mapping multiple ECMP paths to the same spine link, causing asymmetric congestion.
patterns.action: Change the ECMP hash seed on the leaf switches or enable dynamic load balancing (DLB).

patterns.re: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Uncorrected \(Non-Fatal\), type=Transaction Layer
patterns.summary: Max Payload Size (MPS) mismatch between the GPU, PCIe switch, and NIC causing Malformed TLP errors and DMA failures.
patterns.action: Run setpci to align the MPS across the entire PCIe tree to the lowest common denominator (usually 256 or 512 bytes).

patterns.summary: Node conntrack table exhausted by excessive connections, dropping CNI traffic.
patterns.action: Increase net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max or disable conntrack for pod subnets.

patterns.summary: NFS CSI mount invalidated by server-side file deletion or server restart.
patterns.action: Restart pods accessing the mount or force unmount/remount the NFS share.

patterns.summary: Node reached max attachable CSI volumes limit (e.g., AWS EBS limit of 39).
patterns.action: Reduce number of volumes per pod, use larger volumes, or switch to EFS/FSx.

patterns.summary: BuildKit/buildx cache filling up worker node disk space, preventing new images from pulling.
patterns.action: Run docker builder prune or configure buildkit GC policies.

patterns.re: Nitro Enclave attestation failed.*Out of memory|nsm-cli.*Enclave.*OOM
patterns.summary: AWS Nitro Enclave memory limit reached causing attestation failure during federated learning weight aggregation.
patterns.action: Increase the memory allocated to the Nitro Enclave in the enclave allocator configuration.

patterns.summary: GCP A3 supercomputer cross-rail topology violation leading to NCCL fallback and severe throughput degradation.
patterns.action: Ensure strict node allocation policies in GKE/Slurm to align with A3 leaf switch topology.

requiredEvidence.re: NCCL INFO.*falling back to shared memory\/TCP

patterns.re: VPC peering egress bandwidth cap reached
patterns.summary: GCP Egress bandwidth cap hit across VPC peering during global NCCL AllGather operations.
patterns.action: Keep all training nodes within a single VPC subnet to avoid peering throughput limits.

patterns.summary: GCP Preemptible VM shutdown script timed out, failing to gracefully unregister from the Ray head node.
patterns.action: Optimize shutdown scripts to exit quickly and configure Ray node timeouts to aggressively prune dead nodes.
