patterns.summary: Silent Straggler Detected - Collectives are taking >1000ms without a hard crash, indicating severe degradation.
patterns.action: Map stragglers to PCIe bandwidth degradation, thermal throttling, or ECC page retirement storms. Isolate the affected node.

patterns.summary:
Every rank is alive and stopped at the SAME point. Nothing crashed.

The heartbeat is the evidence, and it says two things at once: the processes are still running, so
this is not a crash, an OOM kill or a dead GPU; and they are all parked at the same phase, so they
all entered the same collective and none of them returned from it.

That symmetry is the useful part. If one rank were the culprit, the others would be waiting inside
the collective while it sat somewhere else entirely, and the phases would disagree. Matching
phases across every rank points at the collective itself: the transport, the rendezvous, or a call
that some ranks make with arguments the others do not match.

What this does not establish. It does not say WHICH collective, or why it never completed. The
heartbeat records the phase your code labelled, not the NCCL operation underneath it. The two
checks below name it, and they are worth running before changing any configuration, because the
three usual causes need different fixes.
patterns.action:
Get the stack of EVERY rank, not just one. The comparison is the whole diagnosis.

1. Dump all of them while it is still hung:
     for pid in $(pgrep -f your_train_script.py); do echo "== $pid"; py-spy dump --pid $pid; done
   Read them side by side:
     - every rank inside the same c10d/NCCL call  -> the collective never completed; go to step 2
     - one rank somewhere else (dataloader, file read, a branch)  -> that rank is the culprit and
       the others are merely blocked behind it; fix that rank
     - ranks in DIFFERENT collectives  -> a collective-order mismatch, which is step 3

2. Make the next occurrence provable rather than inferred:
     export TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE=2000
     export TORCH_NCCL_DUMP_ON_TIMEOUT=1
   On the next hang each rank writes a trace; analyse with
   `python -m torch.distributed.flight_recorder.fr_trace -j <dump_dir>`, which names the collective
   and the rank that diverged.

3. Check for rank-dependent control flow. NCCL matches collectives by CALL ORDER, not by name, so
   any conditional that skips or reorders a collective on some ranks hangs the job with no error.
   A dataloader that runs dry on one rank does the same thing.

4. If the stacks show every rank in the first collective of the run, suspect transport rather than
   your code: confirm every rank resolved the same interface, and that the chosen transport can
   actually carry traffic between these hosts.
patterns.resumeFrom: resume-training once the stalling collective is identified

patterns.summary:
The checkpoint is intact. It was written under a different parallel topology.

A state_dict size mismatch whose two shapes are an exact multiple of each other is the
signature of a resharding problem, not a corrupt file. A tensor shape of [4096, 8192] in
the checkpoint against [2048, 8192] in the model is one rank's shard of a tensor that was
split eight ways being loaded into a model expecting it split four ways.

This is why the file loads fine on the original topology and fails on the new one, and it
is why deleting the checkpoint and falling back to an older one does not help: every
checkpoint in that run has the same shape.

What this does not establish. It does not say which topology is correct for your job,
only that the two disagree. Resuming at the original degree and resharding deliberately
is almost always faster than trying to make the new degree read the old shards.
patterns.action:
Resume at the ORIGINAL parallel degree, or reshard the checkpoint deliberately.

1. Read the topology the checkpoint was written with. Most launchers record it, and the
   log line above often states it outright ("saved with TP=8 sharding").

2. Fastest path: relaunch with the original degree. For Megatron-style launchers that is
   --tensor-model-parallel-size and --pipeline-model-parallel-size; confirm both match
   what the checkpoint was saved with, not just the world size.

3. If you must change the degree, reshard as an explicit step rather than hoping the
   loader copes. Megatron ships tools/checkpoint/convert.py for exactly this; DeepSpeed
   users want zero_to_fp32.py followed by a re-partition at the new degree.

4. Verify by shape, not by the absence of an error: load the resharded checkpoint and
   assert one known tensor has the shape the new model expects before starting a long run.

5. To prevent it recurring, record the parallel degrees in the checkpoint directory name
   or its metadata, and fail fast at launch when they disagree with the current job.
patterns.resumeFrom: the same checkpoint, relaunched at the parallel degree it was saved with

patterns.summary: SGLang's radix (prefix) cache is evicting as fast as it fills. Token usage pinned above 0.95 with a near-zero cache hit rate means every request re-computes its prefix: you are paying prefill cost on traffic that should have been a cache hit, and throughput collapses well before any error appears.
patterns.action:
NOW: lower --max-running-requests so the pool is not saturated, giving the radix tree room to retain prefixes. Nothing is broken, this is a silent throughput failure, so there is no crash to wait for.
INVESTIGATE: compare cache hit rate against your traffic's real prefix sharing. If requests genuinely share no prefix (unique system prompts per tenant), the radix cache cannot help and the fix is capacity, not tuning. If they DO share and hit rate is still zero, check that the shared prefix is byte-identical, a per-request timestamp in the system prompt defeats prefix caching entirely and is the single most common cause.
PREVENT: hoist volatile fields (timestamps, request ids, user names) OUT of the system prompt and into the user turn; alert on cache hit rate, not just latency.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, the server is up; retune concurrency or fix prompt prefix stability

patterns.summary: TensorRT-LLM KV-cache block reuse is misconfigured or silently inactive. Block reuse requires paged KV cache AND in-flight batching, both enabled at BUILD time, if either is off, reuse is ignored without an error and you pay full prefill on every request while believing prefix caching is on.
patterns.action:
NOW: verify the engine was built with --paged_kv_cache enable and in-flight batching, then set enableBlockReuse in the runtime config. If the build lacks either, the runtime flag does nothing and a rebuild is required.
INVESTIGATE: measure it rather than trusting the flag, send the same long prefix twice and compare TTFT. No improvement means reuse is inactive whatever the config says. Check the engine's config.json for the build-time settings.
PREVENT: assert on measured prefix-cache benefit in a deploy smoke test; a config flag that is silently ignored is otherwise invisible until someone audits cost.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, fix the runtime config, or rebuild with paged KV + in-flight batching

patterns.summary: The tokenizer does not match the served weights. Vocabulary or special-token drift produces syntactically valid but semantically wrong output, the server is healthy, latency is normal, and quality has silently collapsed. No error rate reflects it.
patterns.action:
NOW: serve the tokenizer from the SAME artifact as the weights (--tokenizer pointing at the model directory, not at a hub id that may have moved). If vocab sizes disagree numerically, the pairing is wrong and no flag fixes it.
INVESTIGATE: compare tokenizer.json / added_tokens and the chat template against the checkpoint that produced the weights. A fine-tune that added special tokens without resizing embeddings, or a base-model tokenizer paired with fine-tuned weights, are the two usual causes. Verify by round-tripping a known prompt and inspecting the token ids.
PREVENT: ship weights and tokenizer as ONE versioned artifact and assert vocab size against config.json at startup; add a golden-prompt output check to the deploy smoke test, since nothing else detects this.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, repair the artifact pairing and restart

patterns.summary: All LoRA adapter slots are occupied, so requests naming a new adapter are refused or forced to wait for an eviction. Multi-tenant adapter serving fails per-tenant rather than globally, which makes it look like a client-specific bug instead of a capacity limit.
patterns.action:
NOW: raise --max-loras if you have memory headroom (each resident adapter costs VRAM), or route requests so hot adapters stay resident and cold ones share a slot.
INVESTIGATE: count DISTINCT adapters in your traffic against --max-loras. If distinct adapters exceed slots, thrash is arithmetic and no tuning avoids it, you need sharding by adapter across replicas. Also check --max-lora-rank: an adapter above the configured rank is rejected outright, which looks identical.
PREVENT: route by adapter id so each replica serves a bounded set; alert on adapter eviction rate, which is the leading indicator of thrash.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, raise the adapter budget or shard by adapter

patterns.summary: Triton could not load a model version from the repository. With repository polling enabled, a partially-written model directory is picked up mid-copy and fails to load, while the previously loaded version may keep serving, so the deployment looks successful and traffic silently stays on the old version.
patterns.action:
NOW: check which versions are actually READY (GET /v2/repository/index) rather than assuming the new one loaded. Re-copy the failed version to a staging path and move it in atomically.
INVESTIGATE: confirm the config.pbtxt version_policy matches intent, "latest" with a failed newest version behaves very differently from "specific". Verify the model directory shape (version-numbered subdirectory containing the model file) which is the most common mistake.
PREVENT: publish model versions atomically (write elsewhere, then rename) so polling never sees a partial directory; assert the expected version is READY as a deploy gate.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, republish the model version atomically and reload

patterns.summary: A Ray Serve replica hosting an inference engine is in a restart loop. Ray restarts the actor automatically, so the deployment reports as up while every restart re-loads model weights, the loop consumes GPU and network continuously and can starve healthy replicas of the resources they need.
patterns.action:
NOW: cap max_restarts on the deployment so the loop stops and the failure becomes visible instead of self-healing forever.
INVESTIGATE: the replica actor's own log holds the cause; the controller log only reports the restart. Distinguish a host OOM kill of the worker (raise object-store / worker memory, check the Ray dashboard's per-actor memory) from a CUDA OOM inside the engine (lower the engine's memory fraction). Confirm num_gpus per replica matches what the engine actually needs, an under-declared replica gets co-scheduled and OOMs.
PREVENT: declare accurate per-replica GPU and memory resources; alert on replica restart count, which is otherwise hidden by successful recovery.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, fix the replica-level cause; Ray will restart it

negativeEvidence.re: GPU is lost|GPU has been reset

patterns.summary: Xid 149. NVLink/C2C fatal link event (newer boards: GH200/GB-class). Coherent-link error; node-local GPU↔GPU or GPU↔CPU traffic compromised.
patterns.action:
NOW: drain node.
INVESTIGATE: nvidia-smi c2c -e (where supported) / nvlink -e; BMC SEL for concurrent power events.
ESCALATE: vendor case with SEL + dmesg; C2C faults are board-level, not user-serviceable.

patterns.re: i915 [0-9a-f:.]+: \[drm\] GPU HANG|i915.*Resetting (rcs|ccs|chip) for hang|GPU hang on (rcs|ccs)
patterns.summary: Intel i915/Xe GPU engine hang, the kernel driver detected a stuck engine and is resetting it. Compute context on the affected engine is lost.
patterns.action:
NOW: restart the workload after the reset completes (dmesg shows "GuC firmware...loaded" / engine reset done).
INVESTIGATE: dmesg -T | grep -i "i915\|GuC"; /sys/class/drm/card*/error (capture before it rotates); check kernel vs intel-gpu firmware versions.
PREVENT: pin validated kernel+GuC firmware pairs; avoid mixing Level Zero runtime versions across the fleet.
ESCALATE: hangs across different workloads on one card → replace card; identical hang fleet-wide after an update → roll back firmware.

patterns.summary: ncclInvalidUsage, the application called NCCL incorrectly (mismatched collective sizes/dtypes across ranks, communicator misuse, group nesting). A code bug, not infrastructure.
patterns.action:
NOW: capture NCCL_DEBUG=WARN output; the message names the offending call.
INVESTIGATE: diff per-rank tensor shapes/dtypes at the failing collective (classic: uneven batch on last dataloader iteration with drop_last=False); check every rank enters the same collectives in the same order.
PREVENT: shape-assert wrapper around collectives in your trainer; drop_last=True or padded batches.
ESCALATE: n/a, application-level fix.

patterns.re: ValueError: Attempting to unscale FP16 gradients|GradScaler.*(unscale.*twice|inf checks)|Attempted unscale_ but _scale is None
patterns.summary: GradScaler misuse, unscaling FP16 gradients (model was .half()ed instead of autocast), double unscale_ per step, or scaler state desync after checkpoint resume without scaler.load_state_dict.
patterns.action:
NOW: keep model weights FP32 + autocast for forward (never model.half() with GradScaler); call unscale_ once, before clip_grad.
INVESTIGATE: was scaler state saved/restored with the checkpoint? (scaler.state_dict() belongs in it).
PREVENT: unit test the AMP step (scale→backward→unscale→clip→step→update) in CI.

patterns.re: \bSlowDown\b|503.{0,40}\bS3\b|Reduce your request rate|Please reduce your request rate|S3.{0,20}throttl
patterns.summary: S3 throttling (503 SlowDown), request rate exceeded per-prefix limits.
patterns.action:
NOW: exponential backoff (SDK adaptive retry) and cut concurrent writers to the hot prefix.
INVESTIGATE: which prefix is hot (server access logs / CloudWatch 5xxErrors by prefix); request rate vs ~3.5k PUT / 5.5k GET per prefix-second.
PREVENT: hash-partition keys; spread shards across prefixes; S3 Transfer Manager.

patterns.summary: vLLM weight loading failed, safetensors corrupt/missing or architecture-shape mismatch for this vLLM version.
patterns.action:
NOW: verify files (sizes vs hub metadata, sha256); confirm --model path/revision.
INVESTIGATE: quantization flag vs artifact (AWQ/GPTQ mismatch); TP degree changes shard expectations.
PREVENT: pin model revision hashes; startup checksum validation.

patterns.summary: Spot/preemption reclaim raced an in-flight checkpoint save - shards written up to the power-off are truncated. The corruption is the EFFECT; the preemption is the root cause.
patterns.action:
NOW: resume from the last COMPLETE checkpoint (verify manifest/shard count), not the raced one.
INVESTIGATE: save duration vs reclaim window (ITN gives ~120s on AWS).
PREVENT: atomic publish (tmp dir + manifest-last), on-SIGTERM checkpoint sized to the window.
ESCALATE: n/a - capacity behavior.

patterns.summary: Xid 119/120 - GSP (GPU System Processor) RPC timeout. The driver-firmware RPC channel deadlocked; the GPU resets and the CUDA context is lost. Known driver/GSP-firmware combo bugs are the usual cause - check vendor advisories before suspecting silicon.
patterns.action:
NOW: reset the GPU (or reboot if reset fails); resume from checkpoint.
INVESTIGATE: driver + GSP firmware version vs NVIDIA advisories for your board; recurrence per GPU serial.
PREVENT: upgrade to the advisory-fixed driver, or disable GSP (NVreg_EnableGpuFirmware=0) where supported and acceptable.
ESCALATE: recurring on one GPU after the fixed driver -> RMA with nvidia-bug-report.

patterns.re: NCCL timeout|Watchdog caught collective operation timeout|ncclTimeout
patterns.summary: NCCL collective timed out. One rank stopped participating.
patterns.action: Check the failing rank with nvidia-smi and kill zombie processes. Raise the collective timeout via init_process_group(timeout=timedelta(minutes=30)) (there is no NCCL_TIMEOUT env var); for watchdog tuning use TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC. For IB-level retries: NCCL_IB_TIMEOUT=22 (valid range 0-31).

negativeEvidence.re: Eviction manager|invoked oom-killer|oom_kill|Out of memory: Killed

patterns.summary: NVLink error (Xid 145/149) - link degraded or failed.
patterns.action: Compare per-GPU NVLink bandwidth (all 8 low = NVSwitch; one low = that link). Check nvidia-smi nvlink -e; drain/reset the implicated component.

patterns.re: Could not find NET with id 0|Could not find a path for pattern
patterns.summary: NCCL network topology lookup failed (NIC fusion remapped NET/0).
patterns.action: Set NCCL_NET_MERGE_LEVEL=LOC or upgrade to NCCL 2.27.x; avoid NCCL 2.26.2 on partial-node IB allocations.

patterns.re: ibv_modify_qp failed with error Connection timed out|ibv_modify_qp[^\n]{0,40}errno 110
patterns.summary: RDMA queue-pair setup timed out (errno 110), often during checkpoint save at scale on RoCE.
patterns.action: Tune RoCE PFC/ECN; verify NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX; raise NCCL_IB_TIMEOUT; stagger/shard checkpoint writes.

patterns.re: Got completion with error 4.*vendor err 81|completion with error 4.*vendor_err 81
patterns.summary: ACS disabled in BIOS breaks GPU Direct RDMA. RDMA transactions between GPU and NIC rejected.
patterns.action: Enable ACS in BIOS under PCIe settings; or disable GDR with NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=0.

patterns.re: Attribute busid of node nic not found
patterns.summary: NCCL topology XML missing NIC PCI bus ID, cannot associate NIC with NUMA node/GPU.
patterns.action: Set NCCL_TOPO_FILE to a manually created topology XML; or set NCCL_IB_HCA explicitly to the correct device name.

patterns.re: could not select device driver.*"nvidia"|nvidia-smi.*not found|NVIDIA-SMI has failed
patterns.summary: Container cannot access NVIDIA GPUs, nvidia-container-toolkit not installed or not configured.
patterns.action: `sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker && sudo systemctl restart docker`. In K8s: set `runtimeClassName: nvidia` in pod spec and install NVIDIA device plugin.

patterns.re: Expected (?:all tensors to be|input tensor) on the same device|to be on the same device|two devices.*received
patterns.summary: Tensors on different devices (CPU vs GPU, or different GPUs) in an operation that requires same-device tensors.
patterns.action: Check that model parameters are on the correct device: `model = model.to(device)`. Verify input tensors are moved to GPU: `inputs = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in inputs.items()}`. For DDP/FSDP, ensure all modules are moved after wrapping.

patterns.summary: DataLoader batch collation error, custom collate_fn or default_collate raised an exception combining samples into a batch, usually from inconsistent tensor shapes.
patterns.action: Check that all samples in a batch return the same tensor shapes and dtypes. Verify custom collate_fn handles edge cases (empty tensors, None values, variable-length sequences). Add `collate_fn=debug_collate` wrapper to log individual sample shapes before merging.

patterns.summary: SentencePiece model file not found or protobuf deserialization error, model.spm is missing, corrupted, or version mismatch with the protobuf library.
patterns.action: Verify model file exists: `ls -la <model_path>/tokenizer.model`. Re-download from HuggingFace Hub: `huggingface-cli download <repo> tokenizer.model --local-dir ./models/`. Update protobuf: `pip install protobuf>=3.20.3`. For local mode, set `TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false` and use `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("<local_path>", use_fast=False)`.

patterns.summary: PCIe Advanced Error Reporting (AER), correctable or fatal PCIe transport errors logged by the kernel.
patterns.action: `dmesg -T | grep -i aer`. Uncorrectable: reboot and reseat GPU. Correctable: update GPU firmware and check PCIe slot power/ground integrity. Set `pci=noaer` only as last resort.

patterns.summary: HBM memory temperature critical. HBM junction temperature exceeded safe threshold.
patterns.action: `nvidia-smi -q -d TEMPERATURE | grep -i hbm`. Reduce ambient / improve airflow. Emergency: cap power with `nvidia-smi -pl 300`. If persistent, the thermal interface may need replacement.

patterns.summary: GPU SRAM or register-file ECC error, on-chip memory (L1/shared/regfile) detected a hardware ECC fault.
patterns.action: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC`. Run `nvidia-smi -r` to reset ECC counters; run `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck python train.py`. RMA if double-bit SRAM ECC recurs.

patterns.summary: cuBLAS handle creation failed, library not initialized or driver context invalid.
patterns.action: Check CUDA driver version matches toolkit. Reinstall: `pip install nvidia-cublas-cu12 --force-reinstall`. Set `CUBLAS_LOG_LEVEL=1` for diagnostics. Verify GPU compute capability with `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=compute_cap --format=csv`.

patterns.summary: CUDA driver not loaded, nvidia kernel module failed to load or was unloaded.
patterns.action: `lsmod | grep nvidia`, if empty: `sudo modprobe nvidia` then `sudo modprobe nvidia-uvm`. Check dmesg for NVRM init errors. Reinstall: `sudo apt install --reinstall nvidia-driver-570`. Reboot required if GPU firmware initialization failed.

patterns.summary: CUDA kernel launch timed out (error 802), a kernel ran past the TDR threshold.
patterns.action: Check for infinite loops in custom CUDA kernels (off-by-one in grid/block dims). Increase TDR on Windows: `reg add HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\GraphicsDrivers\TdrDelay /t REG_DWORD /d 60`. Split long-running kernel into smaller grid launches.

patterns.summary: PyTorch: torch.compile + CUDA graphs error. Inductor CUDA graph capture failed from dynamic shapes or tensor-valued control flow.
patterns.action: TORCH_COMPILE_DEBUG=1 python train.py 2>&1 | grep -E "graph.*break|GraphModule|capture.*fail". Fix: set torch.compile(dynamic=False), or torch._inductor.config.triton.cudagraphs = False, or upgrade to PyTorch >=2.3.

patterns.re: device_map.*auto.*fail|accelerate.*not.*installed|No device_map available|The model\'s device_map is not compatible
patterns.summary: HF Transformers: device_map="auto" failed. Accelerate not installed or incompatible hardware mapping.
patterns.action: pip install accelerate -q && python -c "from accelerate import infer_auto_device_map; print(infer_auto_device_map(model))" 2>&1. Fix: install accelerate>=0.26; or set device_map=None and manually .to("cuda").

patterns.summary: Horovod: allreduce stalled or Horovod process shut down. Usually from rank failure or NCCL timeout.
patterns.action: Increase HOROVOD_FUSION_THRESHOLD=67108864; set HOROVOD_CYCLE_TIME=5; check for straggler ranks; enable HOROVOD_TIMELINE for debugging.

patterns.summary: Triton: out of shared memory or registers. Kernel exceeds GPU hardware limits for the SM.
patterns.action: Reduce block size (e.g. BLOCK_SIZE=64 instead of 128); use TRITON_ALLOW_TM_ALL=0; compile with --triton-reduce-num-warps=4; split kernel into smaller stages.

patterns.summary: DeepSpeed: checkpoint state dict key mismatch between saved optimizer state and current model.
patterns.action: Ensure model architecture matches checkpoint; purge optimizer state with deepspeed.zero.Buffer.init(); or use --resume-from-custom-ckpt with strict=False.

patterns.summary: NCCL invalid argument, wrong rank count, mismatched communicator, or invalid device ordinal passed to NCCL.
patterns.action: Ensure all ranks call torch.distributed.init_process_group with identical world_size and backend. Check that CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES matches across nodes. Validate device count: python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.device_count())".

patterns.summary: NCCL NET plugin (libnccl-net.so) could not be loaded, custom network plugin missing or incompatible.
patterns.action: Check LD_LIBRARY_PATH includes the directory with libnccl-net.so. Unset NCCL_NET_PLUGIN if no custom plugin is needed. Fall back: export NCCL_NET=Socket.

patterns.summary: Gloo TCP store connection failed (connection refused or DNS resolution failed), ranks cannot reach the rendezvous point.
patterns.action: Verify MASTER_ADDR resolves correctly: getent hosts $MASTER_ADDR. Check firewall: nc -zv $MASTER_ADDR $MASTER_PORT. Ensure rank 0 starts first. For K8s, verify headless service DNS.

patterns.summary: PMIx initialization failed. MPI process management infrastructure could not start.
patterns.action: Check PMIx installation: ompi_info | grep pmix. Verify PMIx version compatibility with the MPI implementation. Fall back: --mca pml ^openib or switch to mpich.

patterns.summary: NCCL topology XML file parsing failed, malformed or incompatible topology description.
patterns.action: Remove NCCL_TOPO_FILE if set. Validate XML: xmllint --noout $NCCL_TOPO_FILE. Generate fresh: NCCL_TOPO_DUMP_FILE=/tmp/topo.xml then run any NCCL op.

patterns.summary: vLLM scheduler overload, sequences preempted or max_num_seqs exceeded under load.
patterns.action: Increase `max_num_batched_tokens`. Reduce `max_num_seqs`. Enable `--use-v2-block-manager`. If persistent, scale out with additional replicas.

patterns.re: CUDA graph.*(?:capture|exec|launch).*(?:fail|error|unable|timeout)|cudaGraph.*(?:capture|instantiate).*fail|cuda graph.*batch.*shape.*mismatch|Failed to capture CUDA graph
patterns.summary: TGI CUDA graph capture failed, static batch shape mismatch or graph replay error.
patterns.action: Disable CUDA graphs: set `--disable-cuda-graphs`. Reduce `--max-batch-size` to keep shapes within capture budget.

patterns.summary: SGLang forward pass NaN, custom attention kernel produced NaN values.
patterns.action: Enable `--enable-torch-compile` for deterministic ops. Reduce `--max-batch-size`. Check input normalization.

patterns.summary: TensorRT-LLM weight transposition failed, quantized checkpoint shape incompatible.
patterns.action: Re-quantize checkpoint with matching quantization type (FP8/INT4/INT8). Use `--use-weight-only` with correct precision. Verify checkpoint is for the target model architecture.

patterns.summary: High memory consumption in mount-s3 under a random-read workload, ending in out of memory. Mountpoint prefetches ahead on every open file handle for sequential access; a seek-heavy pattern of small reads discards almost all of it while the per-handle window keeps growing. Hundreds of concurrent handles multiply that into tens of GB, so the mount process is killed while the application itself is using very little. This is the prefetcher, not a leak, which is why --cache and --maximum-throughput-gbps do not help: one changes where data is stored, the other limits bandwidth, and neither bounds buffered bytes.
patterns.action:
1. Confirm the memory is in the mount process, not the workload:
   ps -o rss=,comm= -p $(pgrep -f mount-s3)      # watch RSS during the random-read phase
2. Reduce concurrent open file handles, that count is the multiplier. Pool and reuse handles, or process shards in batches, instead of holding hundreds open.
3. Check your Mountpoint version and upgrade: prefetcher memory behaviour under random access has changed across releases, so a version bisect is the fastest way to separate a fixed regression from your access pattern.
   mount-s3 --version
4. If the phase is genuinely random over many files, Mountpoint is the wrong tool for it: read through the SDK/CRT client with ranged GETs (no prefetch window), or stage the shards to local disk once and read them locally.
5. Do NOT simply raise the memory limit. That postpones the out-of-memory kill by minutes and hides which of the above actually bounded it.

patterns.re: RCCL WARN Call to ibv_modify_qp failed with error 22
patterns.summary: Invalid argument passed to modify Queue Pair state.
patterns.action: Ensure RoCE interface MTU matches switch configuration.

patterns.summary: Bit error rate is suspiciously high but still correctable.
patterns.action: Log for maintenance and monitor for uncorrectable errors.

patterns.re: Severe packet reordering detected .* \d+ out of sequence
patterns.summary: Multipath routing caused excessive out-of-order delivery.
patterns.action: Constrain flow hashing to ensure in-order delivery.

patterns.re: Falling back to host networking .* ICI collective failed
patterns.summary: High-speed network failed, falling back to slow Ethernet.
patterns.action: Stop training and repair the ICI network to avoid massive slowdown.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to device busy.
patterns.action: Check system logs for device busy and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.re: Neuron runtime.*mmap failed.*unsupported tensor layout.*error code 15
patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to unsupported tensor layout.
patterns.action: Check system logs for unsupported tensor layout and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.re: Neuron runtime.*mmap failed.*KMD version mismatch.*error code 31
patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to KMD version mismatch.
patterns.action: Check system logs for KMD version mismatch and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.re: Neuron runtime.*mmap failed.*host memory pinning failed.*error code 44
patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to host memory pinning failed.
patterns.action: Check system logs for host memory pinning failed and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to mailbox timeout.
patterns.action: Check system logs for mailbox timeout and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.re: Neuron runtime.*mmap failed.*host memory pinning failed.*error code 69
patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to host memory pinning failed.
patterns.action: Check system logs for host memory pinning failed and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.re: Neuron runtime.*mmap failed.*KMD version mismatch.*error code 81
patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to KMD version mismatch.
patterns.action: Check system logs for KMD version mismatch and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.re: Neuron runtime.*mmap failed.*host memory pinning failed.*error code 94

patterns.re: NCCL INFO NET\/Socket\s*:|NCCL INFO Using network Socket|Using network Socket\b
patterns.summary:
NCCL is moving collective traffic over TCP sockets, not over InfiniBand or RoCE.

This is not an error and nothing in the job will report it as one. NCCL announces the
transport once at INFO level during init and then runs normally to completion. The job
succeeds. It is simply several times slower than the hardware it is running on, and the
cost shows up as GPU-hours rather than as a failure.

It is most often introduced by a change that had nothing to do with the fabric: a CNI
upgrade, a base image rebuild, a NIC firmware or driver bump, or a container that lost
its /dev/infiniband mount or its IPC_LOCK capability. That is why it is so often found
days later, by someone comparing throughput against an old run.

What this evidence does and does not establish. It establishes that NCCL selected the
socket transport for this run. It does NOT establish that the fabric hardware is
unhealthy: in most cases the hardware is fine and the software path to it is broken.
Confirm before replacing anything.
patterns.action:
Confirm the transport, then find what removed it.

1. Prove which transport NCCL chose:
   NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,NET <your launch command> 2>&1 | grep -E "NET/(IB|Socket)"
   A healthy run prints NET/IB with an HCA name. NET/Socket confirms this diagnosis.

2. Measure the cost, so the fix is justified with a number:
   all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 8G -f 2 -g <gpus>
   Read busbw. TCP fallback typically lands in single-digit GB/s where IB would be
   40 GB/s or better on the same nodes.

3. Find what is missing, in this order. Each is a common single cause:
   ibv_devinfo                       # do the HCAs exist in this container at all
   ls -l /dev/infiniband             # is the device mounted into the container
   ibstat                            # are the ports Active and LinkUp
   lsmod | grep -E "nvidia_peermem|nv_peer_mem"   # is GPUDirect RDMA loaded
   ulimit -l                         # memlock must be unlimited or IB registration fails
   ipcs -l                           # container needs IPC_LOCK

4. If the HCAs are present but NCCL still will not use them, name them explicitly:
   export NCCL_IB_HCA=mlx5_0,mlx5_1
   export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=^lo,docker0
   Do not set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1. If it is already set anywhere in your environment or
   launcher, that alone explains this.

5. Re-run step 1 and confirm NET/IB before you close the ticket.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint needed, this is a throughput fault and the job completes

negativeEvidence.re: GPU is lost|GPU has been reset

patterns.summary: The NCCL tree algorithm stalled on this topology. Tree is chosen automatically for some rank counts and message sizes, and an irregular or asymmetric rank layout can leave it waiting on a peer that never sends.
patterns.action:
NOW: force the ring algorithm to unblock the run, export NCCL_ALGO=Ring. This is a valid production setting, not just a diagnostic.
INVESTIGATE: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=GRAPH shows the chosen algorithm and the constructed topology. Irregular rank counts and mismatched per-node GPU counts are the common trigger; confirm every node contributes the same number of ranks.
PREVENT: keep rank layouts homogeneous across nodes. Where they cannot be, pin NCCL_ALGO explicitly rather than letting auto-selection vary between runs.
ESCALATE: ring also stalls → the problem is the fabric or a dead rank, not the algorithm; check for a missing participant first.

patterns.summary: GPUDirect RDMA was attempted between a GPU and a NIC on different NUMA nodes. The transfer has to cross the CPU interconnect (UPI/Infinity Fabric), which is far slower than a local path and on some platforms is not supported for peer-to-peer at all.
patterns.action:
NOW: bind each rank to the NIC on its own NUMA node, set NCCL_IB_HCA per rank based on topology rather than letting NCCL pick. nvidia-smi topo -m shows which HCA is local to which GPU.
INVESTIGATE: read the topology matrix, a PIX or PXB path is local; SYS means it crosses the CPU interconnect. Any GPU-HCA pair showing SYS will take this path. Also confirm process CPU affinity places the rank on the matching NUMA node.
PREVENT: derive rank-to-NIC binding from nvidia-smi topo -m at job start rather than hardcoding, so the same script is correct across node types.
ESCALATE: no local NIC exists for some GPUs → a chassis topology limitation; consider NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL to disable GDR on those paths rather than taking the slow route.
patterns.resumeFrom: job start with corrected NIC binding

patterns.summary: LayerNorm produced non-finite gradients because the input variance underflowed. The backward pass divides by sqrt(var + eps); in FP16 a near-constant activation drives variance below representable range and the division explodes.
patterns.action:
NOW: raise the layer norm epsilon (1e-5 → 1e-4 for FP16), and run LayerNorm in FP32 even under autocast, it is cheap and is the standard fix.
INVESTIGATE: a near-zero variance means the activations entering that layer are nearly constant. That is usually upstream: a dead residual branch, an over-aggressive initialization, or a preceding activation saturating. Inspect the input statistics to the failing layer rather than the layer itself.
PREVENT: keep normalization layers in FP32 (autocast already does this for LayerNorm by default, a custom implementation may not). Use BF16 rather than FP16 where available.
ESCALATE: variance collapse that reappears in FP32 is a model problem, not precision; check initialization and residual scaling.
patterns.resumeFrom: last checkpoint before the loss went non-finite

patterns.re: Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault in [\w./-]+\.so|Segmentation fault in [\w./-]*_cuda\.so
patterns.summary: A custom compiled CUDA extension segfaulted. The crash is inside your own .so, so the Python traceback is not the fault, it only shows where the call was made from.
patterns.action:
NOW: get a real stack. Run under compute-sanitizer (compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck python train.py), it names the offending kernel and the invalid access, which a Python traceback cannot.
INVESTIGATE: the common causes in hand-written kernels are an unchecked launch configuration (grid/block exceeding device limits), missing bounds checks on a ragged input, and assuming contiguous tensors without calling .contiguous(). Check the input that differs on the failing batch.
PREVENT: build with -lineinfo so sanitizer output maps to source lines, and add TORCH_CHECK on tensor shape, dtype and contiguity at the extension boundary. Most of these crashes are an assertion that was never written.
ESCALATE: sanitizer clean but still crashing → an ABI mismatch; rebuild the extension against the exact torch and CUDA versions in the runtime image.

patterns.re: TCP fast socket table full|too many open files.*tcp

patterns.action: Increase fs.file-max and configure NCCL to use properly sized connection pools.

patterns.summary: SGLang's hierarchical cache (HiCache) exhausted its host-memory tier. HiCache extends the KV cache into pinned host RAM, so its budget competes with the container memory limit, overshooting it gets the whole server OOM-killed by the host rather than degrading gracefully.
patterns.action:
NOW: lower --hicache-ratio, or raise the container memory limit to cover host_tier_bytes plus weight-loading buffers plus normal RSS with headroom.
INVESTIGATE: pinned host allocations do not appear in nvidia-smi and are easy to miss in sizing. Measure container RSS with HiCache enabled and disabled to get the true delta. Then confirm the transfer is actually paying for itself: if the host tier's hit rate is low, PCIe transfer cost exceeds recompute and disabling it is faster.
PREVENT: size the container memory limit from measured RSS with HiCache on; alert on working-set against limit, not on cache metrics alone.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, retune --hicache-ratio or raise the memory limit, then restart

patterns.summary: LMDeploy hit a session limit, either concurrent sessions above max_batch_size, or a conversation exceeding session_len. LMDeploy's session model is stateful, so an abandoned session holds KV cache until it is explicitly freed: leaked sessions consume capacity indefinitely with no error until the limit is reached.
patterns.action:
NOW: raise max_batch_size if you have KV headroom, or fix the client to free sessions it abandons (each session holds cache until released).
INVESTIGATE: distinguish the two causes. session_len exceeded = one conversation grew past the configured context; session COUNT exceeded = leaked sessions. For the second, compare active sessions against genuinely active clients, a large gap is a client-side leak, and restarting the server only postpones it.
PREVENT: give sessions a server-side TTL, and monitor active sessions against max_batch_size as a leading indicator.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, free stale sessions or raise the limit; the server stays up

patterns.summary: The KV lookup buffer between prefill and decode is full, prefill is producing faster than decode consumes. This is backpressure, and it means the two pools are mis-sized relative to each other; adding prefill capacity makes it worse.
patterns.action:
NOW: scale DECODE capacity, not prefill. A full buffer means prefill already outpaces decode, so more prefill deepens the queue.
INVESTIGATE: derive the correct ratio from your traffic, long prompts with short outputs need more prefill; short prompts with long outputs need much more decode. Measure both phases separately and set the pool ratio from the measurement rather than from a default. Raising kv_buffer_size in kv_transfer_config only converts an error into latency; it does not add capacity.
PREVENT: monitor buffer occupancy as the primary signal for autoscaling the two pools independently; a single aggregate metric cannot express this.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, scale the decode pool; the engines are healthy

patterns.summary: Model weight loading took minutes. When many replicas start together they read the same shards from one object store or shared filesystem at once and throttle each other, so a rolling restart is slower per replica than a single cold start, and the scheduler often kills them mid-load for failing startup probes.
patterns.action:
NOW: raise the startupProbe failureThreshold so slow-but-progressing replicas are not killed (kubectl edit deploy, or the equivalent in your chart), then stagger the rollout (lower maxSurge / add a start delay) so replicas do not contend.
INVESTIGATE: compare single-replica cold start against the rollout's per-replica time. A large gap confirms contention rather than slow storage. Check for client-side throttling from the object store (503/SlowDown) which is invisible unless you look for it.
PREVENT: cache weights on local NVMe or a read-through cache so only the first pull crosses the network; size startupProbe from measured p99 cold start with the intended concurrency.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, stagger the rollout and raise the startup budget

patterns.summary: Multimodal preprocessing failed for a request. Image and audio inputs are decoded on the CPU before reaching the GPU, so a malformed or oversized input fails one request without touching engine health, but the decode cost is on the request path and a burst of large inputs becomes a latency incident.
patterns.action:
NOW: validate and bound media inputs at the gateway (dimensions, format, count per prompt). Reject oversized inputs with a 400 rather than letting them consume decode CPU and then fail.
INVESTIGATE: confirm limit_mm_per_prompt matches what clients actually send, exceeding it is a hard rejection. Check whether CPU preprocessing is the real bottleneck by watching CPU saturation during multimodal bursts; that presents as engine slowness with an idle GPU.
PREVENT: normalise media (resize, transcode) before the inference tier; give the preprocessing pool its own capacity so a media burst cannot starve text traffic.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, the engine is healthy; validate media inputs upstream

patterns.summary: Intel GuC (graphics micro-controller) firmware failure, scheduling/submission microcode crashed or failed to load; the GPU cannot accept work.
patterns.action:
NOW: reload the driver (modprobe -r i915 && modprobe i915) or reboot.
INVESTIGATE: dmesg for GuC version line; verify /lib/firmware/i915/*.bin matches the kernel's expected GuC version.
PREVENT: ship firmware with the kernel image (linux-firmware pinning).
ESCALATE: persists with matched firmware → Intel support with the GuC log snapshot.

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Ninja is required to load C\+\+ extensions|error: command ['"]?ninja['"]? failed|ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed|ninja: error:
patterns.summary: JIT CUDA extension build failed under ninja, missing ninja, nvcc/gcc incompatibility, or a compile error in the extension source. Job dies at import time.
patterns.action:
NOW: read the first "error:" line in the ninja output (the real compiler error); pip install ninja if absent.
INVESTIGATE: nvcc --version vs torch.version.cuda; gcc major version supported by that CUDA (12.1→gcc≤12); TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST set for your GPUs.
PREVENT: prebuild extensions into the image (no JIT at scale); cache TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR per image hash.
ESCALATE: n/a, toolchain fix.

patterns.re: RuntimeError: Trying to backward through the graph a second time|Specify retain_graph=True|one of the variables needed for gradient computation has been modified by an inplace operation
patterns.summary: Autograd graph misuse, second backward without retain_graph, or an in-place op clobbered a tensor the backward needs. Code bug; deterministic.
patterns.action:
NOW: the traceback's "Hint" names the op; for in-place: run with torch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly(True) once to get the forward-op stack.
INVESTIGATE: shared modules called twice with cached activations; .add_()/.relu_() on tensors that require grad.
PREVENT: anomaly-detection run in CI on a tiny batch.

patterns.summary: TransformerEngine FP8 delayed-scaling saturated (amax overflow) - an activation outlier exceeded the scaling headroom and produced inf/NaN. Loss and gradients were healthy right up to the saturation step: this is an FP8-recipe problem, not data or learning rate.
patterns.action:
NOW: resume from the checkpoint before the first saturation warning; raise DelayedScaling margin to 2-4 and lengthen amax_history_len.
INVESTIGATE: which layer saturated (TE logs name it); consider bf16 for that block (hybrid recipe).
PREVENT: log scaling factors and alert on saturation before NaN; outlier-audit activations when enabling FP8 on a new architecture.
patterns.resumeFrom: checkpoint predating the first saturation warning

patterns.summary: MosaicML Streaming shard index corruption, canary value mismatch indicates the shard index file was partially written or does not match the shard data.
patterns.action: Re-index the dataset: `python -m streaming.base.util.convert_to_mds --input <raw_data> --output <mds_root>`. Delete corrupt index: `rm <mds_root>/shard.*.mds.idx` and re-run download. Validate shard: `python -c "from streaming import MDSWriter; ..."` or use MosaicML validation utilities.

patterns.summary: GPU BAR1 mapping failure. CPU cannot map GPU memory aperture; often BAR1 exhaustion or firmware bug.
patterns.action: `nvidia-smi -q -d BAR1_MEMORY`. Reduce `vmalloc` pressure. Reboot to refresh BAR. For large-HBM GPUs (80GB+), set `pci=realloc=on` kernel param.

patterns.summary: cuDNN convolution operation failed, unsupported algorithm, channel layout mismatch, or GPU compute capability limit.
patterns.action: Set `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True`. Reduce `--cudnn-benchmark` to allow fallback algorithms. Check feature map channels are multiples of 8/16 for tensor cores. Update cuDNN: `pip install nvidia-cudnn-cu12 --upgrade`.

patterns.summary: CUDA invalid handle (error 11), a GPU resource handle (stream, event, module) was used after destruction or never created.
patterns.action: Check for use-after-free of CUDA streams or events. Ensure `torch.cuda.Stream` objects are not garbage collected during async operations. For NCCL: rebuild communicator with `torch.distributed.destroy_process_group()`. Set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` to identify the source.

patterns.summary: CUDA IPC handle operation failed, cross-process GPU memory sharing between ranks broke down, usually from a peer death or mismatch.
patterns.action: Ensure all ranks are alive before IPC: add a barrier before the IPC call. For NCCL: set `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` or `NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1`. Increase shared memory: `--shm-size=8g`. Check `nvidia-smi topo -m` for peer access support between GPUs.

patterns.summary: PyTorch: torch.jit.trace / torch.export failed. Unsupported control flow or dynamic tensor shapes in traced function.
patterns.action: python -c "import torch; @torch.jit.script def f(x): return x.sum(); print(f.code)" 2>&1. Fix: replace dynamic control flow with torch.jit.is_scripting() guards; use torch.export(..., strict=False) or enable dynamic shapes.

patterns.summary: DeepSpeed: optimizer step error in mixed precision mode. FP32 master weights out of sync with FP16 grads.
patterns.action: Set "zero_optimization.allgather_bucket_size": 5e8 and "zero_optimization.reduce_bucket_size": 5e8; disable optimizer offload; verify gradient clipping range.

patterns.summary: HF Transformers: generation config parameter out of valid range or misconfigured.
patterns.action: model.generation_config.repetition_penalty = max(1.0, min(2.0, penalty)); set generation_kwargs={"repetition_penalty": 1.1, "bad_words_ids": [[tokenizer.eos_token_id]]}.

patterns.summary: Megatron-LM: pipeline parallel microbatch boundary error. Microbatches don't divide sequence length or global batch.
patterns.action: Set --global-batch-size divisible by --micro-batch-size * --num-layers-per-pipeline-stage; ensure sequence length is divisible.

patterns.summary: Triton: kernel autotune timed out. Autotuning heuristic got stuck or took too long.
patterns.action: Set TRITON_MAX_AUTOTUNE=1 to limit autotune; or TRITON_DISABLE_AUTOTUNE=1 for best existing config; upgrade triton to >=2.3.

patterns.summary: Transformer Engine: FP8 quantization error. FP8 scaling factors or amax reduction failed.
patterns.action: Set fp8_format="HYBRID" and update_fp8_meta_interval=1; decrease --fp8-margin; disable FP8 with NVTE_FP8_DPA_BWD=0; FP8 requires SM90+.

patterns.summary: NCCL ring initialization failed, rings could not be created between GPUs for collective communication.
patterns.action: Verify GPU topology: nvidia-smi topo -m. Check NVLink connectivity: nvidia-smi nvlink -s. Set NCCL_NET=IB or NCCL_NET=Socket based on topology.

patterns.summary: NCCL tree algorithm initialization failed, binary tree reduction topology could not be built.
patterns.action: Disable tree algorithm: NCCL_ALGO=RING (forces ring-only). Check for NVLink/NVSwitch asymmetry across nodes. Ring often works when tree fails on unbalanced topologies.

patterns.summary: UCX memory registration failed, cannot pin or register GPU/CPU memory for RDMA transport.
patterns.action: Increase memlock: ulimit -l unlimited. Check /etc/security/limits.conf. For Docker: --ulimit memlock=-1:-1. Set UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n to disable registration cache.

patterns.summary: TGI flash attention kernel selection failed. GPU compute capability unsupported.
patterns.action: Verify GPU CC with `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=compute_cap --format=csv`. Upgrade flash-attn: `pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation`. Set `--disable-flash-attn-2` as fallback.

patterns.summary: Triton Inference Server model repository polling failed, cannot read model files.
patterns.action: Verify model repository directory exists and is readable: `ls -la <model_repo>`. Check filesystem health. Set `--repository-poll-secs 0` to disable polling if using static models.

patterns.summary: Inference request timeout or client disconnect, request abandoned mid-generation.
patterns.action: Increase timeout settings: `--request-timeout` or `--queue-timeout`. Set `--cancel-request-on-client-disconnect=false` to continue generation.

patterns.re: Neuron runtime.*mmap failed.*host memory pinning failed.*error code 19
patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to host memory pinning failed.
patterns.action: Check system logs for host memory pinning failed and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to mailbox timeout.
patterns.action: Check system logs for mailbox timeout and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to VMA overlap.
patterns.action: Check system logs for VMA overlap and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to VMA overlap.
patterns.action: Check system logs for VMA overlap and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.re: NCCL WARN NET\/Socket : Connection closed by peer.*keepalive
patterns.summary: Aggressive TCP keepalives killing idle NCCL connections during compute.
patterns.action: Increase tcp_keepalive_time in sysctl.

patterns.summary: Too few NCCL TCP channels to saturate GCP 100Gbps links.
patterns.action: Set NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=4 or 8 to multiplex TCP streams.

patterns.summary: InfiniBand HDR link mlx5_6 flapping or transitioned to ARMED state.
patterns.action: Perform VM redeploy or node replacement via Azure portal to fix faulty optical transceiver.

patterns.action: Apply custom NDv4 topology XML and ensure NCCL_TOPO_FILE is pointing to it.

patterns.summary: In-network compute (SHARP) failed to allocate resources on partition for mlx5_ib0.
patterns.action: Disable SHARP via NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0 or check UFM quota.

patterns.summary: Sequence Parallelism all-gather buffers fragmenting PP bubble. (Stage/Variant 7)
patterns.action: Reduce sequence length or increase tensor parallel size. Applied at step 7.

patterns.summary: Last PP stage OOM during pipeline flush gradient accumulation. (Stage/Variant 27)
patterns.action: Use fp8/bf16 optimizer or reduce gradient accumulation steps. Applied at step 27.

patterns.summary: Transformer layer activation recomputation vs PP bubble size mismatch. (Stage/Variant 47)
patterns.action: Use selective activation recomputation. Applied at step 47.

patterns.summary: PyTorch caching allocator fragmentation during PP alternating forward/backward. (Stage/Variant 67)
patterns.action: Set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128. Applied at step 67.

patterns.summary: Megatron-LM p2p_communication buffers fragmentation. (Stage/Variant 87)
patterns.action: Set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 or tune PyTorch allocator max_split_size_mb. Applied at step 87.

patterns.re: TimeoutError: Graph recompilation for batch size 92 exceeded threshold.*
patterns.summary: NCCL watchdog triggered during a long CUDA graph capture.
patterns.action: Tuning block allocator size to prevent eviction during capture.

patterns.re: TimeoutError: Graph recompilation for batch size 98 exceeded threshold.*

patterns.action: Allocate a dedicated CUDA graph memory pool.

patterns.action: Fix tokenizer configuration.

patterns.summary: Sequence length updated concurrently.
patterns.action: Synchronize sequence length tracking.

patterns.summary: Dynamic model loading for multimodal took too long, timing out the ensemble.
patterns.action: Set model load mode to EXPLICIT or increase load timeout.

patterns.summary: OpenCV threading deadlocks with multiprocessing forks. (Case 2)
patterns.action: Set cv2.setNumThreads(0) in worker_init_fn.

patterns.summary: OpenCV threading deadlocks with multiprocessing forks. (Case 37)
patterns.action: Set cv2.setNumThreads(0) in worker_init_fn.

patterns.action: Check for PCIe link width drops via nvidia-smi.

patterns.action: Update NCCL version to latest stable release.

patterns.action: Ensure tensor sizes and types are supported by NCCL. (Observed in AllGather).

patterns.summary: DeepSpeed failed to initialize NCCL due to CUDA context errors during Forward pass.
patterns.action: Check GPU health, driver status, and ensure no other processes are holding the GPU. (Observed in Scatter).

patterns.summary: InfiniBand initialization failed for NCCL during Optimizer step.
patterns.action: Check IB setup, or fallback to sockets using NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1. (Observed in AllReduce).

patterns.summary: Gloo backend timed out during initialization or communication during Evaluation loop.
patterns.action: Switch to NCCL for GPU communication or check network for CPU clusters. (Observed in Broadcast).

patterns.summary: TPU High Bandwidth Memory exhausted during AllGather.

patterns.summary: Tenant attempting fault injection on shared SRAM to bypass MIG.

patterns.action: Isolate node, block tenant, capture nvidia-bug-report, review dmesg and audit logs.

patterns.re: BeeGFS MDS.*directory hash collision limit reached
patterns.summary: BeeGFS metadata server encountered severe hash collisions in a directory with millions of files, blocking new file creation.
patterns.action: Reorganize the dataset into nested subdirectories to keep file counts per directory under 100k.

requiredEvidence.re: File exists error on new file

patterns.summary: Triton autotuner selecting suboptimal kernel configuration due to L2 cache thrashing during profiling.
patterns.action: Manually specify kernel configuration or increase warmup iterations in autotuner.

patterns.summary: TorchInductor creating redundant memory copies for view operations on complex tensors.
patterns.action: Avoid complex view operations or use contiguous tensors before passing to TorchInductor.

patterns.summary: TorchInductor generating unoptimized kernels for sparsely accessed embeddings, resulting in severe GPU underutilization.
patterns.action: Use custom optimized kernels for sparse embeddings or disable torch.compile for the embedding layer.

patterns.type: Volcano Metric Server Delay False Scaling
patterns.re: Queue .* overused, but no resources available
patterns.summary: Delayed metrics propagation causes Volcano to miscalculate queue utilization, starving high-priority workloads.
patterns.action: Check Prometheus/kube-state-metrics performance and network latency.

patterns.re: panic: assignment to entry in nil map
patterns.summary: The svc (service) plugin panics when encountering a Job without a generated headless service name, crashing the scheduler.
patterns.action: Restart the scheduler and ensure all Volcano Jobs have service structures.

patterns.summary: A registered PMIx event handler in the application misses a critical node-failure notification due to server-side queue overflow.
patterns.action: Increase the event queue depth in PMIx MCA parameters.

requiredEvidence.re: pmix_server.*failed to deliver event to client

patterns.summary: Gradient norm calculation failed because ZeRO-3 gradients are partitioned and local norm was NaN.
patterns.action: Use DeepSpeed's internal gradient clipping instead of torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_.

patterns.re: RuntimeError: NaN in MoE router probabilities
patterns.summary: FP8 precision loss in MoE gating network resulted in NaN routing probabilities.
patterns.action: Keep the MoE router and gating mechanism strictly in FP32.

patterns.summary: Lustre client hit max_rpcs_in_flight limit, delaying checkpoint writes.
patterns.action: Increase max_rpcs_in_flight (osc.*.max_rpcs_in_flight) for OSTs.

patterns.re: error while loading shared libraries: libibverbs\.so\.20: cannot open shared object file
patterns.summary: HPC cluster node is missing libibverbs.so.20, preventing RDMA/InfiniBand driver initialization.
patterns.action: Install rdma-core or libibverbs-dev package on the affected node. Check LD_LIBRARY_PATH if it's installed in a non-standard prefix.

patterns.re: NCCL WARN Tree timeout during AllReduce .* rank \d+
patterns.summary: Advanced NCCL topology timeout in multi-rail environment (Case 6). Suspected IB interface instability or CPU bottleneck during Ring/Tree synchronization.
patterns.action: Reboot node to reset NVSwitch state and re-initialize NCCL communicators.

patterns.summary: Silent kernel abort triggered by out-of-bounds read during custom fused kernel execution leading to NCCL unhandled CUDA error (Case 26).
patterns.action: Drain node, reset GPUs via nvidia-smi, and test IB bandwidth.

patterns.re: NVLink error .* bridge failure .* link 10 .* CRC
patterns.summary: Obscure NVSwitch bridging failure causing intermittent packet loss on inter-GPU transfers (Case 46).
patterns.action: RMA GPU due to unrecoverable NVLink CRC errors.

patterns.summary: Docker default seccomp profile blocking perf_event_open needed by GPU profilers.
patterns.action: Run pod with unconfined seccomp profile or add CAP_SYS_ADMIN/CAP_PERFMON.

patterns.summary: cgroup CPU quota throttling deep learning data preprocessing pipeline, causing GPU starvation.
patterns.action: Remove CPU limits to prevent throttling, relying only on CPU requests.

patterns.summary: AWS EFA device removal (hotplug event) detected during Spot preemption, corrupting RDMA context.
patterns.action: Restart NCCL communicators immediately upon device disconnect if using dynamic cluster sizing.

patterns.summary: GCP A2 VM PCI topology mismatch preventing optimal NVLink routing for A100 SXM4.
patterns.action: Recreate VM or update to the latest GCP optimized deep learning VM image with correct topology hints.

patterns.summary: Request batches are exceeding the largest captured CUDA graph, so those batches silently fall back to eager execution. There is no error and no alert, only a latency step change at a specific concurrency, which makes it one of the hardest serving regressions to attribute.
patterns.action:
NOW: raise --cuda-graph-max-bs to at least your p99 running-request count (startup cost and memory both rise, so measure rather than maximising), or cap --max-running-requests at the captured ceiling so behaviour is uniform.
INVESTIGATE: plot decode latency against #running-req from the SGLang stats line. A clean knee at the graph ceiling confirms it. Below the ceiling you are on graphs; above it you are eager, and the two regimes have materially different per-token cost.
PREVENT: derive --cuda-graph-max-bs from load-test concurrency, and re-derive it when you change --max-running-requests, the two flags are coupled and neither validates the other.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, restart with an aligned graph/concurrency ceiling

patterns.summary: Inter-token latency has degraded because the decode batch grew. Decode is memory-bandwidth bound, so per-token latency rises roughly linearly with concurrency: aggregate throughput keeps climbing while every individual stream gets slower. Both numbers are real, and optimising the aggregate degrades the experience.
patterns.action:
NOW: decide which metric you are actually serving. Interactive traffic → cap --max-num-seqs so ITL stays inside your SLO and scale out for volume. Batch traffic → the current behaviour is correct and ITL is the wrong metric to watch.
INVESTIGATE: plot ITL against running-request count. A smooth rise is the expected bandwidth trade-off; a sudden step is something else. CUDA-graph ceiling exceeded (eager fallback), preemption starting, or a straggler GPU. Only the smooth case is a tuning decision.
PREVENT: define the ITL SLO first and derive the concurrency cap from it; without a cap, the scheduler will always trade individual latency for aggregate throughput.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, cap concurrency to the ITL SLO; the engine is healthy

patterns.summary: Serving memory is growing monotonically with request count. A long-running server that OOMs after hours or days is leaking, not under-provisioned, and because a restart resets it, this is routinely misfiled as a capacity problem and never fixed.
patterns.action:
NOW: set a rolling restart on a schedule shorter than the observed time-to-OOM. That is mitigation, not a fix, but it stops the pages.
INVESTIGATE: separate GPU from HOST growth first, they have completely different causes. Compare nvidia-smi memory.used against container RSS over the same window. Host RSS growth usually means retained request/response objects or unbounded metrics labels (a per-request-id label is the classic case). GPU growth usually means cached graphs or adapter state not being released. Correlate growth against request COUNT rather than wall time to identify per-request retention.
PREVENT: alert on the memory growth RATE rather than the absolute level, so a leak is caught before the OOM; bound metric cardinality explicitly.
patterns.resumeFrom: no checkpoint, rolling-restart on a schedule while the leak is fixed

patterns.re: NCCL WARN NET\/IB\s*:?\s*(Got completion (with error|from peer)|.*qp.*error|async event)
patterns.summary: NCCL InfiniBand transport completion error (IBV work-completion status != success). Error 12 = RETRY_EXC_ERR (peer unreachable/link flap), 5 = WR_FLUSH_ERR (QP torn down), 4 = LOC_PROT_ERR (memory registration).
patterns.action:
NOW: identify the peer in the WARN line; check that node's NIC/link state (ibstat, dmesg | grep mlx5).
INVESTIGATE: error 12 → link flaps/firmware (mlx5 "port down" events); error 4 → memlock limits / peermem module; correlate across ranks, one common peer = that node is the fault.
PREVENT: fabric health checks in prolog (ibstat DOWN detection); pin NIC firmware fleet-wide.
ESCALATE: repeated extsynd firmware errors on one HCA → mlxfwreset then RMA.

patterns.summary: safetensors header/metadata error, file truncated (interrupted download/save), wrong format (HTML error page saved as .safetensors), or reader raced a writer.
patterns.action:
NOW: file size vs expected (ls -l vs hub metadata / save manifest); file(1) it, an HTML/JSON error page masquerading is common with proxied downloads.
INVESTIGATE: was the save interrupted (spot reclaim, quota)? is the path on a non-atomic-rename FS (gcsfuse/s3fs) with concurrent readers?
PREVENT: atomic publish pattern (tmp name + rename/manifest-last); checksum sidecars.
ESCALATE: n/a.

patterns.re: socket\.gaierror|Name or service not known|Temporary failure in name resolution|getaddrinfo (failed|ENOTFOUND)|SERVFAIL
patterns.summary: DNS resolution failure, hostnames of peers/master/storage do not resolve. In clusters this cascades into rendezvous timeouts and NCCL bootstrap failures that LOOK like network faults.
patterns.action:
NOW: getent hosts <failing-name> from an affected node; check resolver health (CoreDNS pods / systemd-resolved / dnsmasq).
INVESTIGATE: DNS pod OOM/restarts; ndots/search-domain explosion at scale; conntrack drops of UDP 53.
PREVENT: node-local DNS cache; IP-based MASTER_ADDR for very large jobs.
ESCALATE: n/a, infra fix.

patterns.re: CUDA error: initialization error[\s\S]{0,200}(pin_memory|fork)|pin_memory[\s\S]{0,120}CUDA error: initialization error|start method.{0,20}fork.{0,80}CUDA
patterns.summary: CUDA context poisoned by fork() - CUDA was initialized in the parent before multiprocessing forked (pin_memory/DataLoader workers inherit a broken context). Code-pattern misuse, not a driver or GPU fault.
patterns.action:
NOW: multiprocessing.set_start_method('spawn', force=True) (or DataLoader multiprocessing_context='spawn').
INVESTIGATE: what touches CUDA before workers start (imports calling torch.cuda at module load).
PREVENT: lint rule/import guard: no CUDA init before worker spawn.

patterns.summary: Facility power distribution (PDU phase imbalance / rack cap) is browning out GPUs - power-brake slowdowns cluster by rack and time-of-day, not by workload.
patterns.action:
NOW: report to facilities with the PDU phase telemetry; expect recurring windows until rebalanced.
INVESTIGATE: correlate slowdown windows with PDU phase load; nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE during a window.
PREVENT: phase rebalance on rack adds; alert at 85% phase load.
ESCALATE: facilities ticket - not an RMA.

patterns.re: IB device not found|No IB devices found|ib_plugin.*failed to open
patterns.summary: NCCL cannot find InfiniBand devices. IB kernel modules not loaded or devices not exposed to the container.
patterns.action: `ls /dev/infiniband/` should show umad*, uverbs*. Load: `modprobe ib_umad ib_uverbs`. In Docker: `--device=/dev/infiniband`. In K8s: ensure SR-IOV device plugin exposes IB devices.

patterns.summary: Special tokens (PAD, CLS, SEP, MASK) not defined in tokenizer configuration, model config references tokens not present in tokenizer vocabulary (files 6-7).
patterns.action: Verify tokenizer_config.json has `special_tokens_map` defined. Add missing tokens: `tokenizer.add_special_tokens({"pad_token": "<pad>"})`. Resize model embeddings: `model.resize_token_embeddings(len(tokenizer))`. Load from config: `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path, use_fast=True)`. Check `tokenizer.special_tokens_map` for all required tokens.

patterns.summary: HDF5 file open failed, corrupted H5 header or truncated file, typically from interrupted write or storage failure.
patterns.action: Verify file integrity: `h5ls -r <file.h5> || h5debug <file.h5>`. Repair with `h5repair <file.h5> <output.h5>`. Check file size: `ls -lh <file.h5>` (should match expected). Re-download or regenerate the HDF5 file. For network filesystems, set `HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING=FALSE` to bypass stale locks.

patterns.summary: PCIe link speed or width downgraded, the GPU is not running at Gen5 x16 (or expected width).
patterns.action: `nvidia-smi -q -d PCIE | grep -E "Link|Width|Speed"`. Reseat GPU, check for bent pins. Verify PCIe slot generation in BIOS. If persistent, try a different slot.

patterns.summary: GPU reset recovery failure. D3->D0 power-state transition failed; GPU stuck in power-save.
patterns.action: `nvidia-smi -pm 0 && nvidia-smi -pm 1` to reinitialize. Hard reboot required. Check for PCIe ASPM issues: `sudo setpci -v -d *:*.s 0x88.B=0x00` to disable ASPM on the GPU.

patterns.summary: cuDNN batch normalization kernel failed, often due to NaN inputs, channel mismatch, or corrupted running stats.
patterns.action: Set `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True` and `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False`. Verify input shape channels match the batchnorm layer. Reset running stats: `model.apply(lambda m: m.reset_running_stats() if hasattr(m, "reset_running_stats") else None)`.

patterns.summary: TensorRT engine deserialization failed, the serialized engine was built with a different TensorRT, CUDA, or GPU architecture version.
patterns.action: Rebuild the engine on the target GPU: delete `.engine`/`.plan` files and regenerate. Ensure TensorRT version matches between build and deploy: `python -c "import tensorrt as trt; print(trt.__version__)"`. Set `trt.BuilderFlag.REBUILD_PRECISE` for cross-platform portability.

patterns.summary: PyTorch: scaled dot product attention backend failure. Memory-efficient or flash-attn kernel failed.
patterns.action: export TORCH_BACKEND=SDPA_DISABLE=1 && python train.py 2>&1. Fix: set torch.backends.cuda.enable_flash_sdp(False); torch.backends.cuda.enable_mem_efficient_sdp(False); or upgrade flash-attn to 2.6+.

patterns.summary: DeepSpeed: activation checkpointing recomputation error. Gradients not preserved through checkpointed segment.
patterns.action: Ensure wrapped module outputs require grad; check that no in-place ops inside checkpoint region; increase checkpoint.num_layers or adjust partition.

patterns.summary: HF Transformers Trainer: DeepSpeed config mismerged or incompatible with model architecture.
patterns.action: Validate ds_config.json schema; ensure zero_stage=3 requires offload; use TrainingArguments(deepspeed="ds_config.json") without extra ZeRO flags.

patterns.summary: Megatron-LM: vocabulary parallel embedding size mismatch across tensor parallel ranks.
patterns.action: Set --vocab-size divisible by --tensor-model-parallel-size; pad vocab to nearest multiple; or use --make-vocab-size-divisible-by=128.

patterns.summary: JAX: shard_map shape or sharding spec error. Partition spec incompatible with actual tensor shape.
patterns.action: Ensure PartitionSpec axes match mesh axis names; wrap arrays with pspec_sharding before shard_map; verify tensor rank equals spec length.

patterns.summary: Transformer Engine: module forward called before initialization. TE layers require explicit .init() or delayed init in FSDP.
patterns.action: Call model.init() before forward pass; in FSDP, ensure TE layers are initialized after FSDP wrapper; or use te.delayed_scaling.DelayedScaling.

patterns.summary: NCCL P2P connection between two GPUs failed, peer access over NVLink or PCIe could not be established.
patterns.action: Check nvidia-smi topo -m for P2P capability. Verify NVLink status: nvidia-smi nvlink -s. Disable P2P as fallback: NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 (uses IB/RoCE instead). Check BAR1 size: nvidia-smi -q -d BAR1_MEMORY.

patterns.summary: UCX endpoint operation timed out or disconnected, the remote peer stopped responding to UCX transport messages.
patterns.action: Check network connectivity: ucx_perftest -t tag_lat. Set UCX_RC_TIMEOUT=inf to disable RC timeouts. Set UCX_TCP_TIMEOUT=60000ms.

patterns.summary: NCCL InfiniBand RC QP (queue pair) connect timeout. RDMA connection between NICs failed during QP state transition.
patterns.action: Check IB link state: ibstat (expect ACTIVE). Verify switch partition keys. Set NCCL_IB_TIMEOUT=22 and NCCL_IB_RETRY_CNT=7.

patterns.summary: TensorRT-LLM in-flight batching scheduler error, iteration-level scheduling failed.
patterns.action: Reduce `--max-num-sequences` or `--max-tokens-in-paged-kv-cache`. Set `--scheduler-policy=max_utilization`. Check for GPU memory pressure.

patterns.summary: GPU memory grows unbounded during serving, suspected KV cache or request-tracking leak.
patterns.action: Restart the serving process periodically. Enable `--enable-prefix-caching` to reuse KV blocks. Set `--max-num-sequences` cap.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to mailbox timeout.
patterns.action: Check system logs for mailbox timeout and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.re: Neuron runtime.*mmap failed.*NUMA node mismatch.*error code 32
patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to NUMA node mismatch.
patterns.action: Check system logs for NUMA node mismatch and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to device busy.
patterns.action: Check system logs for device busy and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.re: Neuron runtime.*mmap failed.*unsupported tensor layout.*error code 65

patterns.action: Check system logs for unsupported tensor layout and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to VMA overlap.
patterns.action: Check system logs for VMA overlap and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.re: Neuron runtime.*mmap failed.*NUMA node mismatch.*error code 82
patterns.summary: Neuron runtime memory mapping failed due to NUMA node mismatch.
patterns.action: Check system logs for NUMA node mismatch and verify Neuron driver setup.

patterns.re: Cloud Router BGP route flap.*TCP connection broken
patterns.summary: Cloud Router BGP flaps dropping cross-subnet TCP connections.
patterns.action: Review Cloud Router logs and stabilize BGP peerings.

patterns.summary: UFM or Azure Subnet Manager failed to update routes for HDR port mlx5_0.
patterns.action: Contact Azure support to verify UFM routing tables or restart the IB interface.

patterns.summary: InfiniBand HDR link mlx5_1 flapping or transitioned to DOWN state.
patterns.action: Perform VM redeploy or node replacement via Azure portal to fix faulty optical transceiver.

patterns.summary: Last PP stage OOM during pipeline flush gradient accumulation. (Stage/Variant 6)
patterns.action: Use fp8/bf16 optimizer or reduce gradient accumulation steps. Applied at step 6.

patterns.summary: Transformer layer activation recomputation vs PP bubble size mismatch. (Stage/Variant 26)
patterns.action: Use selective activation recomputation. Applied at step 26.

patterns.summary: PyTorch caching allocator fragmentation during PP alternating forward/backward. (Stage/Variant 46)
patterns.action: Set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128. Applied at step 46.

patterns.summary: Megatron-LM p2p_communication buffers fragmentation. (Stage/Variant 66)
patterns.action: Set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 or tune PyTorch allocator max_split_size_mb. Applied at step 66.

patterns.summary: Interleaved 1F1B increases activation memory footprint. (Stage/Variant 86)
patterns.action: Decrease virtual pipeline parallel size. Applied at step 86.

patterns.summary: MPI delay when sharing KV cache across nodes.
patterns.action: Keep KV cache node-local.

patterns.re: Path gather deadlock in spec decode
patterns.summary: Extracting accepted token paths deadlocked.
patterns.action: Simplify tree topology.

patterns.re: DataLoader worker \(pid \d+\) is killed by signal: Bus error.*var7
patterns.summary: Exhausted /dev/shm shared memory limit. (Case 7)
patterns.action: Increase Docker --shm-size.

patterns.re: DataLoader worker \(pid \d+\) is killed by signal: Bus error.*var14
patterns.summary: Exhausted /dev/shm shared memory limit. (Case 14)
patterns.action: Increase Docker --shm-size.

patterns.summary: Hit OS max file descriptor limit. (Case 19)
patterns.action: Use file_system sharing strategy.

patterns.summary: Worker process deadlocked or took too long. (Case 34)
patterns.action: Increase DataLoader timeout.

patterns.summary: Worker process deadlocked or took too long. (Case 76)
patterns.action: Increase DataLoader timeout.

patterns.summary: Worker process deadlocked or took too long. (Case 83)
patterns.action: Increase DataLoader timeout.

patterns.summary: OpenCV threading deadlocks with multiprocessing forks. (Case 86)
patterns.action: Set cv2.setNumThreads(0) in worker_init_fn.

patterns.summary: Hit OS max file descriptor limit. (Case 89)
patterns.action: Use file_system sharing strategy.

patterns.summary: NaNs propagated into Adam momentum states, corrupting the optimizer state in embedding_layer on V100_32GB (BF16).
patterns.action: Clip gradients to a reasonable norm and check for forward pass numerical stability.

patterns.summary: NaNs propagated into Adam momentum states, corrupting the optimizer state in attention_qkv on V100_32GB (BF16).
patterns.action: Clip gradients to a reasonable norm and check for forward pass numerical stability.

patterns.summary: NaNs propagated into Adam momentum states, corrupting the optimizer state in mlp_dense_2 on V100_32GB (BF16).
patterns.action: Clip gradients to a reasonable norm and check for forward pass numerical stability.

patterns.summary: NaNs propagated into Adam momentum states, corrupting the optimizer state in layer_norm_1 on V100_32GB (BF16).

patterns.summary: NaNs propagated into Adam momentum states, corrupting the optimizer state in layer_norm_2 on V100_32GB (BF16).
