patterns.summary: Container was OOM-killed for host RAM, the kernel killed the process, not an in-application error.
patterns.action: Increase container memory limit; reduce batch size; disable CPU offload; check for memory leak in DataLoaders. Run `kubectl describe pod` to confirm OOMKill reason.

patterns.re: No space left on device|Errno 28|Disk quota exceeded
patterns.summary: Filesystem is full, checkpoint writes or log outputs fail because disk is out of space.
patterns.action: Free disk: `find /checkpoint -name "*.pt" -mtime +7 -delete`. Mount a larger volume or increase PV size in K8s. Set up disk usage monitoring with alert at 80%.

patterns.summary: CUDA invalid argument (error 1), a kernel parameter or API argument was out of range or invalid.
patterns.action: Check tensor shapes, dtypes, and strides. Verify all GPU tensors are contiguous: `tensor = tensor.contiguous()`. Ensure NCCL collective inputs match across ranks. Set `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL` for distributed shape validation.

patterns.summary: PyTorch: TorchDynamo encountered a graph break due to unsupported Python construct.
patterns.action: TORCH_COMPILE_DEBUG=1 TORCHDYNAMO_REPORT_COMPILE_ERRORS=1 python train.py 2>&1 | grep "graph break". Fix: refactor problematic code out of hot path; use torch.compiler.disable() decorator on non-critical sections.

patterns.summary: NCCL system-level error (errno from fork, open, mmap). OS resource exhaustion, not a GPU problem.
patterns.action: Check ulimit -n and /proc/sys/fs/file-max. Increase nproc limit in /etc/security/limits.conf. Run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and strace -f to identify the failing syscall.

patterns.summary: Remote rank reported an error propagated via NCCL, another node crashed during a collective.
patterns.action: Identify the failing remote rank and node from the log. SSH to that node and check dmesg, nvidia-smi, and container logs. Fix the root cause on the remote node before restarting.

patterns.re: LoRA.*(?:slot|adapter|load).*(?:ran out|exhausted|full|no more|fail|error)|No available LoRA slots|maximum.*LoRA.*adapter.*reached|Out of LoRA.*slot
patterns.summary: vLLM ran out of LoRA adapter slots, max LoRA modules loaded concurrently.
patterns.action: Increase `--max-lora-rank` or `--max-num-loras`. Reduce concurrent LoRA adapter count. Set `--lora-dynamic-load` to load/unload on demand.

patterns.summary: TGI shard crashed, a model worker process failed during serving.
patterns.action: Check shard stderr for CUDA errors. Restart TGI with `--num-shard <total - 1>` to exclude the bad GPU. Run `nvidia-smi -r` to reset ECC. Inspect dmesg for Xid events.

patterns.summary: Lustre out of quota on OST.
patterns.action: lfs quota -u $(whoami) <mount>; lfs quota -g <group> <mount>; lfs setquota -u <user> -b <soft> -B <hard> <mount>; clean old data: find <mount> -mtime +30 -delete.

patterns.summary: File descriptor exhaustion, too many open files.
patterns.action: ulimit -n 1048576; cat /proc/sys/fs/file-max; echo 20000000 > /proc/sys/fs/file-max; lsof -u $(whoami) | wc -l.

patterns.summary: Slurm job killed by OOM, exceeded allocated memory.
patterns.action: Increase --mem or --mem-per-gpu in job script; check for memory leaks in application.

patterns.summary: Ray actor died unexpectedly, worker crash or node failure.
patterns.action: Set max_restarts=5 in @ray.remote; check worker logs in /tmp/ray/session_latest/logs; increase object store mem.

patterns.summary: CPU/GPU cross-socket QPI bottlenecks.
patterns.action: Ensure Kubernetes TopologyManager is configured with single-numa-node policy to prevent QPI cross-socket latency.

patterns.summary: DDP gradient bucketing imbalance causing cyclic idle wait times.
patterns.action: Your DDP synchronization is stalling on uneven gradient buckets. Set `find_unused_parameters=False`, adjust `bucket_cap_mb`, or use PyTorch Profiler.

patterns.summary: Gradient checkpointing RNG state desynchronization causing flat loss curves.
patterns.action: Temporarily disable gradient checkpointing to see if loss converges. If using custom CUDA kernels (e.g. FlashAttention) with dropout, ensure the kernel internal RNG state is properly synced with PyTorch.

patterns.summary: GPU Hardware Warning (MONITOR Tier) - Non-fatal Xid detected (e.g., Row Remapper, driver warning, or TDR).
patterns.action: Monitor the GPU for recurrent issues. If this is Xid 154, check dmesg for "Node Reboot Required" or "GPU Reset Required" to escalate. Otherwise, check application logs for CUDA errors.

negativeEvidence.re: replay(?:ing|ed)? archived|archived dmesg|postmortem|historical log|end of archive

patterns.summary: Floating point non-associativity over 100k steps in TF32.
patterns.action: For bit-for-bit reproducibility, set torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False.

patterns.summary: Microcode bug generating NaNs on specific matrices (Heisenbug).
patterns.action: Set CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8, upgrade drivers, or pad matrices to avoid buggy math kernels.

patterns.summary: DeepSpeed silently zeroing gradients over network via FP16 casts.
patterns.action: Verify your DeepSpeed config is not silently casting BF16 gradients to FP16 for communication.

patterns.summary: Forgetting set_epoch(), causing data memorization plateau.
patterns.action: Call sampler.set_epoch(epoch) in your training loop to ensure unique data shuffling per epoch.

patterns.re: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
patterns.summary: Asynchronous CUDA illegal memory access, likely inside a fused kernel (Triton/FlashAttention).
patterns.action: The stack trace is unreliable. You MUST re-run the job with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck to capture the true faulting kernel and out-of-bounds pointer.

requiredEvidence.re: CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported

causalContracts.title: Corrupt input batch introduced NaNs
causalContracts.summary: The first NaN coincides with an explicitly invalid decoded sample; the corrupt input batch is the evidenced initiator, while the later NaN state is downstream.
causalContracts.action: Quarantine the named sample/shard, fail decoding instead of substituting silent zeros, and replay the same batch with finite-value checks at preprocessing output and model input. Verify loss and gradients remain finite before resuming.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the identical cleaned batch still produces NaNs, compare activations at the first non-finite layer and investigate model numerics separately.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the last finite checkpoint before the corrupt sample was consumed

causalContracts.title: W&B rate-limit hook terminated rank zero
causalContracts.summary: The W&B sender exhausted its retry policy and the telemetry hook called exit 1 on rank 0; torchrun worker loss is downstream, not a training or fabric failure.
causalContracts.action: Make telemetry failure non-fatal, honor Retry-After with bounded exponential backoff, and buffer or sample events. Reproduce a 429 in staging and verify training continues while telemetry reports a degraded state.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If rank 0 exits after the hook is disabled, capture its first application traceback and diagnose that separate failure.

causalContracts.title: Cloud spot interruption removed a rank
causalContracts.summary: The cloud interruption controller sent SIGTERM to the trainer before peers lost the rank; the NCCL remote-peer failure is downstream of intentional instance termination.
causalContracts.action: Handle the interruption signal by writing an atomic checkpoint and leaving the process group before the deadline, then requeue on replacement capacity. Verify the checkpoint completes within the notice window.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If no interruption event exists for the affected instance, align the first rank exit with node and fabric logs before changing NCCL.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the newest complete checkpoint written before instance termination

causalContracts.title: Launcher exported an empty CUDA device set
causalContracts.summary: GPUs are visible on the host, but the launcher exported an empty CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES value, so the process was deliberately given no CUDA devices.
causalContracts.action: Fix the scheduler/runtime device allocation path so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES contains only the devices granted to the job, then launch a one-process visibility check inside the same cgroup/container before retrying.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the variable is populated inside the failing container, inspect the effective device cgroup and NVIDIA runtime mounts as a separate visibility failure.

causalContracts.title: Transient Hugging Face Hub incident
causalContracts.summary: The same credential succeeded shortly afterward while the provider reported an active resolve-endpoint incident, favoring a transient upstream failure over invalid credentials.
causalContracts.action: Retry downloads with jittered backoff and a bounded cache, preserve the provider request ID, and verify the same token against the same artifact endpoint before rotating credentials.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the request remains a 401 after provider recovery, validate token scope and repository access without printing the token.

causalContracts.title: Attached log stream was lost while the job progressed
causalContracts.summary: Independent progress signals continued after stdout stopped, and kubelet reports the attached stream was dropped during rotation. This is observability detachment, not a process hang.
causalContracts.action: Reattach through a durable log sink and confirm the process PID, checkpoint timestamps, and training metric step continue to advance. Repair log rotation/forwarder configuration without restarting the healthy job.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If checkpoints and metrics also stop advancing, collect process stacks and collective state before classifying a real hang.

causalContracts.title: Host DIMM correctable-error storm

required.re: crashes follow the NODE|follow the node

causalContracts.summary: Hundreds of correctable memory events identify a host DIMM and failures follow the node across images, making host memory degradation the causal owner.
causalContracts.action: Cordon the named node, preserve EDAC/MCE/BMC evidence, run the vendor memory diagnostic, and service the identified DIMM/channel under the hardware runbook. Verify counters stay flat under a burn-in before return.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If errors follow the workload to a known-good node, reopen the incident as software and compare the first faulting instruction/core dump.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume on a screened node from the last complete checkpoint

causalContracts.title: Profiler timing exposed a latent stream-order race
causalContracts.summary: The profiler changes launch timing and the named custom extension omits stream-order dependencies; it exposed a latent synchronization race rather than causing GPU hardware failure.
causalContracts.action: Add explicit event/stream dependencies in the custom extension, run compute-sanitizer race/synchronization checks on a minimal reproducer, and verify both profiled and unprofiled runs pass repeatedly.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If a dependency-correct build still fails, reduce the kernel sequence and test the profiler/runtime version pair separately.

causalContracts.title: Shared ingest path starved synchronized ranks
causalContracts.summary: All ranks idle together while the shared object-store/NAT path reaches its connection/bandwidth limit, identifying ingest capacity rather than a slow GPU.
causalContracts.action: Stage or cache shards closer to compute, spread connections across adequate egress capacity, and cap loader concurrency below conntrack limits. Verify aggregate bytes/s and GPU duty cycle remain stable through an epoch.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the ingest path stays below limits during a dip, profile decode and host-to-device queues before changing GPU settings.

causalContracts.title: Processes from a prior job retained VRAM
causalContracts.summary: Processes belonging to a completed prior job still own most VRAM, so the new job OOM is cross-job resource leakage rather than batch-size pressure.
causalContracts.action: Verify process ownership, terminate only the stale job processes through the scheduler, and repair the epilog/cgroup cleanup. Confirm the device has no prior-job PIDs and expected free memory before requeueing.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the listed PIDs belong to the current job, collect its allocation timeline and treat the incident as current-workload capacity instead.

causalContracts.title: InfiniBand MTU mismatch after maintenance
causalContracts.summary: The host and replaced switch port advertise different MTUs and point-to-point bandwidth collapsed immediately after maintenance.
causalContracts.action: Have the fabric owner restore a consistent supported MTU across the port path, bounce only the affected link under the change runbook, and verify active MTU plus ib_write_bw returns to baseline before requeueing.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If MTUs are consistent end to end, compare link width/rate and error counters for the replaced port.

causalContracts.title: Internal compiler license service outage

required.re: nvcc fatal[^\n]*license file|Could not open license file

causalContracts.summary: The site-specific compiler wrapper could not contact its required license service, and lmstat confirms that service is down.
causalContracts.action: Route the incident to the internal toolchain/license owner, restore or fail over the license service, and run the same wrapped compiler preflight before restarting builds.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If lmstat is healthy, validate the wrapper license path and container DNS/TLS reachability without bypassing license policy.

causalContracts.title: Scheduled host security scan caused step-time spikes
causalContracts.summary: Step spikes share the scanner cadence and coincide with extreme scanner CPU use while GPU telemetry stays flat, identifying host-side scan interference.
causalContracts.action: Coordinate an approved exclusion or lower-impact scan window for training nodes, then repeat the workload while correlating scanner CPU and step latency. Do not disable security controls outside the security owner change process.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If spikes remain with the approved scan control unchanged/off-window, profile host I/O and scheduler pressure at the same cadence.

causalContracts.title: Non-atomic object-filesystem publish exposed a partial checkpoint

required.re: atomic rename NOT supported|reader listed file mid-upload|non-atomic rename

causalContracts.summary: A reader observed a zero-length/partial checkpoint because the object-filesystem publish path does not provide the assumed atomic rename semantics.
causalContracts.action: Write to a unique object, verify size/checksum, then publish a separate completion manifest that readers require. Quarantine the partial object and rerun the writer/reader race test.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If a manifest-verified object still fails, compare end-to-end checksums and the safetensors writer version.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the last manifest-complete checkpoint

causalContracts.title: NCCL network plugin ABI mismatch
causalContracts.summary: The NCCL network plugin cannot resolve the ABI symbol required by the upgraded NCCL library; generic EFA/fabric tuning cannot repair a loader ABI mismatch.
causalContracts.action: Install a network-plugin build explicitly compatible with the deployed NCCL ABI, validate it with ldd/symbol inspection in the final image, and verify NCCL INFO loads the plugin before scaling out.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the compatible plugin loads but transport still fails, collect the new NCCL INFO/driver error as a separate fabric incident.

causalContracts.title: Evaluation loop retained activation graphs/logits
causalContracts.summary: Training memory is stable until evaluation, where gradient tracking remains enabled and every logits tensor is retained, causing deterministic evaluation-time VRAM growth.
causalContracts.action: Run evaluation under inference_mode/no_grad, detach outputs, and stream metrics instead of retaining all logits. Repeat one full evaluation while plotting allocated memory and confirm it returns to baseline.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If memory still grows with detached streaming outputs, take allocation snapshots across evaluation iterations to locate the remaining owner.

causalContracts.title: Facility cooling failure thermally throttled a rank
causalContracts.summary: The straggling GPU reports active hardware thermal slowdown and reduced clocks while facility cooling failed; the collective timeout is downstream of facility thermal throttling.
causalContracts.action: Stop scheduling into the affected thermal zone, restore cooling under the facility runbook, and verify inlet/aisle temperature plus GPU clocks remain nominal under load before returning nodes.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If only one device remains hot after facility recovery, inspect its airflow, heatsink, fan, and power telemetry as a node-local issue.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the last complete checkpoint on thermally healthy capacity

causalContracts.title: RoCE PFC pause storm localized to a switch leaf
causalContracts.summary: A single NIC/port is emitting an extreme pause-frame rate and every slow rank shares its leaf, identifying a PFC storm rather than independent rank stragglers.
causalContracts.action: Quarantine the implicated NIC/port, enable the approved PFC watchdog/recovery policy, and have the fabric owner correct the lossless-traffic configuration. Verify pause rates and collective latency return to baseline.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If pause counters remain high after isolating that endpoint, trace congestion and ECN/PFC configuration upstream one hop at a time.

causalContracts.title: Clock skew invalidated signed object-store requests
causalContracts.summary: The host clock exceeds the signature validity window, so otherwise valid signed checkpoint requests are rejected until retries abort the job.
causalContracts.action: Restore time synchronization under the host runbook, confirm chrony offset is inside the provider signing tolerance, then retry one signed upload before resuming the job.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If time is synchronized and the same request is denied, validate credential scope/expiry as a separate authentication incident.

causalContracts.title: Mixed driver pools broke cross-node peer access
causalContracts.summary: Only the mixed-driver placement fails peer access and the same workload succeeds within one pool, making heterogeneous driver placement the controlled causal discriminator.
causalContracts.action: Constrain each distributed job to a validated homogeneous driver/runtime pool, then qualify mixed-pool P2P separately before allowing it. Verify the same reproducer across the selected pool.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If a homogeneous pool still fails, capture the exact device-pair P2P matrix and NCCL topology.

causalContracts.title: Retention automation deleted active dataset shards
causalContracts.summary: Cleanup automation deleted dataset shards still referenced by the active training snapshot; the epoch transition merely exposed the retention-policy error.
causalContracts.action: Pause the cleanup rule, restore the exact immutable dataset manifest, and add active-snapshot/reference protection plus a dry-run deletion report before re-enabling retention.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the shard was not in the deletion ledger, verify mount/object version consistency and manifest publication.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume after the dataset manifest and all referenced shards pass verification

causalContracts.title: Nightly image drift introduced an API incompatibility
causalContracts.summary: The checkpoint state is compatible, but the rebuilt image changed the Transformers API between save and resume, causing constructor failure.
causalContracts.action: Restore the last qualified lockfile/image digest or update the call site against the new API, then run checkpoint-resume compatibility in CI before promoting rebuilt images.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the pinned original image also fails, compare checkpoint metadata and the full dependency lock as a separate compatibility issue.

causalContracts.title: Node conntrack exhaustion dropped control-plane traffic
causalContracts.summary: The kernel explicitly drops packets because conntrack is full; actor/heartbeat deaths are downstream control-plane loss amplified by per-pod sidecars.
causalContracts.action: Reduce connection churn/sidecar amplification or node density and size conntrack from measured peak demand under the network runbook. Verify table occupancy and drop counters remain below limits during load.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If drops continue with conntrack headroom, inspect packet loss and control-plane latency at the next network layer.

causalContracts.title: Full log disk blocked application stderr
causalContracts.summary: Every rank is blocked in stderr writes after the node log filesystem reached 100%; the apparent distributed hang is log backpressure.
causalContracts.action: Use the approved log-retention cleanup/rotation path to restore space, disable or sample the per-kernel debug hook, and verify write latency plus free-space alerts before resuming.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If stacks remain blocked after the log sink is writable, recapture stacks and pipe state for a separate I/O deadlock.

causalContracts.title: etcd latency stalled gang scheduling
causalContracts.summary: Saturated etcd storage raises API latency and prevents finalizer/binding progress, leaving the gang below minMember; no training process has started.
causalContracts.action: Route to the Kubernetes control-plane owner, remove the etcd disk contention and restore healthy fsync/API latency, then allow finalizers and gang binding to converge before launch.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If etcd/API latency is healthy, inspect the remaining unschedulable pod constraints and capacity reasons.

causalContracts.title: WekaFS client eviction invalidated an mmap
causalContracts.summary: The storage cluster evicted the client lease while the process retained a mapped file; access through that stale mapping raised SIGBUS.
causalContracts.action: Recover the Weka client session, reopen affected files after reconnect, and avoid keeping mmaps across client eviction. Verify a lease-loss/reconnect test cannot expose stale mappings.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If SIGBUS occurs on a fresh mapping with a healthy client, verify file length/integrity and host memory errors.

causalContracts.title: Immediate pod retries amplified an upstream outage
causalContracts.summary: Immediate retries across the fleet amplified an initial upstream 502 into a 429 rate-limit storm, preventing recovery.
causalContracts.action: Stop the synchronized retry loop, add exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget/circuit breaker, and use a shared cache. Verify request rate stays within the upstream limit during a fault injection.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If errors persist at a low controlled request rate, diagnose the original upstream availability failure separately.

causalContracts.title: CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING leaked into production
causalContracts.summary: A debug environment setting persisted in the production template and serializes every kernel; the NCCL timeout is downstream of the induced slowdown.
causalContracts.action: Remove CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING from the production launch environment, make debug flags job-scoped, and compare the same step profile before/after while keeping all other variables fixed.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If serialization remains after the variable is absent in-process, inspect profiler/debug tooling and explicit synchronizations.

causalContracts.title: MIG mode drift changed worker cardinality
causalContracts.summary: Three nodes remained in MIG mode, so launcher-visible device cardinality differed from the full-GPU job contract and the rendezvous could never reach world size.
causalContracts.action: Place the job only on nodes whose GPU partition mode matches its resource contract, or intentionally configure MIG-aware world size. Verify device count and MIG mode in preflight on every allocated node.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If all nodes have the intended mode and count, inspect the three missing process launches and scheduler events.

causalContracts.title: Leftover packet capture saturated one node
causalContracts.summary: A forgotten all-interface packet capture saturates CPU0/storage on the only slow node and coincides with softirq drops and retransmissions.
causalContracts.action: Confirm capture ownership, stop it through the approved debugging process, cleanly archive/remove its capture under retention policy, and verify softirq drops plus bandwidth recover.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the node remains slow without capture load, inspect NIC/PCIe counters and IRQ affinity.

causalContracts.title: Large image pulls prevented gang admission

required.re: pulling image[^\n]*(?:GB|38\.7)|layers evicted by image GC

causalContracts.summary: A subset of pods remains ContainerCreating while very large images refill through saturated shared egress, so the gang admission timeout occurs before training.
causalContracts.action: Pre-pull/pin the qualified image on the target pool, reduce image size/layer churn, and provide adequate registry caching/egress. Verify all gang members reach image-ready within the scheduler timeout.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If images are already present, inspect volume/network sandbox events for the remaining ContainerCreating pods.

causalContracts.title: vGPU license loss enforced a performance cap
causalContracts.summary: Every virtual GPU reports an unlicensed performance-limited state after the license service certificate expired.
causalContracts.action: Restore licensed service connectivity/certificate through the vGPU owner, then verify each guest reports Licensed and benchmark clocks/step time before returning the pool.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If licensing is healthy but performance remains capped, inspect vGPU profile entitlement and host power/clock policy.

causalContracts.title: Transparent huge-page compaction stalled hosts
causalContracts.summary: The new host policy forces aggressive THP compaction and khugepaged bursts align with page-fault and step stalls; collective timeouts are downstream.
causalContracts.action: Apply the fleet-approved THP policy for this workload (commonly madvise with non-forced defrag), then repeat the workload while measuring compaction stalls and step p99.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If compaction counters stay low during spikes, profile NUMA reclaim and storage/page-cache pressure.

causalContracts.title: Object lifecycle moved active shards to archival storage

required.re: InvalidObjectState|not valid for the object's storage class

causalContracts.summary: The lifecycle rule transitioned still-referenced dataset shards to archival storage, making them unavailable to the epoch reader.
causalContracts.action: Restore the referenced objects, protect active immutable dataset manifests from archival transition, and preflight storage class for every shard before launch.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the restored objects remain inaccessible, validate bucket permissions and object version IDs separately.

causalContracts.title: Maintenance reset CPUs to powersave
causalContracts.summary: A maintenance/BIOS change reset the fleet CPU policy to powersave and reduced feed-side throughput, lowering GPU utilization.
causalContracts.action: Restore the approved performance/energy profile through fleet configuration, verify effective governor and frequency under load, and add drift detection after firmware maintenance.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If CPU frequency is nominal and GPUs remain underfed, profile preprocessing, storage, and host-to-device queues.

causalContracts.title: Identity-group drift removed dataset access
causalContracts.summary: The service identity no longer belongs to the dataset access group after directory attestation/sync, producing the filesystem permission failure.
causalContracts.action: Have the identity/data owner restore the approved group entitlement, refresh identity caches/tokens, and verify read access as the exact service account before resuming.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If membership is correct in-process, inspect filesystem ACLs and mount identity mapping.

causalContracts.title: High-frequency telemetry caused NVML contention
causalContracts.summary: Step jitter began when scrape frequency rose, with exporter CPU and NVML call latency showing telemetry-lock contention rather than GPU computation failure.
causalContracts.action: Reduce/coalesce scrape frequency to the validated observability budget and avoid duplicate NVML polling paths. A/B the same workload and verify NVML latency and step jitter fall together.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If jitter persists at the prior scrape rate, profile CPU scheduling and application telemetry locks.

causalContracts.title: Tokenizer service drift changed resumed-run inputs
causalContracts.summary: The resumed run consumed a newly deployed tokenizer whose token distribution shifted sharply, explaining the immediate loss/gradient jump without changing model state.
causalContracts.action: Pin tokenizer artifact/version and preprocessing digest to the checkpoint/run manifest, restore the prior tokenizer for resume, and compare token IDs on a fixed sample set before training.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If token IDs match the original run, validate optimizer/model checkpoint state and the next changed input component.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume the checkpoint only with its original tokenizer/preprocessing manifest

causalContracts.title: Neighbor-table capacity broke large launches
causalContracts.summary: The kernel neighbor table overflows only at the larger launch scale, dropping bootstrap resolution for random subsets of nodes.
causalContracts.action: Size neighbor-cache thresholds from measured maximum peers/churn and reduce unnecessary neighbor fan-out under the network runbook. Verify overflow counters stay zero during a full-scale launch.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the table has headroom, capture the first failed bootstrap resolution and inspect L2/IPoIB reachability.

causalContracts.title: Switch firmware changed ECN/WRED behavior
causalContracts.summary: Collective slowdown begins with the switch firmware change, and the new WRED defaults drive excessive ECN marks and NIC rate limiting.
causalContracts.action: Have the fabric owner restore the validated WRED/ECN profile or roll back firmware through the change runbook, then verify marks, limiter state, and collective bandwidth against baseline.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If ECN behavior normalizes but bandwidth remains low, inspect link errors and endpoint congestion control.

causalContracts.title: Worn NVMe device caused checkpoint write cliff
causalContracts.summary: Checkpoint latency degraded over weeks as the local NVMe reached a documented wear cliff; the later host-memory overlap/OOM is downstream of prolonged writes.
causalContracts.action: Drain the affected storage device/node under the hardware runbook, preserve SMART/latency evidence, replace or rebalance the worn NVMe, and verify sustained checkpoint writes before return.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If a healthy replacement shows the same latency, profile checkpoint serialization and backend queue depth.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the last complete checksum-verified checkpoint

causalContracts.title: Observed non-finite loss
causalContracts.summary: The submitted incident establishes the first non-finite loss/gradient state but does not by itself isolate the numeric or input source.
causalContracts.action: Replay the same batch with finite checks at preprocessing output, layer outputs, loss, and gradients; stop at the first non-finite tensor before changing optimizer settings.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the same batch is clean on replay, compare precision/loss-scaling and hardware telemetry as separate hypotheses.

causalContracts.title: Truncated CUDA out-of-memory exception

required.re: CUDA out of mem(?:ory)?|out of mem$

excluded.re: total capacity|GiB free|MiB free|allocated by PyTorch|already allocated

causalContracts.summary: The available fragment directly identifies a CUDA allocation failure, but truncation prevents distinguishing capacity, fragmentation, or another process owner.
causalContracts.action: Collect the complete exception plus per-process nvidia-smi memory and allocated/reserved values at failure, then choose the least disruptive capacity remedy supported by that evidence.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the complete log does not contain an allocation failure, treat this fragment as insufficient and locate the first full traceback.

causalContracts.title: Truncated NVIDIA Xid event
causalContracts.summary: The log proves that an NVIDIA Xid record began for the named PCI device, but the code and message are truncated, so its semantics are unknown.
causalContracts.action: Collect the complete timestamped NVRM line and nvidia-bug-report for the named PCI device. Do not drain, reset, or map it to a known Xid until the code and device evidence are present.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If no complete current Xid exists, keep the diagnosis at insufficient hardware signal and investigate the first full runtime error.

causalContracts.title: Checkpoint filesystem is full
causalContracts.summary: The checkpoint write failed with filesystem ENOSPC; progress rendering around it is not the causal owner.
causalContracts.action: Inspect filesystem capacity/quota/inodes, remove only approved expired artifacts through retention policy, and retry an atomic checkpoint after verifying headroom.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If capacity and quota are healthy, inspect deleted-open files and the backing storage service.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the last complete checkpoint before the failed temporary write

causalContracts.title: DDP reentrant checkpoint path marked a parameter ready twice

required.re: Expected to mark a variable ready only once|marked as ready twice
checkpoint\(\)[^\n]*(?:two|2) reentrant|two reentrant backward paths|removing the second wrapper completes

causalContracts.summary: Two reentrant activation-checkpoint paths fired autograd hooks for the same DDP parameter in one iteration. The duplicate-ready error is graph reuse, not an NCCL or GPU fault.
causalContracts.action: Wrap the block in only one checkpoint path or use the supported non-reentrant checkpoint mode. If the graph is invariant, `static_graph=True` is a bounded alternative. Verify block.3.weight is reached once per iteration and run a backward pass with `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL` before scaling out.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the error remains with a single non-reentrant checkpoint path, audit parameter use outside `forward` and overlapping forward/backward passes for the same DDP module.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the iteration after correcting the DDP graph; no checkpoint rollback is required

causalContracts.title: FSDP ranks used different parameter sets

required.re: Detected mismatch between collectives on ranks|CollectiveFingerPrint

causalContracts.summary: FSDP ranks produced different collective tensor sizes because the text-only rank skipped image_tower parameters while another rank used them. The collective mismatch is deterministic rank-conditional parameter usage.
causalContracts.action: Make image_tower parameter participation consistent across every FSDP rank: route a zero-weight/dummy image branch through text-only ranks or restructure the batch/mesh so the same parameter set participates. Verify rank 3 and rank 0 emit the same gradient/collective shapes with `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL` before the full run.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If parameter use is identical but shapes still differ, gather the branch token, parameter names, dtype, and collective shape from every rank at the first mismatched sequence.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart after the rank-consistent FSDP control flow is verified

causalContracts.title: TorchInductor BF16 target requires sm_80 or newer
causalContracts.summary: TorchInductor generated BF16 PTX for a T4 (sm_75), but that compiled path requires sm_80 or newer. Eager BF16 success localizes the failure to compiler target support, not general CUDA availability.
causalContracts.action: Capability-gate the compiled BF16 path: on sm_75 use eager execution or FP16, or run the compiled BF16 workload on sm_80+. Verify `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()` before enabling the path and rerun the same operation with and without `torch.compile`.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If a supported sm_80+ GPU still fails, capture the exact PyTorch/Triton/PTXAS versions and treat that as a separate compiler regression.

causalContracts.title: Installed PyTorch wheel lacks H100 sm_90 kernels

required.re: supports CUDA capabilities[^\n]*sm_86|current PyTorch installation[^\n]*not compatible

causalContracts.summary: The installed PyTorch binary contains kernels only through sm_86, while the selected H100 requires sm_90. The healthy device cannot execute a wheel that omitted its architecture.
causalContracts.action: Install a PyTorch/CUDA wheel that explicitly includes sm_90, or rebuild with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="9.0"`. Verify `torch.cuda.get_arch_list()` contains sm_90 and run a one-kernel smoke test on the H100 before relaunching.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If sm_90 is present after reinstall but launch still fails, compare the wheel CUDA runtime with the loaded driver and remove stale extension binaries built for the previous wheel.

causalContracts.title: vLLM AWQ-Marlin CUDA-graph replay failure
causalContracts.summary: The identical AWQ-Marlin request succeeds with graphs disabled and reproduces when CUDA graphs are re-enabled. That controlled A/B isolates vLLM graph capture/replay and exonerates the clean device.
causalContracts.action: Contain with `--enforce-eager`, then reproduce the same request on a canary and pin or upgrade the vLLM/AWQ-Marlin version containing the graph-path fix. Verify at least 500 identical requests in eager mode and again with the candidate CUDA-graph build before restoring graph execution.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If eager mode later fails on the same request, stop attributing the fault to graphs and inspect the quantization/backend kernel with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` on a canary.

causalContracts.title: vLLM SM120 FP4 MoE backend kernel fault
causalContracts.summary: The FP4 MoE failure persists without CUDA graphs and disappears when only the backend changes to Marlin. The evidenced owner is the SM120 FP4 backend kernel, not graph capture or GPU hardware.
causalContracts.action: Run the service with `--moe-backend=marlin` as containment, then upgrade or pin the FlashInfer/vLLM backend at the verified fix boundary. Replay the same request under eager and graph modes with Marlin and confirm both pass before reconsidering the failing FP4 backend.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If Marlin also fails, capture the first synchronized MoE GEMM stack and compare the exact SM120, CUDA, cuDNN, FlashInfer, and vLLM versions on a canary.

causalContracts.title: Transformers mismatch-ignore guard rejected a valid shape mismatch
causalContracts.summary: Checkpoint integrity passes, but the Transformers mismatch-ignore guard incorrectly applies quantized-weight logic to a non-quantized tensor. The evidenced owner is loader mismatch handling; checkpoint integrity is verified.
causalContracts.action: Upgrade to the Transformers release containing the `_find_mismatched_keys` guard fix or apply that narrow patch. Confirm the configured mask_projection shape is intentional, load with `ignore_mismatched_sizes=True`, and verify the loader reports that exact skipped tensor before a forward smoke test.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If loading still fails after the guard fix, compare the model config and state-dict keys/shapes; do not delete or roll back a checkpoint whose checksum and safetensors validation pass.

causalContracts.title: NVIDIA Kubernetes plugin cannot inspect mixed-MIG devices
causalContracts.summary: The mixed-MIG device plugin registered its resources but lacked permission to inspect MIG device 5 during preferred allocation. Enabling MIG monitor visibility makes the same Pod admit.
causalContracts.action: Set `NVIDIA_MIG_MONITOR_DEVICES=all` on the NVIDIA device-plugin DaemonSet and perform a controlled rollout. Verify the plugin re-registers full-GPU and MIG resources, then use `kubectl describe pod` to confirm the same full-GPU Pod is admitted before changing GPU topology.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If allocation still fails, inspect the effective DaemonSet environment, NVML visibility, plugin version, and kubelet device-plugin socket without replacing the GPUs.

causalContracts.title: Classifier head shape differs from the verified checkpoint
causalContracts.summary: The checkpoint is intact; the current classifier has one additional output row because the configured class count changed after training.
causalContracts.action: Set `num_labels`/the class mapping to the checkpoint value, or intentionally initialize a new 1001-class head while loading the compatible backbone weights. Verify the loaded state-dict shapes and run a 1001-class forward/loss smoke test before training.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the class count was not intentionally changed, diff the exact model config and label mapping against the producer manifest before loading again.

causalContracts.title: DDP ready-twice symptom needs graph ownership evidence

required.re: Expected to mark a variable ready only once|marked as ready twice

excluded.re: checkpoint\(\)[^\n]*(?:two|2) reentrant|two reentrant backward paths|removing the second wrapper completes

causalContracts.summary: DDP proves that one parameter fired multiple ready hooks, but the log does not distinguish reentrant checkpoint reuse, parameter use outside forward, or overlapping forward/backward passes.
causalContracts.action: Collect the parameter name and graph path with `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL`; inventory activation-checkpoint wrappers, parameter access outside `forward`, and concurrent forward/backward passes. Test one change at a time, using `static_graph=True` only if the graph is invariant.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the duplicate hook persists after removing reentrant reuse, reduce to one DDP module and one forward/backward to isolate the second hook registration.

causalContracts.title: CUDA illegal access needs a graph/kernel/device discriminator

required.re: CUDA error: an illegal memory access|illegal memory access was encountered

causalContracts.summary: An illegal-access terminal symptom is present, but the evidence does not identify whether the owner is CUDA-graph replay, a backend/custom kernel, invalid input, or a device event.
causalContracts.action: Reproduce the same request on a canary with `--enforce-eager` and `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, then run the smallest failing kernel under compute-sanitizer. Collect current Xid/ECC output; choose an owner only after one of those tests discriminates it.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the crash does not reproduce, preserve the request shape, model/backend versions, and first synchronized stack rather than assigning hardware ownership.

causalContracts.title: Cross-node causal order is unresolved without clock alignment

required.re: separate unsynchronized host journals|clock offsets are unknown

causalContracts.summary: The CUDA and NCCL events came from different unsynchronized clocks. Their displayed wall times cannot prove which event happened first, so patient zero remains unresolved.
causalContracts.action: Collect `chronyc tracking`/source offsets from both hosts or align the events with a shared scheduler/controller timestamp, monotonic Flight Recorder sequence, or another common clock domain. Do not change NCCL or hardware state until ordering is established.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If clock alignment is unavailable, report both causal branches and gather the first per-rank process exit plus kernel/device events from the same host clock.

causalContracts.title: GPU hardware counters are explicitly clean
causalContracts.summary: No hardware fault is evidenced: uncorrectable ECC and row-remap counters are zero, no Xid is present, and DCGM passes. The application log is incomplete.
causalContracts.action: Take no GPU action. Collect the failing application rank’s first exception and incident-window logs; preserve these zero-valued counters as explicit negative evidence.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If a new non-zero device event appears in the same incident window, diagnose that literal event separately.

causalContracts.title: Compiler warning fell back successfully
causalContracts.summary: No incident occurred. torch.compile reported a graph break, successfully fell back for that frame, and the run completed with finite loss and a verified checkpoint.
causalContracts.action: No remediation or restart is required. Track graph breaks only as a performance optimization if they materially affect throughput.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If a later run actually fails, submit its terminal stack separately rather than treating this successful warning as the cause.

causalContracts.title: Opaque attachment has no usable diagnostic evidence
causalContracts.summary: The attachment cannot be interpreted and contains no plaintext error or terminal marker. No failure family can be assigned from this evidence.
causalContracts.action: Provide the attachment with its media type or decode it to plaintext, then collect the first error line and the surrounding incident window.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If decoding is impossible, supply the emitting tool, filename/format, and a textual export from the original system.

causalContracts.title: Rank-zero-only TensorBoard gradient logging deadlocks Horovod collectives
causalContracts.summary: TensorBoard gradient or weight logging is evaluating an optimizer-gradient all-reduce on only rank 0. Horovod therefore reports the matching operations as missing the other ranks; the collective timeout is collateral to rank-asymmetric callback execution.
causalContracts.action: Either disable TensorBoard gradient/weight histogram collection, or invoke that callback on every Horovod rank and give each rank a distinct log directory so every rank submits the same gradient collectives. Log the ordered collective names per rank and replay through the first histogram interval; require no missing-rank warning and no event-file collision.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If every rank already executes the same callback and ordered collective list, withdraw this attribution. Compare per-rank control flow, batch counts, and the first mismatched tensor name before changing NCCL or fabric settings.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the epoch or failed step after one histogram interval completes with identical collective order on every rank

causalContracts.title: MLflow async artifact worker blocks process exit without a deadline
causalContracts.summary: The training work has finished, but MLflow process teardown is waiting without a deadline for an async artifact worker blocked in upload or status I/O. This is logger shutdown, not a training collective or GPU hang.
causalContracts.action: Contain by disabling MLflow async logging (`mlflow.config.enable_async_logging(False)`) for the affected job or by logging critical artifacts synchronously. Upgrade to a release containing bounded async-artifact shutdown, set an artifact upload/download timeout, then inject a blocked endpoint and require the process to return a visible terminal logging error within the job grace period.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the main thread is not in MLflow atexit/join/shutdown code, preserve all thread stacks and withdraw this owner; locate the actual non-daemon thread or distributed rank preventing exit.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart from the last verified training checkpoint; separately reconcile any artifact whose upload did not receive a success acknowledgement

causalContracts.title: MLflow retries an empty artifact root as a file download

required.re: empty (?:root|artifact_path|artifact path)[^\n]{0,160}(?:download thread|HTTP retr(?:y|ies)|treated as a file)

causalContracts.summary: The requested run has an empty artifact root, but the client treats the empty path as a file and enters download retries. The hang is an MLflow empty-root handling defect, not object-store throughput or training health.
causalContracts.action: Before downloading, list the run artifact root and return an empty destination immediately when the listing is empty. Upgrade to a release that handles the empty root before spawning download workers, set a bounded download timeout, and verify both an empty run and a one-file control return correctly.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the root listing contains an object, withdraw the empty-root attribution and capture the exact object URI, HTTP status/retry reason, client/server versions, and a direct authenticated object read.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: continue the consumer after the empty run returns normally, or retry from the first artifact whose checksum-backed download failed

causalContracts.title: W&B run in a Python subprocess waits for teardown that never executes
causalContracts.summary: The W&B run is owned by a multiprocessing child whose normal atexit cleanup is not completing; the explicit `wandb.finish()` control makes the child terminate. This is tracker lifecycle ownership, not a GPU or collective stall.
causalContracts.action: Wrap each subprocess-owned run in `try/finally` and call `wandb.finish()` in that same child. Keep one run owner per process, then verify normal completion, an injected training exception, and SIGTERM all finish or fail within the scheduler grace period without losing the final acknowledged step.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If explicit finish also blocks, capture the W&B internal/debug logs and every child thread stack, test `WANDB_MODE=disabled` on the identical job, and keep the tracker-versus-network owners open.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume training from its checkpoint only after the prior run is marked terminal or assigned a new explicit run identity

causalContracts.title: TensorBoard foreground writer blocks behind a dead background writer
causalContracts.summary: TensorBoard’s background EventFileWriter died after a storage/write exception while the foreground producer filled its queue and waited forever. The original writer exception is the initiating fault; the apparent training hang is downstream backpressure.
causalContracts.action: Upgrade to a TensorBoard build containing the EventFileWriter exception-propagation fix from PR 6168 (or backport it), and preserve the original filesystem exception. Inject a failing record writer and require `add_event`/`flush` to raise promptly; then verify free space, quota, permissions, and a clean event-file write/read before re-enabling logging.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the background writer is alive and the queue is draining, withdraw this dead-writer attribution and profile event volume, filesystem latency, and producer logging rate before enlarging the queue.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the last training checkpoint after a new event file accepts and flushes a sentinel record; do not append to a possibly truncated file

causalContracts.title: Slurm drains a node whose detected GPU inventory contradicts GRES configuration

required.re: fewer resources than configured|Gres count (?:too low|mismatch)|not all system-detected devices|GPU count[^\n]{0,80}(?:configured|detected)[^\n]{0,40}(?:mismatch|differ)

causalContracts.summary: Slurmd’s detected GPU inventory does not satisfy the GRES count or identity declared to slurmctld, so Slurm intentionally drains the node. This is scheduler inventory configuration, not evidence that an allocated GPU failed during training.
causalContracts.action: Keep the node drained. Run `slurmd -G` to print ignored/mismatched GRES and `slurmd -C` to capture detected identities; reconcile `slurm.conf` Gres count/type with `gres.conf` File/Type/AutoDetect and the physical/MIG inventory. Restart/reconfigure the daemons, then require the node to register the expected GRES before clearing drain.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If configured and detected inventory match exactly, withdraw this owner and inspect the full node reason plus slurmd registration logs for CPU, memory, topology, or daemon-version rejection.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: requeue the job only after `scontrol show node` reports the intended GRES inventory and a one-GPU allocation resolves to the expected device

causalContracts.title: FlashAttention receives query and key tensors with different dtypes

required.re: RuntimeError:[^\n]*query and key must have the same dtype

causalContracts.summary: The attention kernel is called with query and key tensors in different dtypes; the explicit runtime invariant failure is the initiating fault, not evaluation memory retention or GPU hardware.
causalContracts.action: At the attention call site, cast query, key, and value to one supported dtype (for this trace, keep all three FP16 under the same autocast context) before invoking FlashAttention. Verify their dtype/device/shape immediately before `_flash_attention_forward`, then replay the identical generation request.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If query/key/value already match at the kernel boundary, switch the identical request to the eager/SDPA attention backend. Eager-only success localizes a FlashAttention integration/version fault; failure in both modes falsifies that owner and requires the next earlier stack frame.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: retry the failed generation request after dtype parity is asserted at the attention boundary

causalContracts.title: The attention kernel was handed a tensor whose last dimension is not contiguous

required.re: must have the last dimension contiguous|Input tensor must have contiguous last dimension|only support(?:s)? contiguous inputs|expected contiguous tensor|input is not contiguous|tensor is not contiguous

causalContracts.summary: The attention kernel requires a stride-1 innermost dimension and received a view whose last dimension is strided, typically the result of a transpose, a permute, a slice, or a head reshape that was never materialised. This is a tensor-layout invariant at the call site, not a container image fault and not GPU degradation.
causalContracts.action: Materialise the layout immediately before the attention call: `q = q.contiguous(); k = k.contiguous(); v = v.contiguous()`. Print `q.stride()`, `k.stride()` and `v.stride()` on the line before the kernel and require the last element of each to be 1, then replay the identical request. If a transpose feeds the call, prefer reshaping once outside the training loop rather than calling `.contiguous()` per step, because the copy is not free.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If all three tensors already report a stride of 1 in the last dimension at the kernel boundary, withdraw this owner. Run the same request through the eager or SDPA math backend: success there localises a FlashAttention integration fault, and failure in both falsifies the layout hypothesis and moves the question to the next earlier frame.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: retry the failed step or request once the innermost stride is asserted at the attention boundary

causalContracts.title: The attention kernel does not support this head dimension

required.re: head dimension at most \d+|head dim(?:ension)?[^\n]{0,40}(?:not supported|unsupported)|head_dim must be\s*<=|unsupported head (?:size|dim(?:ension)?)\s*\d+|does not support head size

causalContracts.summary: The model head dimension falls outside the set the selected attention kernel was compiled for. The kernel is refusing an unsupported shape, which is a build-time capability limit rather than a runtime fault, so retrying, resizing the batch or moving the job to another node changes nothing.
causalContracts.action: Pad the head dimension to a value the kernel supports, normally 64, 128 or 256, with `torch.nn.functional.pad` on query, key and value and slice the output back. Confirm the padded size against the kernel documentation for the exact version in use before assuming a value is supported. If padding is not acceptable, select a backend that supports the native head size, for example the SDPA math backend or the eager attention path.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the reported head dimension is already inside the supported set, withdraw this owner: the message then belongs to a version skew between the compiled kernel and the installed package, so compare the attention package version against the CUDA and PyTorch tuple before changing the model shape.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: retry the failed request after the head dimension is padded or a supporting backend is selected

causalContracts.title: The Triton kernel asks for more shared memory than the device provides

required.re: out of resource:\s*shared memory|OutOfResources[^\n]{0,120}shared memory|shared memory limit exceeded|Required:\s*\d+[^\n]{0,60}Hardware limit:\s*\d+

excluded.re: torch\.cuda\.OutOfMemoryError|CUDA out of memory[^\n]{0,80}Tried to allocate

causalContracts.summary: The compiled Triton kernel requests more per-block shared memory than the target architecture exposes, so the launch is rejected before any work runs. The limit is a property of the device and the chosen tile shape, not of how much free GPU memory is available, which is why the failure reproduces on an otherwise idle GPU.
causalContracts.action: Reduce the tile so the working set fits: lower BLOCK_M and BLOCK_N in the kernel configuration, or lower num_stages, which multiplies the shared memory the software pipeline holds. The error prints both the required and the hardware limit, so divide the required figure by the limit to size the reduction rather than guessing. If the kernel is autotuned, prune the configuration list to the shapes that fit the target architecture.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the tile is already at its smallest useful size, withdraw the tuning remedy and pin the workload to an architecture with a larger shared-memory budget, or select a non-Triton implementation of the same operation. Confirm the device limit with `nvidia-smi -q` and the reported architecture before concluding the kernel cannot be made to fit.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: retry the failed step once the kernel launches with a configuration inside the device shared-memory limit

causalContracts.title: Blackwell reports an NVLink fault as Xid 149 with a NETIR subcode, and the degraded marking is sticky
causalContracts.summary: On B100, B200 and GB200 the driver reports NVLink faults as Xid 149 with a NETIR subcode rather than as the Xid 74 seen on earlier generations, so a fleet rule written for Xid 74 does not fire and the fault reads as a generic GPU error. The second half matters more: once the driver marks a GPU degraded it stays out of the NVLink domain until it is reset, and that marking survives a reboot. A clean nvidia-smi afterwards is therefore not evidence that the fault cleared, it is the expected output of a GPU that is still excluded.
causalContracts.action: Confirm the link state directly rather than inferring it from a clean health summary: run `nvidia-smi nvlink -s` on the affected GPU and require every expected link to report active. If any link is inactive, reset the GPU rather than rebooting the host, because the degraded marking is cleared by the reset and not by the reboot. Re-run the link check after the reset and only return the node to the pool once the full NVLink domain is present. Record the NETIR subcode from the Xid 149 line with the incident, since it is what distinguishes a link event from a link-down.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the links come back active and the fault returns on the same GPU, capture the Xid 149 line with its full hex payload and escalate to the vendor with the NETIR subcode and the link number. Do not raise an RMA on the degraded marking alone: the marking is the driver excluding a link, not a verdict on the silicon, and it is also produced by cable and backplane faults on the peer side.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the last checkpoint once the affected GPU reports every NVLink link active after a reset

causalContracts.title: A fatal NVSwitch SXid aborted the jobs, and the Xid on the GPU is its consequence
causalContracts.summary: The initiating event is on the NVSwitch, not on a GPU. Fabric Manager reports switch faults as SXid, and a fatal SXid on a GPU-to-NVSwitch port aborts the CUDA jobs on that GPU and commonly surfaces as Xid 74 and Xid 45 on the GPU a moment later. Reading the Xid as the cause points the remedy at a card that did nothing wrong. A fatal SXid on a port between GPU baseboards is worse: Fabric Manager aborts every job in the partition and blocks new launches, so the cluster looks like it is refusing work for no reason.
causalContracts.action: Read the severity and the port from the SXid line before touching anything, because the three cases have different remedies. A non-fatal SXid is informational and Fabric Manager keeps jobs running, so record it and move on. For a fatal SXid, stop Fabric Manager and stop every GPU application first, then reset all GPUs and NVSwitches together with `nvidia-smi -r`, which resets the whole set. Do not reset a single device with `-i` here: a fabric that is half reset stays out of service and the symptom returns on the next launch. Restart Fabric Manager and require a clean start before scheduling work.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the fault persists after a full reset, power cycle the affected baseboard during an approved window. If it survives that, escalate with the SXid number, the link number and the Fabric Manager log rather than with the GPU Xid, since the Xid is downstream of the switch event and describes the wrong component.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the last checkpoint once Fabric Manager restarts clean and the partition accepts a new launch

causalContracts.title: GB200 NVL72 driver hang with Xid 150 and 154 is an uptime-linked firmware defect
causalContracts.summary: This signature clusters by uptime rather than by workload or by individual card, which is the tell that it is firmware and not silicon. On GB200 NVL72 racks running R580 or later drivers, NVLink task scheduling can hang the driver after roughly sixty days of continuous uptime and emit Xid 150 and Xid 154. The defect is an overflow in the NVLink management microcode carried in the vBIOS, so a replacement card fails the same way once it reaches the same uptime, and a fleet can lose several cards to RMA before anyone notices the pattern.
causalContracts.action: Before treating any card as faulty, record the node uptime and the vBIOS version and check them against the DGX GB200 NVL72 release notes, because the fix ships as firmware. Apply the firmware release containing the NVLink management microcode overflow fix. If cards were already pulled, re-test them after the update rather than assuming they are bad. Until the fleet is updated, correlate incidents against uptime so the reboot is scheduled ahead of the threshold instead of arriving as an outage.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the uptime correlation does not hold across the fleet, or the racks are already on a firmware release that carries the fix, withdraw this owner and treat the Xid 150 and 154 pair as an ordinary NVLink fault: capture the link state and escalate with the driver and vBIOS versions attached.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the last checkpoint after the node is rebooted, and schedule the firmware update rather than repeating the reboot

causalContracts.title: Index tensor and indexed tensor are on different devices

required.re: RuntimeError:[^\n]*indices should be either on cpu or on the same device as the indexed tensor
indexed tensor\s*\((?:cpu|cuda(?::\d+)?)\)|same device as the indexed tensor

causalContracts.summary: The index operation receives indices on a device that differs from the indexed tensor; this tensor-placement contract is the direct initiating fault.
causalContracts.action: Move the indices/input_ids to the indexed tensor’s device immediately before the failing lookup (`indices = indices.to(indexed_tensor.device)`), or keep both on CPU if that table is intentionally CPU-resident. Log both `.device` values at the failing line and replay the identical input.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If both values already report the same device at the failing line, inspect model sharding/device-map hooks for a post-check move and reduce the lookup outside generation before changing placement policy.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: retry the failed generation request after the index/tensor device invariant is asserted

causalContracts.title: Containerd upgrade breaks NVIDIA device-plugin strategy discovery

required.re: Incompatible strategy detected\s+auto|No devices found[^\n]*Waiting indefinitely

causalContracts.summary: GPU discovery regresses only after the containerd 2.0 transition and returns with 1.7, isolating the device-plugin/runtime strategy compatibility boundary.
causalContracts.action: Contain by pinning containerd 1.7 with the currently deployed NVIDIA device plugin/toolkit, or upgrade the plugin/toolkit to a release explicitly compatible with containerd 2.0 and regenerate the runtime configuration. Restart containerd and the device-plugin DaemonSet, then require node Capacity to advertise the expected `nvidia.com/gpu` count.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If GPU capacity remains absent on the known-good 1.7 tuple, withdraw the version attribution and inspect the plugin pod logs, configured containerd socket, runtime class, and toolkit hook paths.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: reschedule GPU pods only after every affected node advertises stable GPU capacity

causalContracts.title: NCCL/PyTorch version tuple multiplies CUDA-graph capture memory
causalContracts.summary: The same graph-capture workload increases from roughly 10 MB to more than 100 MB per graph across the PyTorch/NCCL version change, selecting a version-tuple capture-memory regression.
causalContracts.action: Contain by pinning the known-good PyTorch 2.1/NCCL 2.18 tuple or disabling CUDA graphs. Bisect PyTorch and NCCL independently with the identical capture set, measuring reserved and allocated bytes before and after each graph; promote only a tuple whose per-graph delta returns to the baseline.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the old tuple also shows the larger delta on identical inputs, withdraw the version attribution and compare graph count, captured shapes, allocator settings, and retained graph pools.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart graph capture from a clean process after the selected tuple stays within the measured memory budget

causalContracts.title: NCCL reduce requires a valid receive buffer on every rank for this build

required.re: valid recvbuffer[^\n]*(?:every|all) rank|recvbuffer[^\n]*not only the root

causalContracts.summary: The affected reduce path hangs when non-root ranks omit a receive buffer; the maintainer workaround and fixed build identify the collective API/version contract.
causalContracts.action: Pass a valid receive buffer on every rank (not only the root) for the affected NCCL build, or upgrade to a release containing commit `8e1d6f9`. Replay reduce at 2, 3, and the production GPU count and require identical completion plus correct root output.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the fixed build with valid per-rank receive buffers still hangs, capture the first stalled collective sequence and topology; do not keep attributing the failure to this legacy buffer contract.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the failed collective/job after the corrected buffer contract passes at production world size

causalContracts.title: FSDP-wrapped module compute bypasses nn.Module.forward

required.re: weight should have at least three dimensions

causalContracts.summary: Calling a non-forward method directly on an FSDP-wrapped child bypasses FSDP’s forward boundary, so parameters are not all-gathered before compute.
causalContracts.action: Route the VisionTransformer computation through the wrapped module’s `forward()` method (or expose `forward_features` from inside that forward) so FSDP owns the parameter all-gather. Verify parameter shapes inside the call and run one forward/backward at the production shard policy.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the call already crosses the wrapped `forward()` boundary, inspect the autowrap boundary and parameter ownership to find which child is executing with local shards.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the failed iteration after the wrapped forward path completes one forward/backward

causalContracts.title: Distributed checkpoint API does not support the FSDP local-shard state-dict path
causalContracts.summary: The selected distributed-checkpoint state-dict API does not implement this custom local-shard process-group layout, while the full-state path succeeds.
causalContracts.action: Use the supported `FULL_STATE_DICT` path as containment (rank-0-only plus CPU offload where appropriate), or upgrade to a PyTorch release that implements local-shard checkpointing for this HYBRID_SHARD layout. Verify a save/load round trip with the same process groups and compare parameter checksums.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If FULL_STATE_DICT also fails, preserve the original shards and compare the producer/consumer world size, shard process groups, and optimizer state ownership before conversion.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the first checkpoint that passes the same-layout save/load checksum test

causalContracts.title: Ray fractional workers share the same CUDA visibility assignment
causalContracts.summary: Fractional Ray workers are inheriting the same CUDA visibility assignment; the supplied scheduler control targets that sharing behavior directly.
causalContracts.action: Set `TRAIN_ENABLE_SHARE_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` in every Ray Train worker before startup and explicitly establish the intended `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` mapping. Log PID, Ray worker ID, visible devices, and CUDA ordinal per worker, then verify no two exclusive ranks resolve to the same physical GPU.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If workers still share a physical GPU with sharing disabled, inspect placement-group bundles and the scheduler’s fractional resource policy rather than modifying NCCL.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart all workers after the corrected visibility map is verified before process-group initialization

causalContracts.title: vLLM frontend remains healthy after Ray worker death
causalContracts.summary: vLLM 0.8.3 fails to propagate Ray worker death to frontend liveness, leaving requests queued until a later trigger; the same behavior is fixed in 0.8.5.
causalContracts.action: Upgrade/pin vLLM to 0.8.5 or newer and make frontend readiness fail immediately when any required Ray worker dies. Kill one worker in a canary and verify readiness drops, in-flight requests terminate with a bounded error, and the supervisor restarts the service.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If 0.8.5 still stays ready after worker death, inspect the deployed image/version and Ray actor-death subscription; keep the external health check tied to worker quorum as containment.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: retry only idempotent requests after worker quorum and readiness recover; replay non-idempotent work from its application checkpoint

causalContracts.title: vLLM version tuple regresses tensor-parallel engine startup
causalContracts.summary: The identical host/model works on vLLM 0.11.0 and at TP=1 but fails at TP=2 on the 0.11.1 tuple, isolating a tensor-parallel version regression.
causalContracts.action: Pin vLLM 0.11.0 or the known-good commit `250fb1b8ea836ab4cdd2890581815a9c19b8b8ed`, then bisect vLLM separately from the torch/NCCL tuple. Verify TP=2 startup and a representative collective/request soak before promoting.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the known-good commit also fails on the identical image, withdraw the vLLM-version attribution and compare torch/NCCL binaries, rank mapping, and shared-memory transport.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart EngineCore and retry requests after the TP=2 canary completes successfully

causalContracts.title: Requested vLLM KV-cache block size has no supported common layout
causalContracts.summary: The selected KV-cache block size is accepted by the CLI but has no common backend layout; the identical configuration starts with block size 16.
causalContracts.action: Set `--block-size 16` for this model/backend tuple and rebuild the KV cache from a clean process. Verify initialization, available KV blocks, representative prompt lengths, and one sustained serving soak before rollout.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If block size 16 fails on the identical model, capture the backend, dtype, cache layout, and complete initialization error; do not delete tokenizer/model caches for this allocator-layout failure.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the serving process with an empty in-memory KV cache; model weights do not require rollback

causalContracts.title: vLLM shared-memory broadcast timeout has conflicting transport controls

required.re: No available shared memory broadcast block found[^\n]*60 seconds
reports disagree|no single controlled owner|changes the hang

causalContracts.summary: The shared-memory broadcast is timing out, but the supplied P2P, custom-all-reduce, and container-SHM observations do not isolate one causal owner.
causalContracts.action: Run three identical single-variable controls: measure `/dev/shm` capacity/usage, toggle custom all-reduce only, then toggle NCCL P2P only. Capture every worker stack and the first blocked broadcast block ID at 60 seconds; keep confidence below the action threshold until exactly one control removes the timeout.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If no single control changes the result, inspect worker liveness and producer/consumer progress for the named shared-memory block before changing transport or allocating more SHM.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the serving workers only after one controlled configuration completes the same request soak

causalContracts.title: DDP cannot discover tensors in a custom forward return

required.re: Expected to have finished reduction|parameters? that were not used|did not receive grad
could not locate the output tensors|forward returned Custom\w+|custom (?:return|container|object)

causalContracts.summary: DDP cannot traverse the custom forward return to discover the tensors that participate in loss, so its unused-parameter reduction bookkeeping is incomplete.
causalContracts.action: Return loss-participating tensors in a DDP-discoverable standard structure (tensor/list/tuple/dict), or make the custom container expose those tensors before backward. Re-run with `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL` and verify every reported parameter index either receives a gradient or is intentionally unused.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the standard return structure still fails, map the named parameter indices to modules and verify the returned tensors actually contribute to the loss.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the failed iteration after correcting the forward return contract

causalContracts.title: Multiple DDP forwards create duplicate unused-parameter traversal

required.re: Expected to mark a variable ready only once|marked as ready twice

causalContracts.summary: Two forwards through the same DDP wrapper create overlapping unused-parameter graph traversals before one combined backward, so one parameter-ready hook fires twice.
causalContracts.action: Move both computations and their loss aggregation inside one DDP wrapper forward so each iteration has one graph traversal. Keep find_unused_parameters=True only if parameters are genuinely conditional, then verify the graph traversal and ready-hook sequence with TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If a single wrapper forward still marks a parameter twice, inspect reentrant checkpointing and parameter use outside forward before enabling static_graph.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the failed iteration after the DDP forward boundary is corrected

causalContracts.title: Reentrant activation checkpoint conflicts with DDP autograd.grad

required.re: Expected to mark a variable ready only once|marked as ready twice

causalContracts.summary: The reentrant checkpoint path and `autograd.grad` register an unsupported duplicate DDP-ready path; removing checkpointing makes the same gradient computation pass.
causalContracts.action: Use the supported non-reentrant checkpoint path (`use_reentrant=False`) or remove the overlapping checkpoint wrapper for this graph. Keep the `autograd.grad` call unchanged for the A/B, then verify one forward/backward with `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL` before scaling out.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the duplicate-ready hook remains without reentrant checkpointing, inspect parameter use outside `forward` and overlapping forward/backward passes.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the failed iteration; checkpoint data is not implicated

causalContracts.title: Shared parameter is reached by multiple reentrant checkpoint paths

required.re: Expected to mark a variable ready only once|marked as ready twice

causalContracts.summary: Multiple reentrant checkpoint paths reach the same named DDP parameter and fire its ready hook more than once in one iteration.
causalContracts.action: Use one checkpoint owner for the shared block or switch every overlapping wrapper to `use_reentrant=False`. If the topology is truly invariant, `static_graph=True` is a bounded alternative. Verify the named shared parameter is reached once per iteration with `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL`.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the graph is not invariant, do not use static_graph; restructure the shared branch so one DDP forward owns the combined loss.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the iteration after correcting the graph; no checkpoint rollback is required

causalContracts.title: DDP static-graph promise is contradicted by changing parameter use
causalContracts.summary: Parameter participation changes between iterations, directly violating DDP’s `static_graph=True` contract.
