causalContracts.action: Disable `static_graph` and use `find_unused_parameters=True`, or make the conditional branch participate consistently on every rank and iteration. Verify the parameter set across at least two branch-changing iterations with `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL`.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If parameter participation is stable after the change, re-evaluate static_graph only after a multi-iteration trace proves the invariant.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart after the DDP graph contract is corrected

causalContracts.title: FSDP flattened checkpoint is interpreted by an incompatible runtime
causalContracts.summary: The intact FSDP checkpoint contains a flattened parameter representation that the current runtime interprets as an unflattened tensor shape.
causalContracts.action: Load with the PyTorch/FSDP version containing the state-dict compatibility fix, or convert the checkpoint once with a version that understands its flattened format. Preserve the checksum-verified source and verify one save/load round trip before resuming.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the compatible runtime still fails, compare the producer’s FSDP state-dict type, world size, and wrap policy against the consumer.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the checksum-verified checkpoint after a successful compatibility load

causalContracts.title: CUDA extension exports conflicting CUB symbols
causalContracts.summary: A CUDA extension exports colliding CUB symbols; the extension load A/B and namespaced rebuild isolate an ABI/symbol fault rather than invalid data or GPU hardware.
causalContracts.action: Rebuild the extension with an isolated CUB namespace (for example `CUB_WRAPPED_NAMESPACE`) and ensure its CUDA/PyTorch ABI matches the runtime. Inspect exported symbols with `nm -D`, then repeat the same tensor test with the rebuilt extension.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the namespaced build still fails, minimize the extension call under compute-sanitizer and compare the exact CUDA/PyTorch build tuple.

causalContracts.title: Inductor emits a bounds assert for an input proven valid in other modes
causalContracts.summary: The same bounded indices pass eager CUDA and compiled CPU, while Inductor’s dynamic CUDA path asserts during generated-kernel autotuning. This is a compiler analysis/codegen regression.
causalContracts.action: Contain by running this path eagerly or disabling dynamic compilation, then test a PyTorch/Inductor build containing the fix. Preserve a minimal reproducer with the symbolic sizes and generated kernel; verify eager and compiled outputs agree before restoring compilation.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If eager CUDA also fails on the identical input, withdraw the compiler attribution and validate the index-producing data path.

causalContracts.title: Loss kernel receives a target outside its class range
causalContracts.summary: The submitted loss targets violate the generated kernel explicit class bound, and eager execution rejects the same values; compilation is collateral, not the owner.
causalContracts.action: Validate the target range before nll_loss or cross-entropy (0 <= target < 10 for the submitted ten-class input), repair the label-generation path, and replay the exact batch on CPU or with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1. Restart the worker before the CUDA replay because a device assert poisons the process context.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If every target in the exact batch is in range, preserve that batch and compare eager versus compiled execution before assigning an input-data fault.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the failed batch in a fresh worker after correcting the invalid targets

causalContracts.title: CUDA index or class label is outside the legal range

required.re: index out of bounds|Class values must be smaller|target[^\n]*(?:max|min|randint)|labels?\.max|num_classes|num_embeddings

causalContracts.summary: The kernel assertion and submitted bounds values identify an out-of-range index/class label; later CUDA errors may be sticky fallout from the poisoned process context.
causalContracts.action: Validate token/target/label bounds before the operation (`0 <= index < size`, class value `< num_classes`, token id `< num_embeddings`). Re-run the exact batch on CPU or with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, fix the first invalid value, then restart the worker process to clear the asserted CUDA context.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If every submitted index is proven in range, reduce the operation and compare eager versus compiled execution before assigning an input fault.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the failed batch in a fresh worker after correcting the invalid input

causalContracts.title: Compiled CUDA kernel is incompatible with the loaded runtime/driver tuple

required.re: Triton Error \[CUDA\]: device kernel image is invalid|device kernel image is invalid

causalContracts.summary: Only generated kernels fail, and the submitted build/runtime versions are not a qualified tuple; eager execution and a matched image pass.
causalContracts.action: Use a PyTorch/CUDA/Triton image qualified with the loaded driver, or update the driver to support the wheel’s CUDA runtime. Keep eager fallback (or disable compilation) as containment and verify a compiled one-kernel smoke test in the final image.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the exact matched tuple still fails, capture `torch.version.cuda`, driver version, target architecture, Triton version, and generated PTX for a compiler reproducer.

causalContracts.title: Triton cannot find a working ptxas executable

required.re: working version could not be found|searched in TRITON_PTXAS_PATH|ptxas[^\n]*not found

causalContracts.summary: TorchInductor cannot find a working `ptxas` in its configured search paths, so compilation stops before any device kernel executes.
causalContracts.action: Install a compatible CUDA toolkit/ptxas and expose it through `TRITON_PTXAS_PATH` or the container `PATH`. Verify `ptxas --version` inside the final runtime and run a one-operation `torch.compile` smoke test.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If ptxas is present but rejected, compare its supported PTX ISA/SM targets with the Triton-generated target.

causalContracts.title: Compiler environment has no resolved CUDA toolkit root

required.re: expected str, bytes or os\.PathLike object, not NoneType

causalContracts.summary: The failing compiler environment has no CUDA toolkit root, while the same compile succeeds where `CUDA_HOME` resolves.
causalContracts.action: Use a complete CUDA development image or set `CUDA_HOME` to the actual mounted toolkit root and ensure `bin/ptxas` plus headers/libraries exist there. Verify the resolved path inside the final container with a compiled smoke test.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If CUDA_HOME resolves but the build fails, inspect the next concrete compiler/loader error rather than the old NoneType stack.

causalContracts.title: Triton toolchain does not support the requested GPU target/instruction
causalContracts.summary: The compiler/assembler explicitly rejects the requested SM target or generated instruction; this is toolchain target support, not GPU degradation.
causalContracts.action: Install a newer compatible CUDA toolkit/ptxas/PyTorch/Triton tuple whose PTX ISA version explicitly supports the reported target (for this signature, PTX .version 7.4 must be replaced by a version that supports sm_89). Disable the unsupported compiled path as containment and verify the exact SM target with a minimal JIT kernel.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If a supported toolchain still rejects one generated instruction, pin/disable that kernel and file the reduced PTX/codegen reproducer upstream.

causalContracts.title: Weights-only loader lacks an opcode from the selected pickle protocol
causalContracts.summary: The checkpoint is intact, but the weights-only unpickler does not implement an opcode emitted by pickle protocol 4.
causalContracts.action: Prefer a PyTorch release whose weights-only loader supports the protocol, or re-save from a trusted source/environment using a supported protocol. Keep `weights_only=True` for untrusted artifacts; do not use `weights_only=False` merely to bypass this security boundary.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: Only for a checkpoint whose producer and contents are fully trusted, isolate any legacy conversion in a sandbox and emit a new weights-only-compatible artifact.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the checksum-matching checkpoint after safe format conversion

causalContracts.title: Checkpoint producer format requires an explicit model conversion
causalContracts.summary: The checksum-verified artifact is in its producer’s native layout and must be converted to the consumer model’s state-dict schema.
causalContracts.action: Run the official model-specific conversion script in a pinned environment, record the producer/config versions, and validate the converted state shapes plus a forward smoke test. Preserve the original artifact and checksum.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the converted artifact still mismatches, compare model variant, hidden size, vocabulary, and config identity before changing weights.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the converted, validated checkpoint

causalContracts.title: Cache state violates activation-checkpoint recomputation metadata

required.re: CheckpointError[^\n]*different metadata|recomputed values have different metadata

causalContracts.summary: Generation cache state changes tensor metadata between the original forward and activation-checkpoint recomputation.
causalContracts.action: Set `use_cache=False` whenever gradient/activation checkpointing is enabled, then repeat forward/backward and confirm recomputed tensor metadata matches. Keep cache enabled only for inference paths without checkpoint recomputation.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If metadata still changes with cache disabled, compare autocast, dynamic-shape branches, and mutable module state across the original and recompute passes.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the failed iteration after disabling cache for training

causalContracts.title: Checkpoint head/embedding shape follows a changed vocabulary
causalContracts.summary: The intact checkpoint and current model use different vocabulary cardinalities, so the affected embedding/head tensor shapes cannot match by construction.
causalContracts.action: The passing checksum/manifest means the checkpoint is not corrupt. Use the producer tokenizer/vocabulary, or intentionally resize token embeddings and initialize/train the new rows. Verify tokenizer IDs stay below the new vocabulary and run a forward/loss smoke test before resuming.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If vocabulary cardinality is identical, diff tied-weight configuration and model revision before loading again.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume after the vocabulary and model shapes are intentionally reconciled

causalContracts.title: Transformers loader rejects an intentional mismatch despite its ignore guard
causalContracts.summary: Checkpoint integrity passes and the loader incorrectly rejects an intentional non-quantized task-head mismatch despite `ignore_mismatched_sizes=True`.
causalContracts.action: Upgrade to the Transformers version containing the mismatch-guard fix (or apply that narrow patch), reinitialize only the intended task head, and run a forward smoke test. Preserve the verified checkpoint.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the fixed loader still fails, compare the exact config, state-dict keys, and intended output-class count.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume after a successful guarded load and head validation

causalContracts.title: Distributed checkpoint save did not publish every shard

required.re: expected shards?\s*=\s*\d+[^\n]*present shards?\s*=\s*\d+|only \d+ of the expected \d+[^\n]*shards

causalContracts.summary: The distributed save never reached an atomic completion state: expected shards are absent and no completion manifest was published.
causalContracts.action: Quarantine the partial directory and do not resume from it. Upgrade Megatron/the distributed checkpoint writer or disable async saving for containment, require every expected shard plus checksums before publishing a completion manifest, and verify a save/load round trip at the same world size.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If all writers report success but shards remain absent, capture per-rank writer completion and storage errors before investigating collectives.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume only from the previous manifest-complete checkpoint

causalContracts.title: Accelerate state restore runs before prepare or on only one rank
causalContracts.summary: Accelerate state is restored before distributed objects are prepared and on only one rank, so per-process RNG/dataloader state diverges.
causalContracts.action: Call `accelerator.prepare(...)` first, then call `accelerator.load_state(...)` on every process so each rank restores its own RNG and registered state. Verify resumed step, sampler position, and RNG fingerprints agree across ranks.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If ranks still diverge, compare the saved per-rank RNG files, sampler epoch, gradient-accumulation step, and process count.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the same checkpoint after correcting prepare/load ordering on every rank

causalContracts.title: NCCL socket fallback is visible but the timeout owner is unresolved

required.re: ALLREDUCE timed out|collective operation timeout|ProcessGroupNCCL watchdog

causalContracts.summary: NCCL fell back from verbs to sockets and later timed out, but that fallback alone does not identify why progress stopped; the causal rank, link, and collective sequence are absent.
causalContracts.action: Collect per-rank NCCL_DEBUG=INFO output and a PyTorch NCCL Flight Recorder trace (TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE plus dump-on-timeout), then align the first stalled sequence with rank exits, host dmesg/Xid, and NIC/link counters. Do not attribute the hang to libibverbs or raise timeouts until that evidence identifies the owner.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the same collective passes over sockets in nccl-tests, inspect application collective ordering and the first missing rank; if it fails there too, compare verbs/socket controls with switch and HCA counters.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: the last checkpoint before the unresolved timeout

causalContracts.title: Multiple ranks select the same CUDA device
causalContracts.summary: NCCL directly reports two ranks on the same CUDA device, and the launcher trace confirms both processes select cuda:0; this is rank-to-device mapping, not a fabric timeout.
causalContracts.action: Map exactly one local process to each visible GPU: derive the device from LOCAL_RANK, call torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank) before process-group initialization, and correct the launcher so rank 2 and rank 3 do not both select cuda:0. Verify every rank prints a unique rank-to-device/PCI-bus mapping before rerunning the collective.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the printed mapping is unique but NCCL still reports a duplicate, compare container GPU visibility and UUID/PCI-bus mappings on each host rather than extending the timeout.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the distributed job after validating the one-rank-per-device map

causalContracts.title: RDMA completion status localizes a layer but not a causal component

required.re: NET\/IB[^\n]*completion with error|Got completion with error
No port counters|no[^\n]*(?:mlx5 health|switch events|cable A\/B|host dmesg)|not (?:included|attached)

causalContracts.summary: The completion error identifies the RDMA/IB layer, but the submitted evidence cannot distinguish endpoint, cable, switch, congestion, firmware, or a process/resource failure.
causalContracts.action: Collect incident-window mlx5 health/dmesg, HCA and switch port counters, `ibstat`/link state, vendor-error decoding for the exact adapter, and a controlled cable/port or host A/B. Do not replace a component or raise NCCL timeouts until one discriminator identifies it.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If all physical/link evidence is clean, inspect process exits, memory pressure, and RDMA resource lifecycle at the same timestamp.

causalContracts.title: Distributed rendezvous is missing a participant

required.re: DistStoreError:\s*Socket Timeout|Socket Timeout waiting for key|Setting up process group[^\n]*env:\/\/

causalContracts.summary: The process group is missing a participant, but the available log cannot distinguish rank death, rank/device mapping, bind-address selection, or cross-host reachability.
causalContracts.action: Capture rank 1’s first exception and effective `LOCAL_RANK`/device map, then verify `MASTER_ADDR:MASTER_PORT` from every worker with the actual bind address, route, and firewall policy. Keep the first failing clock-aligned event.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If rendezvous connectivity passes, reduce to one worker per host and compare process launch/environment propagation before testing the collective backend.

causalContracts.title: Resume hang is localized to restored optimizer/RNG state but needs a bisect
causalContracts.summary: The combined no-optimizer/no-RNG A/B localizes the hang to restored training state, but it does not yet separate optimizer contents from per-rank RNG/control-flow divergence.
causalContracts.action: Bisect the restore flags independently: load model+RNG without optimizer, then model+optimizer without RNG, while comparing validation batch/branch fingerprints on every rank. Capture the first divergent collective sequence with the PyTorch NCCL flight recorder.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If both isolated restores pass but the combination hangs, reduce the optimizer step/validation transition and compare serialized state versions plus rank counts.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: keep the source checkpoint frozen and resume only after the restored-state combination passes validation

causalContracts.title: Distributed evaluation ranks collide on one local cache file

required.re: another evaluation module instance is already using the local cache file|evaluation[^\n]*cache[^\n]*collision

causalContracts.summary: One evaluation rank exits on a shared metric-cache collision before the remaining ranks time out in collectives; the NCCL watchdog is downstream.
causalContracts.action: Give every distributed evaluation instance a unique `experiment_id`/per-rank cache path (or use the framework’s distributed metric aggregation), clean only the stale metric cache, and rerun evaluation. Verify rank 6 remains alive and all ranks complete the same metric barrier.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If rank 6 still exits with unique cache ownership, diagnose its new first exception before changing NCCL.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the last complete training checkpoint after the evaluation cache fix

causalContracts.title: Kubelet socket restart leaves stale device-plugin health state

required.re: Deleting only the device-plugin pod[^\n]*re-register|device-plugin pod[^\n]*re-registers

causalContracts.summary: The kubelet socket lifecycle leaves stale device-plugin health state; plugin-only re-registration recovers while GPU diagnostics remain clean.
causalContracts.action: Roll the NVIDIA device-plugin DaemonSet/pod to force clean re-registration after kubelet restarts, then verify node Capacity/Allocatable and a GPU Pod admission. Upgrade to a release/configuration using the supported CDI path for durable kubelet-restart handling.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If re-registration does not restore capacity, inspect plugin NVML/runtime visibility and kubelet device-plugin socket state before taking hardware action.

causalContracts.title: NVIDIA device-plugin discovery strategy is incompatible with the runtime
causalContracts.summary: The host sees the GPU, but the device plugin rejects its automatic discovery strategy and therefore publishes no schedulable GPU resource.
causalContracts.action: Correct the NVIDIA Container Toolkit/device-plugin runtime and strategy configuration for this host, then roll the DaemonSet. Verify plugin logs show a valid platform, node Capacity/Allocatable includes `nvidia.com/gpu`, and the same Pod schedules.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If resource registration remains empty, inspect the plugin container’s NVML library/device visibility and its effective configuration.

causalContracts.title: Accelerate forwards an unsupported checkpoint argument to DeepSpeed
causalContracts.summary: Accelerate forwards `weights_only` to a DeepSpeed checkpoint API that does not accept that argument. The call-signature mismatch stops restore before checkpoint contents are interpreted.
causalContracts.action: Install a tested Accelerate/DeepSpeed version pair whose checkpoint adapter has a matching `load_checkpoint` signature, or patch the adapter so it does not forward `weights_only` to this DeepSpeed version. Preserve the checkpoint and verify the exact `accelerator.load_state` call restores model, optimizer, scheduler, and step state in a disposable run.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the signature is compatible but restore still fails, diagnose the new first checkpoint error; do not disable safe loading or rewrite the checkpoint based on this superseded TypeError.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from the same checkpoint only after the full-state restore smoke test reports the expected step

causalContracts.title: Loaded cuDNN sublibraries are from an incompatible version tuple
causalContracts.summary: cuDNN rejects its own backend descriptor because the loaded cuDNN sublibraries are not one compatible version set. The failure occurs during library finalization, before the convolution executes.
causalContracts.action: Install one qualified PyTorch/CUDA/cuDNN wheel or container tuple and remove earlier cuDNN directories from the runtime loader path. In the final environment, record the resolved cuDNN library paths and versions, then run the submitted convolution as a smoke test.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If every resolved cuDNN component is from the same qualified build, reduce the descriptor/conv call and test a newer patched PyTorch build before changing model inputs.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the failed operation in a fresh process after replacing the mixed library set

causalContracts.title: Dynamo tries to materialize a lazy module with symbolic dimensions

required.re: SymIntArrayRef expected to contain only concrete integers

causalContracts.summary: Dynamo reaches lazy-parameter materialization while the inferred shape is still symbolic, but the materialization path requires concrete integer dimensions.
causalContracts.action: Materialize the lazy module once with a representative concrete input before calling `torch.compile`, then compile the initialized module. Alternatively use a PyTorch build containing the Dynamo lazy-module fix. Verify eager and compiled outputs and parameter shapes match for the submitted input family.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the initialized module still fails, contain the affected module in eager mode and preserve a minimal dynamic-shape reproducer for the compiler regression.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart from job initialization after materializing the lazy parameters; checkpoint data is not implicated

causalContracts.title: AOTInductor reads a large constant-file offset through a narrow integer path
causalContracts.summary: AOTInductor misreads the aligned weight offset after a large constant artifact crosses a narrow file-offset boundary; later alignment or illegal-memory errors are consequences of that corrupted offset.
causalContracts.action: Use a patched AOTInductor runtime with 64-bit file-size/offset operations, rebuild the compiled artifact, and reject any old artifact generated for the narrow-offset loader. Verify every serialized offset is 16K-aligned and in range, then compare one eager and AOTI inference result before rollout.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the patched loader reads the exact offset correctly but execution still fails, preserve the rebuilt artifact and diagnose the new first kernel/runtime error independently.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart inference with the rebuilt artifact; do not reuse the incompatible compiled package

causalContracts.title: A large pinned-host allocation exceeds the host pinning path limit

excluded.re: (?:Assertion|assertion)[^\n]*failed|IndexKernel\.cu|ScatterGatherKernel\.cu|Class values must be smaller than num_classes

causalContracts.summary: The failing operation is an explicitly large pinned host-memory allocation. The generic CUDA device-assert footer is debugging guidance, not evidence that a GPU kernel asserted.
causalContracts.action: Reduce or chunk the pinned-host allocation and check the process memlock limit plus available host RAM.
