causalContracts.summary: Gloo all-reduce reaches a device-type registry without a linked CUDA creator in this build. This is backend/build capability, not an NCCL or GPU fault.
causalContracts.action: Use NCCL for CUDA collectives or move tensors to CPU for a Gloo control. If CUDA Gloo is intended, link/register `makeAllreduceCUDAWork` and fail initialization clearly when unavailable.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the CUDA creator is registered and selected, capture the exact Gloo work exception and reduce it on two ranks before changing backends.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the collective after backend capability validation succeeds

causalContracts.title: NCCL checkpoint restore hangs in the cuMem host allocation path
causalContracts.summary: Every rank reaches restore, but only the cuMem host-enabled path hangs; disabling it restores successfully. Rendezvous timeout and checkpoint contents are not the selected owner.
causalContracts.action: Contain with `NCCL_CUMEM_HOST_ENABLE=0` for the affected tuple. Upgrade or patch the restore allocation path, then run repeated checkpoint→restore cycles with cuMem host re-enabled and bounded progress telemetry.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If restore also hangs with cuMem host disabled, compare per-rank restore phase markers and KVS progress; withdraw this allocation owner.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume only from a checkpoint whose restore completed on every rank and passed an application-state checksum

causalContracts.title: NCCL RAS query dereferences an unavailable status response
causalContracts.summary: Communicator churn leaves null RAS status entries; the text formatter applies count-leading-zeros to zero while the JSON control keeps running. This selects the formatter/null-status boundary, though the upstream report labels the source-level explanation a theory.
causalContracts.action: Guard zero/null status before CLZ and fix the communicator-index advancement that can leave entries unfilled. Stress communicator churn at scale through text and JSON serialization and require both to return typed unavailable status without crashing.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If a symbolized core does not enter the RAS text formatter, withdraw this theory and use the first proven frame as owner.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the diagnostic process after null-response tests pass

causalContracts.title: NCCL topology XML exceeds a fixed node-capacity limit
causalContracts.summary: Fusing the multi-rail topology exceeds NCCL’s fixed XML node capacity. This is representation capacity, not evidence that a NIC or GPU link failed.
causalContracts.action: Contain the topology within supported capacity, then replace the fixed array with checked dynamic capacity or raise it with explicit overflow validation. Parse and round-trip the complete 32-NIC topology in CI.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the parsed count is below the limit, capture duplicate/fusion expansion and the first rejected node; do not remove healthy rails blindly.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: launch after NCCL accepts and prints the complete intended topology

causalContracts.title: Accelerate eval mode does not traverse the DeepSpeed optimizer wrapper
causalContracts.summary: Accelerate handles the one-level DeepSpeed optimizer wrapper in `train()` but not in `eval()`, so evaluation mode never reaches the wrapped optimizer.
causalContracts.action: Mirror the existing one-level DeepSpeed traversal from `AcceleratedOptimizer.train()` in `eval()`, then test wrapped and unwrapped optimizers in both transitions.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the wrapped object receives `eval()`, inspect the underlying optimizer implementation and withdraw this traversal owner.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume evaluation after train/eval symmetry tests pass

causalContracts.title: Accelerate device transfer drops defaultdict construction semantics

required.re: TypeError|first argument must be callable|mapping type

causalContracts.summary: Recursive batch transfer reconstructs a `defaultdict` like a plain mapping and loses or misplaces its callable factory.
causalContracts.action: Special-case `defaultdict` reconstruction so its `default_factory` and transferred items use the correct constructor positions. Test nested batches, missing-key behavior, and device placement.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: For a custom mapping, preserve its documented constructor contract or return an unsupported-container error instead of guessing.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume at the failed batch after type, values, and missing-key behavior are verified

causalContracts.title: Kernel warmup stages issue collectives without rank synchronization
causalContracts.summary: Ranks advance through warmup stages at different speeds while those stages issue real collectives, so they enter different collective sequences. Host jitter exposes the missing synchronization but is not the owner.
causalContracts.action: Insert a model-parallel barrier between every warmup stage that can issue a collective, or one proven-safe boundary barrier. Stress startup with injected rank jitter and require identical ordered stage entry.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If ordered traces prove identical stages and collectives on all ranks, withdraw this owner and inspect the first argument mismatch.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart workers after jittered warmup completes repeatedly with identical stage order

causalContracts.title: MiniMax FP8 KV insertion mutates graph-captured state unsafely
causalContracts.summary: The FP8 KV path allocates and scatters during CUDA graph capture, corrupting the index cache; eager FP8 and graphed BF16 controls isolate the graph-unsafe write.
causalContracts.action: Contain with eager execution. Break `_insert_kv` out of capture or use the graph-safe fused cache write, then compare fixed-prompt logits and KV/index checksums in eager versus replay.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If FP8 output is wrong in eager mode too, withdraw the graph-only owner and validate scales and the first KV write.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart requests after eager/graph logit parity and repeated replay pass

causalContracts.title: Granite MoE loader looks up weights owned by another pipeline rank
causalContracts.summary: The model builds only its rank-local layer interval, but one load helper still looks up checkpoint weights owned by another rank. A startup timeout cannot fix deterministic ownership.
causalContracts.action: Apply the rank-local layer/parameter filter to every Granite MoE load helper. Test PP=1 and PP>1 and assert each checkpoint key is loaded only by its owning rank.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the missing parameter belongs to the local interval, withdraw this owner and compare checkpoint naming/conversion for that key.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart loading after every key is loaded by exactly one owning rank or explicitly shared

causalContracts.title: Custom all-reduce admits a cross-node group that cannot share CUDA IPC
causalContracts.summary: The custom all-reduce eligibility shortcut admits ranks on different hosts even though graph buffers rely on shareable CUDA IPC. The invalid handle is a locality-contract violation.
causalContracts.action: Use NCCL for the cross-node group. Make custom-allreduce admission and buffer registration topology-aware, then test two ranks on one host and two hosts.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the ranks are on one host and share an IPC namespace, capture device UUIDs and handle ownership before blaming locality.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart after admission selects NCCL for unsupported cross-node groups

causalContracts.title: FlashInfer MoE weight conversion retains scratch memory until OOM
causalContracts.summary: Startup OOM occurs while converting MoE weights because conversion scratch allocations are not reclaimed. The Triton control bypasses conversion and succeeds.
causalContracts.action: Contain with the Triton MoE backend. Release or reuse bounded conversion scratch layer-by-layer and add peak-memory assertions for the affected TP/model size; split-size tuning is not a fix.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If peak memory remains after scratch is explicitly released, capture an allocation snapshot and locate the retained owner before reducing capacity.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: start serving after conversion stays below its memory ceiling and a first request succeeds

causalContracts.title: Profiler endpoint repeats a non-idempotent start/stop transition

required.re: Can.t disable Kineto profiler when it.s not running|segfault|use-after-free

causalContracts.summary: The endpoint invokes raw profiler lifecycle methods more than once; the second stop acts on an already-consumed Kineto trace and can raise or use freed state.
causalContracts.action: Protect start/stop with an atomic profiler state machine. Return a stable conflict/no-op for duplicate transitions, serialize trace save, and test repeated and concurrent calls with large traces.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If one valid stop crashes, symbolicate that trace and withdraw duplicate-transition ownership.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the API process after lifecycle idempotency and concurrency tests pass

causalContracts.title: V2 model runner accepts CPU offload without installing an offloader
causalContracts.summary: V2 accepts `cpu_offload_gb` but leaves the offloader as a no-op, so weights stay on GPU and later OOM. V1 installing it and succeeding isolates missing V2 wiring.
causalContracts.action: Fail safe by declaring weight offload unsupported in V2 so selection falls back to V1, or forced V2 errors. Claim support only after initialization plus eager/graph tests verify measured GPU residency.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If V2 logs a real offloader and residency drops by the requested amount, withdraw this owner and inspect the later allocation snapshot.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart with V1 or a qualified V2 implementation after measured offload and first-forward checks pass

causalContracts.title: CUDA IPC memory accounting underflows with multiple consumers
causalContracts.summary: Multiple consumers release one shared CUDA IPC allocation without per-consumer ownership, allowing reference underflow and premature producer release.
causalContracts.action: Track one acknowledgement/reference per consumer and release only after every imported handle closes. Test crash, duplicate close, and out-of-order completion under compute-sanitizer.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If every consumer has a balanced independent reference, symbolicate the first invalid access and inspect handle lifetime instead of retaining memory indefinitely.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart IPC participants after ownership accounting passes stress and crash recovery

causalContracts.title: Exception-checkpoint callback suppresses the initiating rank failure
causalContracts.summary: One rank’s original training exception is swallowed after checkpoint handling, so peers continue into a collective and time out. The timeout is a victim symptom.
causalContracts.action: Save best-effort and re-raise the original exception on the same rank; coordinate terminal state before any later collective. Inject a rank-local exception and require one preserved root error plus bounded shutdown.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the original exception is re-raised, compare per-rank callback order and use the earliest non-timeout error as owner.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume only after the exception checkpoint is verified complete and intact across ranks

causalContracts.title: KV cache manager is sized without average sequence length for extreme prompts
causalContracts.summary: The V2 KV manager operates at an extreme maximum without the workload average used for sizing and fails natively on a large prompt instead of rejecting an impossible layout.
causalContracts.action: Set `avg_seq_len` from measured prompts and cap requests beyond the qualified layout. Add bounds checks so insufficient capacity returns a typed error, then replay the 256k control.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the manager reports sufficient blocks with an explicit average, symbolicate the crash and inspect the first invalid block index.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart after the cache planner accepts the large-prompt control without native faults

causalContracts.title: Asymmetric speculative decode makes attention-DP ranks enter different collectives
causalContracts.summary: Asymmetric gen-only speculative setup delivers different request states to attention-DP ranks, but per-iteration collectives are entered or shaped from rank-local state, so ranks execute incompatible contracts and deadlock.
causalContracts.action: Make the request mix rank-consistent or make every affected collective rank-safe: all model-parallel ranks enter or skip together with compatible shapes. Stress burst arrival with injected skew.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If ordered traces prove every rank enters the same collective with the same shape, withdraw divergence and inspect the first non-progressing transport rank.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart generation workers after burst and continuous controls preserve collective order

causalContracts.title: GRPO creates packed metadata for a local attention backend that rejects it

required.re: Packed sequence is not supported by DotProductAttention

causalContracts.summary: The GRPO reference-logprobs path creates single-sequence THD metadata with RL graphs disabled, then passes it to local unfused attention, whose dense path rejects packed metadata.
causalContracts.action: Construct synthetic `PackedSeqParams` only when RL training CUDA graphs are enabled, in both `get_logprobs()` and the GRPO forward step. Test local/unfused attention with graphs on and off.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If `packed_seq_params` is already `None` at local attention, use the new earliest assertion and withdraw this guard attribution.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the RL step after reference and policy logprob passes complete under the same graph setting

causalContracts.title: Vocab-parallel cross entropy mutates a custom-autograd view in FP32
causalContracts.summary: The FP32 vocabulary-parallel loss mutates a view returned by a custom autograd function, which would override its custom backward; PyTorch correctly rejects the aliasing.
causalContracts.action: Clone the gathered output before mutation or rewrite the operation out-of-place, then compare FP32 loss and gradients against a non-parallel reference.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the gathered output is cloned before mutation, capture the next alias-producing frame and withdraw this exact owner.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the step after FP32 forward/backward gradient parity passes

causalContracts.title: GRPO silently constructs an empty optimizer from a frozen PEFT adapter

required.re: optimizer param(?:eter)? count[^\n]{0,40}(?:0|zero)|zero trainable parameters|empty optimizer

causalContracts.summary: GRPO receives a PEFT adapter loaded in inference mode; creating the KL reference adapter leaves the active adapter frozen, so the optimizer is empty even though transient gradients make the run look active.
causalContracts.action: Fail initialization when the training adapter contributes zero optimizer parameters. Load or enable the active adapter as trainable, explicitly freeze only the reference adapter, and verify an expected parameter changes after a deterministic step.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the optimizer contains intended adapter parameters, compare pre/post-step hashes and optimizer state before claiming a no-op.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart from the last genuinely changed adapter checkpoint, not a byte-identical no-op output

causalContracts.title: AutoTP rewrites a dimension attribute without sharding its owning weights
causalContracts.summary: AutoTP halves a vision-tower dimension attribute even though the Conv3d weight is not sharded, so reshape silently doubles the token count at half width and the next LayerNorm catches the inconsistency.
causalContracts.action: Rewrite dimension attributes only on modules whose corresponding weights AutoTP actually shards, or validate the attribute against the post-transform weight. Test multimodal vision towers at TP1 and TP2 and assert shape invariants after injection.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If `embed_dim` still equals the projection output channels at the failing forward, withdraw this owner and inspect the preceding reshape producer.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart from model initialization after transformed attributes and weight shapes agree on every rank

causalContracts.title: DeepSpeed release regression breaks process-group initialization
causalContracts.summary: The same PyTorch/NCCL environment initializes without DeepSpeed and on DeepSpeed 0.17.2, while the newer launcher fails before training. This isolates a DeepSpeed release boundary, but not the internal line without a version bisect.
causalContracts.action: Pin 0.17.2 as containment. Bisect DeepSpeed releases/comm initialization with identical environment and capture the first synchronous CUDA call returning 600; then upgrade only to a release containing the identified fix.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the vanilla process-group control begins failing, withdraw the DeepSpeed owner and re-open driver/device readiness using the first failing CUDA call.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the job on the known-good tuple after process-group and one collective smoke tests pass

causalContracts.title: Ray compiled-DAG mutable objects outlive their driver owner

required.re: driver process (?:has )?exited|after the driver process exits?
Plasma memory usage[^\n]{0,80}(?:40 MiB|[1-9]\d* MiB)|Objects consumed by Ray tasks

causalContracts.summary: Compiled-DAG mutable-object references remain owned by the cluster after the creating driver exits, so object-store memory is not reclaimed until cluster teardown.
causalContracts.action: Explicitly tear down the compiled DAG/channel as containment. Tie mutable-object reference ownership to driver lifecycle and release on driver death; verify `ray memory` returns to baseline after normal exit and forced termination.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If reference-creation sites show a live actor/task still owns the objects, withdraw driver-lifecycle ownership and close that owner explicitly.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the workload only after repeated driver exits return object-store usage to baseline

causalContracts.title: Sparse MLA decode kernel spins indefinitely without a device-side deadline
causalContracts.summary: Device capture localizes non-progress to the sparse MLA decode kernel; the much later assertion is collateral. The kernel lacks a bounded progress/failure path.
causalContracts.action: Disable the sparse MLA backend for containment. Add bounded iteration/progress checks and a typed kernel failure, reproduce under device capture, then require sustained identical-input replay before re-enabling.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If device capture shows the kernel completed, withdraw this owner and use the earliest subsequently active kernel or host wait.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the failed request after the corrected kernel passes bounded-progress stress

causalContracts.title: NIXL metadata handshake assumes symmetric tensor-parallel block layout
causalContracts.summary: The NIXL handshake exchanges metadata before KV transfer but maps incompatible local/remote block layouts for asymmetric prefill/decode TP. Symmetric TP succeeds, selecting the heterogeneous-layout contract.
causalContracts.action: Use symmetric TP as containment. Make the metadata exchange describe and map heterogeneous TP block ownership explicitly, validate counts/IDs before `loadRemoteMD`, and test pTP2→dTP4 plus the inverse.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If asymmetric peers advertise compatible mapped block sets, withdraw layout ownership and inspect the NIXL backend error with transport debug enabled.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart both P/D engines after metadata compatibility and first KV checksum transfer pass

causalContracts.title: FlashInfer b12x MoE path triggers an MMU illegal write under chunked prefill
causalContracts.summary: The workload faults only on the FlashInfer b12x MoE path under concurrent chunked prefill; a backend control passes. This selects the kernel/backend path, but the non-identical build control limits confidence and does not justify RMA.
causalContracts.action: Quarantine `flashinfer_b12x` for the affected SM/model tuple. Reproduce the identical build and request mix with synchronous launching and compute-sanitizer, then bisect backend versions and require the same-input control to pass before re-enable.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the exact same build faults on the alternate backend or Xid 31 appears in an independent DCGM stress test, reopen hardware/driver ownership and quarantine the GPU.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the failed requests on the known-good backend, then re-admit only after an exact-build control passes

causalContracts.title: DFlash logs graph capture before proving any graph needs capture
causalContracts.summary: The status line is emitted before the capture-eligibility check, so it claims capture even when mode is NONE and the capture descriptor list is empty. This is an observability defect, not a GPU incident.
causalContracts.action: Call `needs_capture()` before logging or mutating capture state; emit an explicit skipped reason when false. Test NONE and active modes and assert logs agree with actual descriptors.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If capture descriptors are non-empty, retain the log and inspect actual capture completion rather than suppressing it.

causalContracts.title: Zero-embedding fallback lets one audio request decode forever

required.re: Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings
Returning zero embeddings to avoid engine crash

causalContracts.summary: The audio path repeatedly substitutes zero embeddings for an invalid empty multimodal result, never reaches EOS, and monopolizes the engine. The fallback hides a request error and converts it into an infinite decode.
causalContracts.action: Reject the request with a typed multimodal preprocessing error when required embeddings are empty, impose per-request decode/progress bounds, and isolate cancellation so health and other requests survive. Preserve the deterministic audio fixture.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If valid non-empty embeddings reach the model on the failing request, withdraw this fallback owner and capture the first non-progressing decode state.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the poisoned engine once, then require the same audio to fail boundedly without affecting health

causalContracts.title: Gloo local synchronization deadlocks on overlapping group creation history
causalContracts.summary: Overlapping Gloo groups are created with only participant-local synchronization while nonparticipants follow a different global creation history. The NCCL control and documented local-sync deadlock condition select group-creation ordering, not GPU transport.
causalContracts.action: Disable local synchronization for overlapping groups or make every rank create groups in one identical global order. Add a timeout and log the ordered group IDs on all ranks before each creation.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If every rank has an identical global group-creation sequence, withdraw this ordering owner and capture the first Gloo rendezvous key that lacks a participant.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart all ranks after a deterministic global group-order smoke test passes

causalContracts.title: NCCL graph search collapses to one channel after rejecting the viable SM80 tree
causalContracts.summary: Tree graph search rejects the viable simple-tree path on SM80 and the remaining balanced-tree constraints collapse selection to one global network channel. This is graph-search policy, not a dead NIC.
causalContracts.action: Contain with a known-good NCCL version or validated topology override. Patch/test SM80 simple-tree eligibility and correct bidirectional tree bandwidth accounting; require multi-channel NIC utilization in nccl-tests.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the generated graph contains multiple channels but runtime uses one, withdraw graph-search ownership and inspect channel launch/transport selection.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart after the generated tree graph and measured traffic use the intended rails

causalContracts.title: NCCL IB async thread does not reconcile a GID-change event
causalContracts.summary: The verbs async thread receives a GID-change event but lacks an explicit refresh/recovery path, leaving cached addressing potentially stale. The event alone does not prove a fabric outage.
causalContracts.action: Refresh or invalidate affected GID/route state on `IBV_EVENT_GID_CHANGE`, log device/port/old/new GID, and validate a controlled RoCE GID rotation without wedging communicators.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the active GID and route remain unchanged, treat the event as informational and investigate the actual first transport failure.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: reconnect affected communicators only after address state is validated

causalContracts.title: Ray hides the distinction between NVML failure and missing GPU devices
causalContracts.summary: GPU device nodes exist but NVML discovery failed; current logging collapses those states. This is an observability finding and is not enough evidence to diagnose a GPU fault or scheduler capacity loss.
causalContracts.action: Log NVML initialization/error code, visible device nodes, permissions, container mounts, driver library path, and any fallback decision separately. Fail or degrade explicitly rather than reporting zero GPUs without cause.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If device nodes are absent too, classify container/device admission instead of NVML-only discovery.

causalContracts.title: Ray accelerated DAG does not propagate NCCL channel failure cleanly
causalContracts.summary: An NCCL transport failure occurs inside an experimental accelerated DAG, but the orchestration path lacks a complete typed propagation/cleanup contract. The NCCL error text alone does not identify its lower-level cause.
causalContracts.action: Preserve the original NCCL code and rank/channel, cancel dependent DAG work, close transport resources, and surface one bounded task failure. Add injected NCCL-error tests for setup, send, receive, and teardown.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: After propagation is correct, diagnose the preserved first NCCL error with per-rank transport evidence rather than attributing it to Ray automatically.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: rebuild and retry the DAG only after failed channel resources are confirmed released

causalContracts.title: Lightning static-graph strategy diverges under manual optimization
causalContracts.summary: Only Lightning’s static-graph strategy under manual optimization produces rank-divergent parameters; vanilla DDP and non-static controls synchronize. This selects Lightning strategy integration rather than NCCL.
causalContracts.action: Contain with `static_graph=False`. Compare reducer preparation and manual-backward hooks against vanilla DDP, assert parameter checksums across ranks after every step, and re-enable only when both static/non-static paths agree.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If identical seeds/data and vanilla DDP also diverge, withdraw Lightning ownership and inspect sampler and rank-local optimizer inputs.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart from the last checkpoint whose parameter hashes match on every rank

causalContracts.title: Sparse DSV4 attention backend repeats one impossible decode token
causalContracts.summary: The sparse DSV4 path deterministically emits one token/logprob at every position across parallel layouts and a clean environment. This isolates the backend/model path, but a same-build alternate-backend logit control is still missing.
causalContracts.action: Quarantine the sparse DSV4 backend. Capture fixed-prompt pre-sampling logits and intermediate sparse-index/KV outputs, then compare the same build to a supported alternate backend before localizing the first divergent kernel.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If a same-build alternate backend produces the same degenerate logits, withdraw backend ownership and verify checkpoint scales, tokenizer, and model implementation.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart on a backend with coherent fixed-prompt logits; re-enable only after same-build parity

causalContracts.title: NVLS BF16 reduction changes with multicast allocation history
causalContracts.summary: BF16 results vary with multicast/communicator allocation history and stabilize under the runtime-connect control. This selects NVLS connection/allocation ordering, not application artifacts, but exact reduction grouping remains unproven.
causalContracts.action: Use `NCCL_RUNTIME_CONNECT=0` only as a deterministic containment after measuring its cost. Record communicator/NVLS allocation order and result hashes, compare NCCL/CUDA/driver tuples, and require repeated bitwise or declared-tolerance stability.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If results vary with runtime connect disabled, withdraw NVLS allocation-history ownership and audit application nondeterminism and input/order controls.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume from a checkpoint produced under a verified deterministic communication configuration

causalContracts.title: Long-running serving quality drift lacks a causal state discriminator
causalContracts.summary: Output quality reportedly degrades with uptime, but the supplied evidence does not distinguish mutable model/KV state, request-state leakage, numeric drift, sampling changes, or upstream input differences.
causalContracts.action: Replay a fixed deterministic canary at startup and at drift time; record pre-sampling logits, KV allocation/reset state, adapter/model hashes, RNG/sampling parameters, and memory/error counters. Restart only one component at a time and identify the first control that restores logit parity.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If fresh and aged replicas have identical fixed-input logits, investigate request/input distribution and evaluation criteria rather than serving state.

causalContracts.title: Cross-version throughput regression needs a controlled profile diff
causalContracts.summary: The version boundary is useful, but throughput alone does not identify whether scheduling, kernel choice, graph capture, batching, CPU work, or configuration defaults changed.
causalContracts.action: Run both versions with identical image dependencies, model, requests, warmup, and explicit flags. Diff engine arguments, kernel/backend selection, batch/queue metrics, GPU timelines, tokens/s, and MFU; bisect the first release/commit where the dominant time category changes.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If normalized profiles match, verify client pacing, tokenizer work, and measurement window before calling a runtime regression.

causalContracts.title: Recurring post-uptime kernel failures have multiple live owners
causalContracts.summary: Failures appear only after long uptime and span more than one kernel family. The report does not yet separate cache corruption, resource leakage, driver/runtime degradation, workload-triggered bad inputs, or hardware.
causalContracts.action: Preserve the first synchronized source-located error, failing request hash, cache artifacts, GPU reset generation, thermals/ECC/Xid, and allocator state. Replay the request on a fresh process/same GPU and aged process/peer GPU; change one axis at a time.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: Quarantine hardware only if an independent stress test or cross-workload replay fails on that GPU; otherwise bisect process/cache/runtime state.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart from a clean serving process while preserving the failing request and artifacts for replay

causalContracts.title: Healthy HTTP with zero generation throughput needs internal progress evidence

required.re: Avg generation throughput[^\n]{0,40}0\.0|generation throughput drops? to 0

causalContracts.summary: The front door remains responsive while token progress stops. That proves a data-plane stall, but not whether the scheduler, worker IPC, GPU kernel, KV allocation, or output consumer owns it.
causalContracts.action: At stall time collect scheduler queue/running states, per-request token counters, every process/thread stack, GPU kernel/stream activity, IPC channel depth, KV free blocks, and a bounded internal health canary. Compare the last progressing transition to a healthy replica.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If workers and GPU continue producing tokens, inspect output serialization/backpressure; if no kernel is active, inspect scheduler/IPC before blaming CUDA.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: retry idempotent requests after replacing only the component proven non-progressing

causalContracts.title: Resume-only distributed instability needs rank-state comparison
causalContracts.summary: A pre-train evaluation changes whether resumed ranks start cleanly, implicating rank-local lazy initialization or restored state order, but it does not identify which state is missing.
causalContracts.action: Diff fresh versus resumed rank state before the first collective: model/optimizer/scaler/RNG/sampler/checkpoint hashes, lazy buffers, graph/cache initialization, and ordered collective calls. Replace `evaluate()` with the minimal initialization step that changes the outcome.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If all restored/lazy state and collective order match, inspect nondeterministic hardware/runtime errors rather than retaining evaluation as a ritual workaround.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: resume only from a checksum-verified checkpoint after every rank passes the same initialization canary

causalContracts.title: CUDA 999 during NCCL initialization has no proven owner yet
causalContracts.summary: CUDA 999 is a terminal wrapper error and does not distinguish a lost device, prior asynchronous kernel fault, driver/runtime failure, permissions, or NCCL setup. No Xid or failing CUDA call is supplied.
causalContracts.action: Before restarting, capture `dmesg`/Xid, `nvidia-smi -q`, GPU UUID↔rank mapping, and the first failing CUDA call with synchronous launch. Test one-device CUDA allocation and a minimal nccl-tests collective on the same rank/GPU.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: Quarantine a GPU only when lower-level telemetry or an independent control fails on that UUID; otherwise follow the first source-located software call.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart all ranks only after every assigned GPU passes the same CUDA/NCCL preflight

causalContracts.title: DDP parameter-shape verification hang needs per-rank participation evidence
causalContracts.summary: Ranks block in the first DDP parameter-verification collective after NCCL initialization. The report does not show whether a rank never entered, built a different model, crashed, or lost transport progress.
causalContracts.action: Log entry/exit and model parameter-name/shape hash on every rank, enable bounded distributed debug/timeout, and collect all rank stacks plus NCCL INFO. The first missing rank or mismatched hash selects control-flow/model construction; identical participants shift focus to transport.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: Do not increase the timeout until all ranks and shape hashes are proven identical; a longer wait hides the discriminator.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: relaunch only after rank participation and model-shape parity preflight passes

causalContracts.title: CUDA FFT hang needs cuFFT plan and kernel localization
causalContracts.summary: FFT execution hangs on an Ada GPU, but no plan parameters, active kernel, driver event, or CPU/GPU stack proves whether cuFFT, stream synchronization, prior asynchronous work, or hardware owns it.
causalContracts.action: Reduce to one deterministic transform; log shape/dtype/strides/device/stream, synchronize before and after, collect a GPU trace and host stack, and compare CPU, peer GPU, and a known-good CUDA/driver tuple.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the same plan passes in a fresh process but hangs after prior work, preserve and bisect the preceding operation/state rather than blaming FFT alone.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the failed transform after its minimal plan passes repeatedly on the assigned GPU

causalContracts.title: Elastic restart connection refusal needs rendezvous-generation evidence
causalContracts.summary: A restarted rank connects to an endpoint that is not listening, but the log does not prove stale rank metadata, a failed master/store, port reuse, or startup-order delay.
causalContracts.action: Record restart generation, rank, MASTER_ADDR/PORT, store owner PID, listen socket, and ordered agent events. Verify every generation publishes a fresh endpoint and all old workers/ports are gone before the next process group initializes.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the intended store is listening and reachable from that host, inspect firewall/NAT/routing and the exact destination rather than changing rendezvous timing.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the full elastic generation after endpoint ownership and reachability pass

causalContracts.title: RDMA invalid-request completion identifies a QP, not the causal component
causalContracts.summary: The HCA rejected a local work request on a queue pair. That localizes the transport object but not whether opcode/SGE/MR lifetime, QP state, device firmware, or an upstream memory bug owns it.
causalContracts.action: Capture QP number, opcode, WR ID, status/vendor syndrome, QP state, lkey/rkey and MR lifetime, HCA/port, firmware, and the first failed completion. Correlate with switch/port counters and reproduce in a minimal verbs or nccl-tests path.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the same QP/port passes a minimal verbs stress, inspect application registration and work-request lifetime before replacing fabric hardware.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: reconnect the communicator only after the failed QP is destroyed and a transport health control passes

causalContracts.title: NCCL graph construction violates requested rail isolation
causalContracts.summary: The generated ring and tree contain cross-rail inter-node links despite an explicit CROSS_NIC=0 policy. This is graph/policy enforcement, not proof of a physical link failure.
causalContracts.action: Dump the selected NCCL graphs and GPU↔NIC topology, keep a validated topology override as containment, and fix graph search to preserve rail identity for every inter-node edge. Verify traffic stays on the intended rails.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If graph edges are rail-consistent but counters show cross-rail traffic, withdraw graph ownership and inspect plugin/device mapping.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart collectives after graph and measured NIC traffic both satisfy rail isolation

causalContracts.title: High per-peer network-channel override triggers a send/recv progress failure
causalContracts.summary: The send/recv path loses progress only with the explicit 32-channel-per-peer override. That isolates channel-scaling/configuration interaction, but not the internal resource or scheduler defect.
causalContracts.action: Remove or lower the override for containment. Sweep channel counts while recording QP/channel creation and progress, enforce resource-cap validation at init, and bisect the first count that fails.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If default channel count also hangs, withdraw the override owner and compare the first non-progressing rank/channel.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart after the selected channel count passes repeated send/recv stress

causalContracts.title: Repeated fixed-port NCCL stress needs socket lifecycle evidence
causalContracts.summary: The hang correlates with repeated reuse of one port, but the report does not show whether a prior listener, TIME_WAIT, stale rendezvous generation, collision, or an unrelated collective owns it.
causalContracts.action: Record listener PID/generation, bind/connect/close results, socket states, and per-run rendezvous IDs. Compare an ephemeral-port control and ensure prior workers fully exit before reuse.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the port is clean and every connection establishes, withdraw socket lifecycle and inspect the first collective with missing progress.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart the stress generation only after old listeners and workers are absent

causalContracts.title: Ray Serve/Voxtral startup wrapper hides the initiating worker error

required.re: Engine core initialization failed|WorkerProc initialization failed|DEPLOY_FAILED

causalContracts.summary: Ray Serve reports only that vLLM worker initialization failed. That wrapper exception is not a diagnosis; the causal line is earlier in the worker/core logs and is missing here.
causalContracts.action: Collect the complete first-failing worker stderr before ServeController rewraps it, plus vLLM/Ray/model/CUDA tuple. Reproduce the identical model directly under vLLM and under Ray Serve to isolate orchestration.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If direct vLLM fails identically, diagnose its earliest worker error; if direct works, diff Ray environment, resources, mounts, and startup arguments.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: redeploy only after the direct and orchestrated startup canaries identify or clear the same failure

causalContracts.title: glibc heap-corruption abort requires a symbolized native owner
causalContracts.summary: glibc detected corrupted allocator metadata, usually after an earlier native out-of-bounds write or double free. The abort site is not the write site and cannot identify CUDA, NCCL, or a framework from this message alone.
causalContracts.action: Preserve a core dump and exact native library tuple; reproduce with ASan/valgrind for CPU extensions and compute-sanitizer for CUDA paths, disabling one native extension at a time. Symbolize the first invalid write/free.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the failure disappears without a specific extension under identical load, keep it isolated and verify ABI compatibility before re-enable.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart from the last durable checkpoint after the corrupting native component is isolated

causalContracts.title: Post-NCCL worker CPU spin has no source-located owner yet
causalContracts.summary: Workers spin on CPU after NCCL setup, so a fabric diagnosis is not supported. Without thread stacks or profiler samples, compilation, weight processing, polling, and Python/native loops remain open.
causalContracts.action: Capture repeated `py-spy`/native stacks and per-thread CPU, log the last completed startup phase on every rank, and compare a single-GPU/non-distributed control. Select the hottest stable frame before changing NCCL.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If stacks show a blocked collective rather than active CPU work, reopen per-rank collective order and arguments.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart only after the isolated startup phase completes under a bounded canary

causalContracts.title: Mooncake packed-MLA transfer failure lacks a registration-path discriminator

required.re: Requested address not found|address not found

causalContracts.summary: The failed span equals one packed-MLA page and the NVLink resolver cannot find its address, but controls separating layout-specific registration from general NVLink registration or topology support are missing.
causalContracts.action: Run the same transport with a non-MLA model, a different block size, and a standalone registered-buffer transfer. Trace register→publish→resolve IDs and reject unsupported fallback/topology combinations at startup.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If generic buffers fail too, diagnose NVLink registration/topology; if only packed MLA fails, inspect connector layout ownership.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: retry KV transfer only after one discriminating registration control passes

causalContracts.title: NCCL GPU-to-NIC mapping ignores IP subnet reachability
causalContracts.summary: This is a topology-policy report: proximity-based GPU-to-NIC selection does not incorporate subnet reachability. It is not evidence of an active GPU or fabric failure.
causalContracts.action: Include routable subnet/rail identity in NIC eligibility before proximity scoring, or provide an explicit validated mapping. Test unreachable-near and reachable-far NICs.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If every selected NIC routes to its peer subnet, use actual connection/counter evidence rather than this design gap.

causalContracts.title: RoCE completion log omits queue-pair identity needed for triage
causalContracts.summary: This is an observability request: the completion error lacks QP identity needed to correlate a flow. It does not prove what caused any completion error.
causalContracts.action: Log QP number with rank/channel, HCA/port, WR ID/opcode, completion status, and vendor syndrome in parser-stable fields.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: Use existing trace/QP creation logs to correlate the flow until structured identity ships.

causalContracts.title: Lightning multi-node NCCL failure lacks the initiating logs
causalContracts.summary: The report names Lightning and NCCL but omits the first per-rank failure and the upstream workaround’s mechanism. No root cause can be assigned safely.
causalContracts.action: Collect full per-rank Lightning/PyTorch/NCCL logs and the exact workaround/config change. Compare vanilla torchrun and identify the earliest rank-specific non-timeout event.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If vanilla torchrun fails identically, move ownership below Lightning; if only Lightning fails, diff strategy, environment, and launch arguments.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: restart after first-failure evidence and one direct torchrun control are captured

causalContracts.title: Voxtral model import fails inside FlashAttention capability probing

required.re: Error in loading model architecture|failed to be inspected

causalContracts.summary: Voxtral architecture discovery fails while importing the FlashAttention backend and probing CUDA device capability, before model weights or inference run. The later Ray Serve deployment error is collateral.
causalContracts.action: Pin the previous compatible vLLM tuple for containment. Patch capability probing to resolve a valid current device at runtime rather than failing during model-module inspection, then add a Voxtral registry/import smoke test before deployment.
causalContracts.fallbackAction: If the module imports successfully outside Ray under the identical environment, diff CUDA visibility and device initialization timing in the Serve replica.
causalContracts.resumeFrom: redeploy after direct registry resolution and one transcription startup canary pass

encyclopedia.title: Xid 149 NETIR_LINK_DOWN on Blackwell: the NVLink fault that Xid 74 knowledge misses
encyclopedia.text: Xid 149 NETIR_LINK_DOWN on Blackwell: the NVLink fault that Xid 74 knowledge misses Hardware Kernel log line of the form: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0018:01:00): 149, NETIR_LINK_DOWN Fatal Xid 154 GPU recovery action changed logged immediately after the 149 knvlinkSetDegradedMode_IMPL reporting that the GPU is marked Degraded NCCL falling back to a slower path or failing ring setup on one rank only blackwell nvlink xid-149 netir gb200 b200 degraded-mode Collectives fail or hang on a Blackwell node while every Xid 74 check stays silent nvidia-smi looks healthy after a reboot but the same rank keeps failing collectives Existing NVLink runbooks written for Hopper do not fire on Blackwell hardware Blackwell moved the NVLink fault family to Xid 149 with NETIR subcodes; the subcode name distinguishes a hard link-down from bit-error-rate and data-error events A fatal NETIR_LINK_DOWN takes the GPU out of the NVLink domain and marks it Degraded The degraded marking is sticky, so the GPU stays out of the domain until it is reset even though nvidia-smi may look normal
encyclopedia.anchorText: Xid 149 NETIR_LINK_DOWN on Blackwell: the NVLink fault that Xid 74 knowledge misses Kernel log line of the form: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0018:01:00): 149, NETIR_LINK_DOWN Fatal Xid 154 GPU recovery action changed logged immediately after the 149 knvlinkSetDegradedMode_IMPL reporting that the GPU is marked Degraded NCCL falling back to a slower path or failing ring setup on one rank only blackwell nvlink xid-149 netir gb200 b200 degraded-mode Blackwell moved the NVLink fault family to Xid 149 with NETIR subcodes; the subcode name distinguishes a hard link-down from bit-error-rate and data-error events A fatal NETIR_LINK_DOWN takes the GPU out of the NVLink domain and marks it Degraded The degraded marking is sticky, so the GPU stays out of the domain until it is reset even though nvidia-smi may look normal
encyclopedia.action: Capture the complete Xid 149 line. The subcode name (NETIR_LINK_DOWN versus NETIR_LINK_EVT) and the hex payload are what separate a hard link-down from a bit-error-rate event, so a truncated log is not actionable.
steps: Capture the complete Xid 149 line. The subcode name (NETIR_LINK_DOWN versus NETIR_LINK_EVT) and the hex payload are what separate a hard link-down from a bit-error-rate event, so a truncated log is not actionable.
Generate a full bug report from the affected host with nvidia-bug-report.sh before resetting anything, because the reset clears the state that support and RMA triage need.
Confirm NETIR dumps are present in that bug report. A known defect where mst gpu add failed on broken symbolic links produced bug reports with the NETIR dumps missing.
Reset the GPU to clear the sticky degraded marking, then re-check that the link is back in the NVLink domain rather than trusting a clean nvidia-smi.

Check driver, vBIOS and NMX versions against the DGX GB200 NVL72 release notes before concluding the hardware is faulty. The GB200 stack pins specific NVLINK5, DOCA-Host and NMX-M versions and a mismatch is a common false positive.

encyclopedia.title: NVSwitch SXid errors: what aborts your CUDA jobs and what is only informational
encyclopedia.text: NVSwitch SXid errors: what aborts your CUDA jobs and what is only informational Hardware Kernel log line: nvidia-nvswitch0: SXid (PCI:0000:00:00.0): 20034, Fatal, Link 30 LTSSM Fault Up Kernel log line: nvidia-nvswitch3: SXid (PCI:0000:05:00.0): 12028, Non-fatal, Link 32 egress non-posted PRIV error (First) Correlated Xid 74 and Xid 45 on GPUs when the fatal SXid is on a GPU-to-NVSwitch port Fabric Manager refusing new CUDA job launches nvswitch sxid fabric-manager nvlink ltssm All CUDA jobs on a node abort at once and new launches are refused Operators grep for Xid and find nothing because the switch reports SXid Unclear whether an observed SXid requires action or is informational noise Non-fatal SXids are informational; Fabric Manager keeps running jobs alive, though a brief performance drop or stall can occur A fatal SXid on a GPU-to-NVSwitch port is propagated to that GPU, aborting its CUDA jobs, and commonly surfaces as Xid 74 plus Xid 45 A fatal SXid on a port connecting two GPU baseboards makes Fabric Manager abort every running CUDA job and block new launches, with Xid 45 reported as part of the abort
encyclopedia.anchorText: NVSwitch SXid errors: what aborts your CUDA jobs and what is only informational Kernel log line: nvidia-nvswitch0: SXid (PCI:0000:00:00.0): 20034, Fatal, Link 30 LTSSM Fault Up Kernel log line: nvidia-nvswitch3: SXid (PCI:0000:05:00.0): 12028, Non-fatal, Link 32 egress non-posted PRIV error (First) Correlated Xid 74 and Xid 45 on GPUs when the fatal SXid is on a GPU-to-NVSwitch port Fabric Manager refusing new CUDA job launches nvswitch sxid fabric-manager nvlink ltssm Non-fatal SXids are informational; Fabric Manager keeps running jobs alive, though a brief performance drop or stall can occur A fatal SXid on a GPU-to-NVSwitch port is propagated to that GPU, aborting its CUDA jobs, and commonly surfaces as Xid 74 plus Xid 45 A fatal SXid on a port connecting two GPU baseboards makes Fabric Manager abort every running CUDA job and block new launches, with Xid 45 reported as part of the abort
encyclopedia.action: Read the severity field in the SXid line first. Non-fatal entries are informational and do not by themselves justify draining the node.
steps: Read the severity field in the SXid line first. Non-fatal entries are informational and do not by themselves justify draining the node.
For a fatal SXid, identify the reporting port. A GPU-to-NVSwitch port limits the blast radius to that GPU; a baseboard-to-baseboard port takes down the whole node.

For the baseboard case, stop the Fabric Manager service, stop every application using the GPUs, then reset all GPUs and NVSwitches with nvidia-smi -r. Do not scope the reset with -i, because a partial reset leaves the fabric inconsistent.
If the fault survives the reset, reboot or power cycle the system before treating it as a hardware fault.
Look up the specific SXid number in the Fabric Manager user guide appendices for its documented meaning rather than inferring it from the number alone.

encyclopedia.title: GB200 NVL72 driver hang with Xid 150 and 154 after long uptime is a firmware bug, not a dead GPU
encyclopedia.text: GB200 NVL72 driver hang with Xid 150 and 154 after long uptime is a firmware bug, not a dead GPU Reliability Xid 150 and Xid 154 appearing in the kernel log on R580 or later drivers GPU driver hangs tied to NVLink task scheduling Onset after roughly sixty or more days of continuous uptime gb200 nvl72 xid-150 xid-154 vbios firmware blackwell A long-running GB200 rack starts hanging the GPU driver with no hardware change Cards are pulled and RMA-ed but replacements fail the same way after similar uptime Failures cluster by uptime rather than by workload or by individual card Overflow handling in the NVLink management microcode inside the vBIOS firmware, fixed in a later firmware release The failure accumulates with uptime, which is why it presents as a sudden fleet-wide problem on a mature cluster
encyclopedia.anchorText: GB200 NVL72 driver hang with Xid 150 and 154 after long uptime is a firmware bug, not a dead GPU Xid 150 and Xid 154 appearing in the kernel log on R580 or later drivers GPU driver hangs tied to NVLink task scheduling Onset after roughly sixty or more days of continuous uptime gb200 nvl72 xid-150 xid-154 vbios firmware blackwell Overflow handling in the NVLink management microcode inside the vBIOS firmware, fixed in a later firmware release The failure accumulates with uptime, which is why it presents as a sudden fleet-wide problem on a mature cluster
encyclopedia.action: Check the vBIOS version against the DGX GB200 NVL72 release notes before treating the card as faulty, because the fix ships as firmware.
steps: Check the vBIOS version against the DGX GB200 NVL72 release notes before treating the card as faulty, because the fix ships as firmware.
Apply the firmware release containing the NVLink management microcode overflow fix.
If cards were already pulled, re-test them after the firmware update rather than assuming they are bad.
As an interim measure, correlate incidents against node uptime so maintenance can be scheduled before the threshold rather than triggered by an outage.

steps: Monitor ECC error trending: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC | grep -E "Aggregate"` and set Prometheus alert on >10 correctable errors/hour per GPU

Add NCCL flight recorder: set `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_FILE=/tmp/nccl_%h.log` and `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=GRAPH,INIT,COLL` before job start

steps: Profile per-layer compute time: add `torch.cuda.Event` timers around each forward/backward in the pipeline and aggregate by stage
Use automated partitioning: set `model_parallel_config.pipeline_partition_mode=balanced" in DeepSpeed or Megatron-LM config

encyclopedia.title: NIXL Firmware Page Registration Fan-Out Triggers Host OOM Kills on HGX H200 and B200
encyclopedia.text: NIXL Firmware Page Registration Fan-Out Triggers Host OOM Kills on HGX H200 and B200 Reliability /proc/meminfo shows MemAvailable = 0 with buffers/cache fully reclaimed during NIXL-heavy workloads fw_pages_total in debug counters shows >1 million firmware pages per NIC for ~75 GB registered per GPU Kernel dmesg: "Out of memory: Killed process <PID> (python)" with no GPU-side errors crusoe nixl ucx firmware-page host-oom h200 b200 nic-registration rdma Host processes killed by OOM killer with GPUs at normal HBM utilization levels MemAvailable in /proc/meminfo drops to zero despite adequate host RAM capacity Swap fills up and kernel OOM killer activates without GPU memory pressure UCX registers each GPU buffer on every reachable HCA (all 8 NICs per node) creating firmware page duplication factor of N_nics Each firmware page consumes ~35 KB of locked host memory per registration entry With 75 GB registered per GPU * 8 NICs, firmware overhead reaches ~34 GiB of host memory before any workload memory

encyclopedia.text: NCCL Mismatched Collective. Different Ranks Executing Different Operations Communication NCCL error: Mismatched collective detected at rank X NCCL_DEBUG=INFO shows different collective types on different ranks at the same step Training hangs before the mismatch error if ranks are waiting at different barriers The error occurs after a conditional branch that differs across ranks nccl collective mismatch ddp fsdp programming-error synchronization Training crashes with 'Mismatched collective' error from NCCL One rank calls all-reduce while another calls all-gather at the same collective step The error is deterministic and reproducible with the same code path A conditional branch (if/else) causes different ranks to execute different collective operations at the same point in the training loop One rank skips a collective (e.g., skips backward pass for a batch with no loss) while other ranks execute it Dynamic model architectures (MoE routing, early exit) produce different collective patterns on different ranks Mismatched data loading: one rank processes a different number of batches, causing it to be one collective ahead or behind

encyclopedia.title: OFI Memlock Exhaustion. RDMA Memory Registration Failure
encyclopedia.text: OFI Memlock Exhaustion. RDMA Memory Registration Failure Communication NCCL WARN NET/OFI Unable to register memory RC:12 NCCL init timeout after the memory registration error Training works when switching to Socket transport: NCCL_NET=Socket ulimit -l shows a low memlock value (e.g., 64KB or 65536) ofi memlock rdma memory-registration nccl efa ulimit NCCL initialization fails with 'Unable to register memory' on the OFI transport Training works with NCCL_NET=Socket but fails with the default OFI/IB transport The error appears on all ranks simultaneously during NCCL channel setup The OS per-process memlock limit (ulimit -l) is too low for RDMA memory registration RDMA requires pinning (locking) GPU memory in physical RAM so the NIC can DMA directly to it The default memlock limit on many Linux distributions is 64KB, which is far too low for NCCL's RDMA buffers Containers inherit the host's memlock limit unless explicitly overridden

encyclopedia.title: ACS Disabled. GPU Direct RDMA Failure (Vendor Err 81)
encyclopedia.text: ACS Disabled. GPU Direct RDMA Failure (Vendor Err 81) Communication NCCL WARN Got completion with error 4, vendor err 81 NCCL_DEBUG=INFO shows GDR registration failures Performance is significantly worse than expected on RoCE/IB fabrics ibv_devinfo shows the NIC supports GDR but NCCL cannot use it acs gdr gpu-direct-rdma rdma nccl bios pcie vendor-err-81 NCCL RDMA operations fail with completion error 4 and vendor error 81 Multi-node training with GDR enabled crashes or performs very poorly The same training works with GPU Direct RDMA disabled ACS (Access Control Services) is disabled in the server BIOS, which prevents peer-to-peer DMA between the GPU and NIC across the PCIe fabric Without ACS, the IOMMU cannot validate DMA transactions between the GPU and NIC, so the RDMA completion fails with vendor error 81 ACS is sometimes disabled for PCIe passthrough (e.g., for VM device assignment), which has the side effect of breaking GPU Direct RDMA NCCL attempts to use GDR by default on supported hardware, and the failure is not gracefully handled on all NCCL versions

encyclopedia.title: NCCL BUFFSIZE Oversized, Socket Transport Stall
encyclopedia.text: NCCL BUFFSIZE Oversized, Socket Transport Stall Communication NCCL hangs during all-reduce or all-gather after NCCL_BUFFSIZE was manually increased NCCL_DEBUG=INFO shows Socket transport timeouts or retransmissions Watchdog timeout after increasing NCCL_BUFFSIZE Training works with default NCCL_BUFFSIZE but hangs with custom value nccl buffsize socket buffer configuration tuning Training hangs at NCCL communication after setting NCCL_BUFFSIZE to a very large value Socket transport stalls while IB transport works fine with the same buffer size Increasing NCCL_BUFFSIZE made performance worse instead of better NCCL_BUFFSIZE controls the per-channel buffer size for NCCL communication When Socket transport is used, the buffer size must fit within the OS socket buffer limits (rmem_max, wmem_max) Setting NCCL_BUFFSIZE to a value larger than the OS socket buffer limits causes the socket write to block indefinitely IB transport has its own memory registration and doesn't have this socket buffer limit
encyclopedia.anchorText: NCCL BUFFSIZE Oversized, Socket Transport Stall NCCL hangs during all-reduce or all-gather after NCCL_BUFFSIZE was manually increased NCCL_DEBUG=INFO shows Socket transport timeouts or retransmissions Watchdog timeout after increasing NCCL_BUFFSIZE Training works with default NCCL_BUFFSIZE but hangs with custom value nccl buffsize socket buffer configuration tuning NCCL_BUFFSIZE controls the per-channel buffer size for NCCL communication When Socket transport is used, the buffer size must fit within the OS socket buffer limits (rmem_max, wmem_max) Setting NCCL_BUFFSIZE to a value larger than the OS socket buffer limits causes the socket write to block indefinitely IB transport has its own memory registration and doesn't have this socket buffer limit

steps: Remove the custom NCCL_BUFFSIZE setting and let NCCL use its default value

encyclopedia.title: NCCL Topology Detection Regression (v2.18.3+)
encyclopedia.text: NCCL Topology Detection Regression (v2.18.3+) Communication NCCL topology XML shows different GPU-NIC assignments after upgrading NCCL Performance regression of 10-50% on multi-node training after NCCL upgrade NCCL_DEBUG=INFO shows different channel counts or algorithm selections than before Downgrading NCCL to v2.18.1 restores performance nccl topology regression version upgrade performance Training performance degrades after upgrading NCCL to v2.18.3 or later NCCL uses a different (worse) topology than the previous version GPU-NIC affinity is incorrect in the NCCL topology XML after the upgrade NCCL v2.18.3 changed the topology detection algorithm to handle more complex NIC configurations, but the new algorithm produces incorrect GPU-NIC affinity on some systems The regression causes NCCL to assign GPUs to NICs across NUMA boundaries instead of within the same NUMA node On systems with NVSwitch, the regression may incorrectly prefer P2P transport over the faster NVLS transport The fix was included in NCCL v2.22.x but not backported to v2.18.x or v2.19.x

encyclopedia.title: DeepSpeed bf16 Gradient Norm Underflow
encyclopedia.text: DeepSpeed bf16 Gradient Norm Underflow Training Stability AssertionError: all_groups_norm > 0 in DeepSpeed gradient norm computation Training runs fine with fp16 but crashes with bf16 The error occurs at the same step consistently Gradient norms reported as 0.0 in DeepSpeed logs even though the model is learning deepspeed bf16 gradient-norm underflow precision numerical-stability Training crashes with 'assert all_groups_norm > 0' when using bf16 precision with DeepSpeed The error occurs even though gradients are non-zero (they're just too small for bf16 to represent) Switching to fp16 resolves the issue but bf16 is preferred for training stability bf16 has fewer mantissa bits (7) than fp16 (10), reducing the smallest representable positive number When gradient norms are very small (common with large models, small LR, or gradient accumulation), they can underflow to zero in bf16 DeepSpeed's gradient norm assertion assumes non-zero norms, which is not guaranteed with bf16 precision The gradient norm is computed in bf16 precision instead of being upcast to fp32 for the norm calculation

encyclopedia.title: DeepSpeed MoE + ZeRO-3 Hang. Missing Leaf Module Marking
encyclopedia.text: DeepSpeed MoE + ZeRO-3 Hang. Missing Leaf Module Marking Distributed Training Training hangs with NCCL timeout during the first forward pass through MoE layers nvidia-smi shows 0% GPU utilization on all ranks during the hang DeepSpeed logs show parameter gathering initiated but never completing for MoE parameters No error output. The job just hangs indefinitely deepspeed moe zero3 leaf-module hang mixture-of-experts parameter-gathering Training with DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 and MoE models hangs at the first forward pass NCCL timeout occurs during parameter gathering for MoE layers The hang is specific to MoE models. Non-MoE models with the same ZeRO-3 config work fine ZeRO-3 parameter gathering traverses the model hierarchy recursively, entering MoE router logic during the gather phase MoE routers have conditional parameter access (only active experts per token), which creates deadlocks when ZeRO-3 tries to gather all expert parameters simultaneously Without leaf module marking, ZeRO-3 doesn't know to treat MoE blocks as atomic units that should not be recursively decomposed The hang occurs because rank 0 is waiting for rank 1's expert parameters while rank 1 is stuck in the MoE router

The job just hangs indefinitely deepspeed moe zero3 leaf-module hang mixture-of-experts parameter-gathering ZeRO-3 parameter gathering traverses the model hierarchy recursively, entering MoE router logic during the gather phase MoE routers have conditional parameter access (only active experts per token), which creates deadlocks when ZeRO-3 tries to gather all expert parameters simultaneously Without leaf module marking, ZeRO-3 doesn't know to treat MoE blocks as atomic units that should not be recursively decomposed The hang occurs because rank 0 is waiting for rank 1's expert parameters while rank 1 is stuck in the MoE router

encyclopedia.title: DeepSpeed NaN from overlap_comm + contiguous_gradients
encyclopedia.text: DeepSpeed NaN from overlap_comm + contiguous_gradients Training Stability grad_norm is nan reported by DeepSpeed Training loss becomes NaN after a variable number of steps The NaN disappears when setting overlap_comm: false or contiguous_gradients: false DeepSpeed logs show NaN in gradient norm calculation deepspeed nan overlap-comm contiguous-gradients race-condition zero3 gradient Training produces NaN gradient norms when both overlap_comm and contiguous_gradients are True in DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 Disabling either flag individually resolves the NaN The NaN appears non-deterministically, making it hard to reproduce When overlap_comm is True, DeepSpeed starts communication (all-reduce) for one gradient bucket while the next bucket is being computed When contiguous_gradients is True, DeepSpeed copies gradients into a contiguous buffer for efficient communication The race: the communication overlap reads from the contiguous buffer while it's being rewritten by the next bucket's gradient copy, producing corrupted (NaN) values This is a buffer reuse race condition in DeepSpeed's gradient communication pipeline
encyclopedia.anchorText: DeepSpeed NaN from overlap_comm + contiguous_gradients grad_norm is nan reported by DeepSpeed Training loss becomes NaN after a variable number of steps The NaN disappears when setting overlap_comm: false or contiguous_gradients: false DeepSpeed logs show NaN in gradient norm calculation deepspeed nan overlap-comm contiguous-gradients race-condition zero3 gradient When overlap_comm is True, DeepSpeed starts communication (all-reduce) for one gradient bucket while the next bucket is being computed When contiguous_gradients is True, DeepSpeed copies gradients into a contiguous buffer for efficient communication The race: the communication overlap reads from the contiguous buffer while it's being rewritten by the next bucket's gradient copy, producing corrupted (NaN) values This is a buffer reuse race condition in DeepSpeed's gradient communication pipeline

encyclopedia.title: DeepSpeed FusedAdam Illegal Memory Access on H100
encyclopedia.text: DeepSpeed FusedAdam Illegal Memory Access on H100 Memory CUDA error: illegal memory access in FusedAdam kernel Training crashes during the optimizer step (not forward or backward) nvidia-smi shows the GPU in a bad state after the crash The error is deterministic: it happens at the same step every time deepspeed fusedadam h100 sm90 illegal-memory optimizer cuda Training on H100 with DeepSpeed FusedAdam crashes with 'CUDA error: illegal memory access' The same training works on A100 with FusedAdam Switching to the standard PyTorch AdamW optimizer resolves the crash FusedAdam's CUDA kernels were compiled for SM80 (A100) and are not compatible with SM90 (H100) architecture H100's SM90 architecture has different shared memory layout and warp scheduling that causes out-of-bounds access in FusedAdam kernels The illegal memory access occurs in the Adam update kernel when updating optimizer states (momentum, variance) for large parameter tensors DeepSpeed's FusedAdam has not been updated to support SM90 architecture natively

encyclopedia.title: DeepSpeed DecoupledCheckpointEngine Infinite Hang
encyclopedia.text: DeepSpeed DecoupledCheckpointEngine Infinite Hang Data Integrity Training stops making progress at a checkpoint save step nvidia-smi shows 0% GPU utilization on all ranks DeepSpeed logs show 'Saving checkpoint...' but no completion message ps aux shows the checkpoint writer thread stuck in D (uninterruptible sleep) state No timeout or error is triggered. encyclopedia.text: DeepSpeed FastFileWriter File Descriptor Leak, Phantom ENOSPC Data Integrity OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device when saving checkpoints df -h shows ample free space on the checkpoint storage lsof -p <pid> | wc -l shows file descriptor count near the ulimit -n limit The error occurs after a specific number of checkpoint saves (consistent across runs) deepspeed fd-leak enospc file-descriptor checkpoint fastfilewriter Training fails with 'No space left on device' but df shows plenty of free space The error occurs after many checkpoint saves, not at the beginning lsof shows thousands of open file descriptors for checkpoint files that should have been closed FastFileWriter opens checkpoint files for writing but doesn't close them after the write completes Each checkpoint save opens new file descriptors without closing the previous ones After enough saves, the per-process file descriptor limit (ulimit -n, typically 1024 or 65536) is exceeded The OS returns ENOSPC because the filesystem can't allocate new inodes or directory entries when fd limits are hit

encyclopedia.title: DeepSpeed Universal Checkpoint Lexicographic Sort Corruption
encyclopedia.text: DeepSpeed Universal Checkpoint Lexicographic Sort Corruption Data Integrity Training loss diverges after resuming from a universal checkpoint with 10+ ranks Model accuracy drops significantly after checkpoint resume Parameter checksums differ across ranks after loading the same universal checkpoint The issue only appears with 10+ ranks (rank_10 sorts before rank_2 lexicographically) deepspeed checkpoint sort corruption universal-checkpoint lexicographic silent Model weights are silently corrupted after loading a universal checkpoint Training produces wrong results or diverges after resuming from a universal checkpoint The corruption is invisible. No error is raised during checkpoint loading DeepSpeed sorts rank directories using lexicographic order: rank_0, rank_1, rank_10, rank_11..., rank_2, rank_3... Numeric order should be: rank_0, rank_1, rank_2, rank_3..., rank_10, rank_11... When rank_10 is loaded in rank_2's position, all parameters from rank_10 onwards are loaded into the wrong rank This silently corrupts model weights because each rank's optimizer states (momentum, variance) are mismatched with its parameters

encyclopedia.title: DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 Small Parameter Partition Bug
encyclopedia.text: DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 Small Parameter Partition Bug Distributed Training UnboundLocalError: local variable 'partition_dim' referenced before assignment in partition_parameters.py Error occurs in deepspeed/runtime/zero/partition_parameters.py around line 862 Crash happens during DeepSpeed engine initialization, before training starts Reducing the number of GPUs or switching to ZeRO-2 avoids the crash deepspeed zero3 partition small-parameter unboundlocalerror partition-parameters Training crashes with UnboundLocalError in DeepSpeed's partition_parameters.py The error occurs during ZeRO-3 initialization for models with very small parameters (e.g., bias vectors, layer norm parameters) The same model works with fewer GPUs but crashes when scaled to more GPUs ZeRO-3 partitions each parameter's elements equally across GPUs. When a parameter has fewer elements than the number of GPUs, the partition calculation produces zero or negative slice sizes The partition_dim variable is never assigned when the parameter is too small to partition, causing the UnboundLocalError Small parameters (e.g., a bias vector with 8 elements on 16 GPUs) cannot be meaningfully partitioned The bug is in DeepSpeed's partition_parameters.py which doesn't handle the edge case of parameters smaller than world_size

encyclopedia.title: Straggler / Slow-Rank Detection
encyclopedia.text: Straggler / Slow-Rank Detection Reliability One rank's step time is consistently 1.5-10x the median GPU utilization on most ranks oscillates between 100% and 0% (waiting) MFU / tokens-per-second degrades over hours without a config change No NCCL timeout fires because the slow rank still responds, just late straggler slow-rank reliability distributed throughput gray-failure stall Throughput drops with no error in the logs All ranks block at all-reduce waiting on one slow rank Step time is dominated by the slowest rank A degraded GPU (thermal throttle, ECC row-remap, reduced clocks) on one rank Slower network path (oversubscribed link, bad cable, PFC pause storms) to one node CPU/dataloader contention starving one rank's input pipeline NUMA / PCIe misconfiguration on a single host
encyclopedia.anchorText:
Straggler / Slow-Rank Detection One rank's step time is consistently 1.5-10x the median GPU utilization on most ranks oscillates between 100% and 0% (waiting) MFU / tokens-per-second degrades over hours without a config change No NCCL timeout fires because the slow rank still responds, just late straggler slow-rank reliability distributed throughput gray-failure stall A degraded GPU (thermal throttle, ECC row-remap, reduced clocks) on one rank Slower network path (oversubscribed link, bad cable, PFC pause storms) to one node CPU/dataloader contention starving one rank's input pipeline NUMA / PCIe misconfiguration on a single host # Lightweight per-rank straggler check. Log ranks slower than 1.5x median
import torch, torch.distributed as dist

step_t = torch.tensor([elapsed], device='cuda')
gathered = [torch.zeros_like(step_t) for _ in range(dist.get_world_size())]
dist.all_gather(gathered, step_t)
times = torch.stack(gathered).flatten()
median = times.median()
slow = (times > 1.5 * median).nonzero().flatten().tolist()
if dist.get_rank() == 0 and slow:
    print(f'[straggler] ranks {slow} slower than 1.5x median ({median.item():.3f}s)')

encyclopedia.title: DeepSpeed ZeRO GPU Memory Not Freed After Training (hooks leak)
encyclopedia.text: DeepSpeed ZeRO GPU Memory Not Freed After Training (hooks leak) Memory torch.cuda.memory_allocated stays high after del trainer Memory grows monotonically across folds ZeRO-2/3 + PEFT training loops deepspeed zero-2 memory-leak hooks gradient-accumulation memory GPU memory stays high after training finishes Each fold/sweep iteration leaks until CUDA OOM del trainer + empty_cache does not reclaim memory DeepSpeed left backward/gradient-accumulation hooks and internal references attached after the engine/optimizer were destroyed Those lingering references prevented garbage collection of the model and optimizer state, so CUDA memory was never freed

encyclopedia.title: DeepSpeed Pipeline Parallel Hangs with Variable Input Shapes
encyclopedia.text: DeepSpeed Pipeline Parallel Hangs with Variable Input Shapes Distributed Training PP engine stops progressing mid-epoch with no error Ranks wait at pipeline send/recv Hang correlates with variable-length microbatches deepspeed pipeline-parallel dynamic-shapes p2p hang distributed Pipeline-parallel training stalls partway through Ranks block at p2p send/recv Variable sequence lengths trigger the hang The pipeline engine negotiates send/recv buffer sizes from the first microbatch's shapes and reuses them A subsequent microbatch with a different shape mismatches the pre-sized p2p buffers, so paired ranks deadlock

encyclopedia.title: DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 High GPU Memory / OOM Loading a Large Model Without zero.Init
encyclopedia.text: DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 High GPU Memory / OOM Loading a Large Model Without zero.Init Memory CUDA OOM during AutoModel.from_pretrained under ZeRO-3 Full dense model materialized on every GPU before partitioning 11B+ model won't load on hardware that should fit the partitioned model deepspeed zero-3 zero-init hf-deepspeed-config oom memory ZeRO-3 uses much more per-GPU memory than the partitioned size implies OOM while loading the model with from_pretrained Memory does not drop after ZeRO-3 'partitions' the model The model was instantiated outside deepspeed.zero.Init(), so each rank loaded the complete dense parameters into GPU memory before ZeRO-3 could shard them Without zero.Init the partitioning happens too late to avoid the full-model memory spike

encyclopedia.title: NCCL Collective Operation Timeout
encyclopedia.text: NCCL Collective Operation Timeout Distributed Communication NCCL timeout or Watchdog caught collective operation timeout in logs NCCL WARN messages with specific rank and collective name Multiple ranks report timeout simultaneously (cascade pattern) Job exits with ncclInternalError or ncclSystemError nccl timeout distributed watchdog collective symptom downstream One or more NCCL collectives (all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter) fail to complete Watchdog timer fires after the configured timeout period Training job aborts with NCCL timeout errors affecting multiple ranks The timeout is a symptom, not a root cause. The initiating fault is elsewhere: GPU crash (OOM, Xid), host OOM killer, network link degradation, or storage stall. NCCL watchdog timeout default (30s) may be too short for very large all-reduces across many nodes Network congestion or PFC/ECN misconfiguration on RoCE fabric causes RDMA retransmission delays exceeding timeout
